jobs.description:
We are looking for developers who have a software project they personally own, such as a side project, personal tool, or open-source library.

In this project, you will use an AI coding assistant to work on your existing software project. This may involve building new features, fixing bugs, refactoring code, or writing documentation. As you work, you will be presented with two versions of the AI assistant's response and asked to select the one that works better, along with a short explanation of your choice.

What You'll Do:

  • Bring and work on a software project that you personally own and maintain in a Git repository.
  • Use an AI coding assistant to build features, fix bugs, refactor code, and improve documentation.
  • Review and compare two versions of AI-generated coding responses.
  • Evaluate which response is more useful, accurate, and effective for your project.
  • Provide clear, honest feedback explaining why you selected one response over the other.
  • Work comfortably with terminal commands and Git during project sessions.
  • Follow project guidelines and ensure that no passwords, API keys, or other people's personal information are included in your sessions.

Requirements:

  • Experienced software developer with a personal software project that you own and maintain in a Git repository.
  • Comfortable working with terminal commands and Git.
  • Has a computer running macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2.
  • Able to review and evaluate AI-generated code and coding suggestions.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to explain decisions clearly and briefly.
  • Able to provide independent and honest feedback without using AI assistance to write evaluation responses.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience maintaining open-source software projects.
  • Experience building personal tools, applications, libraries, or other software projects.
  • Familiarity with AI coding assistants and developer productivity tools.
  • Experience with software debugging, feature development, code refactoring, and documentation.
  • Fully remote freelance opportunity.
  • Worldwide applicants are welcome, subject to project eligibility.
  • Rate: Up to $100 per hour.
  • Expected Workload: Approximately 10–39 hours per week, depending on project needs.
  • Work volume may fluctuate throughout the contract.
  • Payments will be released weekly as a lump sum for work completed during the previous week.
  • AI usage during the project will be covered, so candidates will not need to pay for an AI subscription or API usage.

Project Eligibility and Ownership Requirements:

  • Candidates must bring a software project they personally and solely own.
  • Open-source projects must have an approved license. Projects with multiple maintainers may require additional confirmation.
  • Projects owned by an employer, client, university, or startup are not eligible.
  • Projects covered by an NDA are not eligible.
  • Projects involving AI model training or evaluation, machine learning infrastructure, security exploit tooling, or the processing of other people's personal data are not eligible.
  • The client's team must review and approve the project before work begins.
  • Selected candidates must sign contributor terms before starting.

Important Privacy and Participation Notes:

  • Transcripts from project sessions will be used to improve AI models. Once submitted, these transcripts cannot be withdrawn.
  • Only project session transcripts will be shared, not the rest of the candidate's software project.
  • Ratings and written feedback provided by candidates will become part of the project's deliverables.
  • Candidates must not include passwords, API keys, or other people's personal information in their sessions.
  • All ratings and written evaluations must be completed independently, without AI assistance.

Important: An active Upwork contract is required before candidates can receive onboarding instructions, access to the evaluation platform, or payment for the project. Candidates should accept the contract offer once received.

Due to the high volume of applicants being contacted, the team may not be able to respond to every individual message. Thank you for your understanding.

jobs.title: Associate Business Development Alliances Manager
jobs.excerpt: At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise.
jobs.description:
At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. With this insight, organizations can investigate smarter, stop threats faster, and keep operations running.

Our mission is fueled by a profound social and moral responsibility to be the best at what we do, ensuring a secure world where everyone can thrive. If this sounds like a place you’d like to spend the next chapter of your career, we’d love to hear from you.

Position Summary

We are looking for an Associate Business Development Alliances Manager to run the day-to-day operations behind ExtraHop’s co-sell, marketplace, referral, and partner activation programs with our strategic cloud and technology partners. The initial focus is on expanding co-sell and marketplace activity in North America, with AWS and Google Cloud through co-sell and marketplace motions, and with CrowdStrikeand other strategic tech partners through joint selling and integration-led co-sell.

This role works closely with ExtraHop sales teams, Deal Ops, channel partners, technology partners, and internal cross-functional teams to keep shared opportunities moving, activate partners and sellers, and turn partner relationships into measurable pipeline and revenue. You will manage the operational mechanics of co-sell, referral, and marketplace programs, including opportunity registration and follow-up, handoffs to Deal Ops, partner activation, and performance reporting, so that field teams and partner sellers can sell together with minimal friction.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience running co-sell, marketplace, or referral programs and is comfortable working in Salesforce and partner tooling. Familiarity with the cybersecurity landscape is valuable, and you will build deep knowledge of ExtraHop’s Network Detection and Response platform and its role within the broader security ecosystem. This is a highly collaborative role that requires building working relationships with partner field organizations while coordinating effectively across Sales, Deal Ops, Marketing, Product, and Alliances.

Key Responsibilities

As a member of the Alliances organization, you will work with technology and channel partners to develop and execute joint go-to-market strategies. Your day-to-day responsibilities could include any of the following:

Co-Sell

  • Execute co-sell programs with strategic cloud and technology partners (AWS, Google, CrowdStrike, others), supporting the strategy set by Alliances leadership.
  • Manage co-sell opportunity workflows in AWS Partner Central/ACE and the Google partner portal, including submission, acceptance, and follow-up, so shared opportunities keep moving.
  • Facilitate joint account mapping and opportunity progression between ExtraHop account teams and partner field counterparts.
  • Maintain working relationships with partner field, channel, solutions engineering, and alliance teams to support joint customer meetings and co-sell execution.

Marketplace

  • Identify and track marketplace-eligible opportunities, and work with account teams and partner reps to move them toward marketplace transactions.
  • Serve as the Alliances point of contact for Deal Ops, handing off deal details and following up so marketplace deals close smoothly. Deal Ops creates and enters the Marketplace offers.
  • Educate sellers and partners on the marketplace motion, including cloud commitment drawdown and how to position marketplace purchasing with customers.

Referrals and Programs

  • Operationalize referral programs
  • Build and document repeatable playbooks and processes for co-sell, referral, and marketplace motions that increase partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline.

Partner Activation and Enablement

  • Run partner activation, including onboarding checklists, first-deal playbooks, and time-to-first-opportunity tracking.
  • Coordinate partner and seller enablement (sales presentations, use cases, competitive positioning, and joint solution messaging) with Marketing and Partner Solutions Architecture.
  • Support joint webinars, events, executive briefings, and customer workshops.

Reporting and Cross-Functional Work

  • Track and report partnership performance, including joint opportunities, pipeline, sourced and influenced revenue, marketplace-transacted bookings, and customer activity. Maintain pipeline hygiene and dashboards, and report regularly to leadership.
  • Prepare data and materials for partner business reviews led by Alliances leadership.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Sales Ops/RevOps, Deal Ops, Marketing, and Partner Solutions Architecture to remove friction from partner-led deals.
  • Build working knowledge of ExtraHop’s Network Detection and Response platform and the partner platforms it complements.
  • Identify and fix process gaps to make our partner programs more scalable and efficient.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in alliances, partner operations, channel, or business development, including hands-on work with a cloud marketplace (AWS or Google), co-sell, or referral program..
  • Proven experience developing relationships with partner field organizations and translating those relationships into measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience working with cybersecurity technology vendors, channel partners, resellers, or systems integrators.
  • Understanding of enterprise cybersecurity technologies and the security operations market.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute joint go-to-market and co-selling strategies.
  • Strong business acumen and ability to understand pipeline, revenue, and sales performance metrics.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, relationship-building, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with Sales, Deal Ops, Marketing, Product, Engineering, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple strategic initiatives simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with how AWS and Google Cloud marketplace transactions work, including private offers, CPPOs, and commitment drawdown.
  • Experience working with leading cybersecurity technology platforms, and familiarity with Endpoint, SIEM, NDR, XDR, SOAR, cloud security, and security operations technologies.
  • Existing relationships with cybersecurity channel partners, resellers, and systems integrators.
  • Experience developing referral, co-sell, marketplace, or other partner-led commercial programs.
  • Experience with Cloud 3PI (e.g., Tackle.io), account-mapping (e.g., Crossbeam), or other ecosystem-led growth and partner management tools.
  • Advanced proficiency with spreadsheets, pivot tables, and business reporting.

Compensation & Benefits: The salary range for this role is $75,000 – $85,000 per year, plus eligibility for an annual performance-based discretionary bonus and stock option grants. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage (effective Day 1), a 401(k) with employer match, flexible PTO, parental leave, and more.

ABOUT EXTRAHOP

ExtraHop is reinventing Network Detection and Response (NDR) to offer enterprises unparalleled visibility, context, and control against emerging threats. The platform integrates NDR with Network Performance Management (NPM), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and forensics, providing a single, comprehensive solution. By decrypting and analyzing complete packet-level data at wire speed and leveraging cloud-scale machine learning, ExtraHop empowers Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to detect, investigate, and remediate modern cyber risks in real time across their entire hybrid infrastructure, including data center, cloud, and SASE environments.

This comprehensive approach and market innovation have earned ExtraHop unique recognition as the only NDR vendor acknowledged as a leader by all major analyst firms, including the 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant for Network Detection and Response™, the 2025 Forrester® Wave for Network Analysis and Visibility, the 2024 IDC® Marketscape for NDR, and the 2025 Gigamon® Radar Report for Network Detection and Response. Since 2007, ExtraHop has consistently helped organizations worldwide extract in-depth network telemetry and contextual insights, affirming its commitment to protecting and empowering the connected enterprise.

OUR VALUES

Our culture is rooted in our five Values. These set the expectations for how we work individually and collectively as a team.

Lead with Purpose: We are driven to deliver results that create a positive impact for our customers, partners, and colleagues.

Act with Integrity: We operate with transparency, authenticity, and always in the best interest of the company.

Find a Way: We are resourceful, tackle hard problems with a sense of urgency and ownership, and do what it takes to get the job done.

Innovate: We listen to customers, partners, and the market, and respectfully push boundaries and challenge the status quo.

Share Success: We run together, we win together. We value diverse perspectives, hold space for all voices, and achieve the best results as a team.

BENEFITS

Employees' wellbeing is top of mind for the ExtraHop team. Employees and their families will have the option to participate in the following benefits:

  • Health, Dental, and Vision Benefits
  • Flexible PTO, Sick Time Prorated Based on Date of Hire, and All Federal Holidays (US Only) + 3 Days of Paid Volunteer Time
  • Non-Commissioned Positions may be eligible to participate in the Annual Discretionary Bonus Plan
  • FSA and Dependent Care Accounts + EAP, where applicable
  • Educational Reimbursement
  • 401k with Employer Match or Pension where applicable
  • Pet Insurance (US Only)
  • Parental Leave (US Only)
  • Hybrid and Remote Work Model

Our people are our most important competitive advantage, leading the charge against cyber criminals. Join the fight today!

To learn more, visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn.

Principales responsabilités

  • Prendre en charge le développement complet de fonctionnalités back-end, de l’analyse des besoins et de l’estimation jusqu’à la conception, au développement, aux tests, à la documentation et à la mise en production, tout en respectant les échéanciers et le cycle de développement logiciel réglementé (SDLC) d’Intelerad.

  • Utiliser quotidiennement des outils de programmation assistée par agents intelligents, en faisant preuve de jugement quant aux tâches à déléguer à l’IA, à celles à réaliser directement et à la façon de valider les résultats obtenus.

  • Appliquer les mêmes exigences de révision, de tests, de traçabilité et de gestion des changements au code produit avec l’aide de l’IA qu’au code écrit manuellement, afin d’assurer la conformité aux exigences réglementaires.
  • Collaborer avec les équipes de développement produit et les autres parties prenantes sur les aspects fonctionnels, l’expérience utilisateur et l’architecture technique.

Qualifications et expérience

  • Minimum de 6 ans d’expérience professionnelle en développement et maintenance de logiciels commerciaux.
  • Excellente maîtrise de Java, incluant le développement d’architectures client-serveur complexes, distribuées et multithreads, ainsi qu’une solide compréhension des principes de conception orientée objet.
  • Expérience professionnelle avec Linux/UNIX, PostgreSQL (conception de schémas, optimisation de requêtes et migrations), les API REST et les intégrations entre services.
  • Expérience avec les tests unitaires et d’intégration automatisés, Git et les outils CI/CD.
  • Expérience concrète de livraison de code en production à l’aide d’outils de programmation assistée par agents intelligents, avec la capacité d’expliquer quelles tâches sont confiées à l’IA, lesquelles sont réalisées manuellement et comment les résultats sont validés.

  • Capacité démontrée à livrer des résultats de façon autonome dans un environnement Agile/Scrum, avec d’excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite et verbale et la capacité d’influencer les autres sans autorité hiérarchique directe.
  • Baccalauréat en informatique, en génie logiciel ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.

Qualifications privilégiées et exigences particulières

  • Expérience de l’intégration d’outils d’IA agentique dans un cycle de développement logiciel formel, auditable et réglementé.

  • Connaissances de C++, JNI, Perl ou des scripts Shell.

But that’s just the beginning:

Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.

Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET, our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.

Tether Education: Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.

Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.

Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.

If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.

Are you ready to be part of the future?

About the job

We are seeking a highly driven Head of AI Expansion to lead the global adoption of Tether’s AI ecosystem, with a focus on QVAC and decentralized, privacy-preserving AI infrastructure.

The role will engage leading enterprises, institutions, and governments globally, helping them deploy AI solutions built around local computing, data sovereignty, privacy, and independence from centralized cloud infrastructure.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining exceptional commercial and relationship-building capabilities with deep AI knowledge. You will identify and prioritize opportunities, structure complex projects, close strategic partnerships, monitor success of partnerships and build the team required to scale Tether AI globally.

The ideal candidate can comfortably move between technical discussions with AI and engineering teams and strategic conversations with CEOs, CTOs, CIOs, and government leaders and should be used to work in multiple geographies/ cultures.

International travel is required.

Responsibilities

Business Development & Partnerships

  • Drive global adoption of QVAC and Tether AI across enterprises, institutions, and governments.

Strategic Representation

jobs.description:
Field Sales Representative

Location: Croydon, covering Croydon or surrounding areas (fully field-based)

£50,000–£90,000 OTE (£30,000–£54,000 base salary + uncapped commission, based on experience) + £800 monthly car allowance and a comprehensive benefits package

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re ambitious, enjoy meeting new people and want to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We’re looking for ambitious, driven people to join our growing Field Sales team and help bring Teya to more local businesses across the UK.

As a Field Sales Representative, you’ll take ownership of your own territory, getting out into your local community, meeting business owners face-to-face and showing them how Teya can help their businesses thrive.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the field, building relationships and winning new business. You’ll have the freedom to manage your territory, the support of a team that wants you to succeed, and the opportunity to build a rewarding career in sales.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own your territory: Proactively identify and engage local businesses through face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals and other opportunities to generate new business.

  • Build meaningful relationships: Get to know business owners, understand their challenges and identify how Teya’s products and services can make their lives easier.

  • Win new Members: Use a consultative, value-led approach to demonstrate Teya’s solutions, build trust and turn conversations into long-term customer relationships.

  • Deliver results: Take ownership of your sales performance, maintain a healthy pipeline and consistently work towards your commercial targets.

  • See things through: Take responsibility for your Members’ experience from the first conversation through to onboarding, ensuring they’re set up successfully and ready to start using Teya.

  • Keep learning: Develop strong knowledge of our products, competitors and sales methodology through structured training, coaching and feedback.

  • Represent Teya: Be a trusted face of Teya in your local community, delivering the genuine care and hospitality that we want every Member to experience.

  • Help us improve: Share insights from the field to help us continuously improve our products, sales approach and Member experience.

Your Story

We believe great salespeople come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might already be an experienced field sales professional with a strong track record of winning new business. Or you might be earlier in your career, with the ambition, drive and potential to become an exceptional salesperson.

What matters most to us is your mindset, your ability to connect with people and your willingness to learn and improve.

We’re looking for people who bring:

  • Ambition and drive: You’re motivated to succeed, enjoy working towards challenging goals and take pride in delivering great results.

  • A competitive mindset: You enjoy winning, hold yourself to high standards and are always looking for ways to improve.

  • Resilience and determination: You’re comfortable with rejection, stay positive when things get tough and don’t give up easily.

  • Strong people skills: You enjoy meeting new people, build rapport naturally and can have meaningful conversations with business owners from all walks of life.

  • Curiosity and commercial awareness: You ask good questions, listen carefully and want to understand what makes a business successful.

  • Coachability: You’re open to feedback, willing to challenge yourself and committed to developing your skills.

  • Ownership and self-discipline: You’re organised, proactive and comfortable managing your own time and priorities in a field-based role.

  • A genuine care for others: You understand that great sales isn’t just about closing a deal. It’s about doing what’s right for the customer and building trust that lasts.

Experience in field sales, business development, payments or financial services is an advantage, but not essential for every level. We care just as much about your potential as your experience.

You’ll also need:

  • Fluency in English.

  • A full UK driving licence and access to a car.

  • The right to work in the UK.

  • Willingness to work in a fully field-based role, travelling regularly throughout your territory.

The Perks

We believe great performance should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

  • £30,000–£54,000 base salary, depending on your experience and demonstrated capability.

  • Uncapped commission.

  • £800 per month car allowance (£9,600 annually), on top of your salary and commission.

  • 25 days of paid annual leave, plus UK bank holidays.

  • Bupa private healthcare and life insurance.

  • Employer pension contributions through our company pension scheme.

  • Free gym membership through Wellhub, alongside one-to-one therapy sessions, meditation and digital fitness and nutrition apps.

  • Structured onboarding, practical sales training, ongoing coaching and opportunities to grow your career at Teya.

What Happens Next?

Our recruitment process is designed to help us get to know you, understand your strengths and give you a genuine opportunity to show us what you can do.

Stage 1 - Introductory conversation (30 minutes)
A conversation with our Talent team to learn more about you, your motivation and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2 - Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes)
An opportunity to explore your experience, how you approach challenges and what makes you successful.

Stage 3 - Final Assessment (60 minutes)
You’ll meet members of our Sales leadership team, present a short territory plan and take part in a practical sales role-play. We’ll share everything you need to prepare in advance.

We know interviews are a two-way process, and we’ll make sure you have plenty of opportunities to ask questions and get to know us along the way.

Teya is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, including those without a traditional sales or commercial track record.

Teya is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or background can thrive and do their best work. We believe that a diverse team leads to better ideas, stronger outcomes, and a more supportive workplace for all.

If you require any reasonable adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process whether for interviews, assessments, or other parts of the application—we encourage you to let us know. We are committed to ensuring that every candidate has a fair and accessible experience with us.

Job Title: Global Category Lead, Full-Service CRO - Associate Director, Global Procurement

Job Location: Washington D.C., District of Columbia, United States

Job Seniority Level:

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Global Category Lead, Full-Service CRO - Associate Director, Global Procurement R&D


What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. We are seeking an individual who thrives in ambiguity, capable of driving category management initiatives with strategic vision and precision.

You will serve as the Global Category Manager and lead the global category strategy for Full-Service CRO. This includes developing multi-year category strategies that address business needs while achieving best practice outcomes, building enterprise-wide business partnerships, and activating Procurement resources to drive strategic sourcing results to reduce costs and enable top-line performance.

Your responsibilities will include analyzing internal demand (using Business Partner Management processes), external market data, spend & specifications to produce category plans aligned with Business objectives and cost reduction / sourcing initiates. As a Category Manager, you will play a pivotal role in managing the innovation agenda of Procurement. This role will drive supplier performance, manage risk, and deliver sustained value across a complex global professional services landscape.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead category management for Full-Service CRO, supporting all phases of fully outsourced clinical trials, including ClinPharm, Ph I-IV, Observational Research, and inherited studies resulting from M&A activity.
  • Partner with R&D, Clinical, Regulatory, and Compliance teams to ensure alignment with FDA, EMA, HIPAA, and GCP standards.
  • Negotiate contracts, amendments, and competitive commercial terms, rates, and discounts with vendors supporting fully outsourced clinical trials, balancing innovation with compliance & risk, while positioning Amgen and stakeholders for success.
  • Partner with Program Leads, Study Teams, and R&D Supplier Governance to enable supplier governance frameworks, drive high-quality delivery and performance, and ensure effective & timely issue resolution.
  • Monitor market trends & intelligence, including the evolving digital health regulations, and integrate compliance, quality, and risk mitigation into sourcing strategies.
  • Provide strategic oversight as the lead for the Full-Service CRO category and sourcing, ensuring alignment between category strategies and Amgen’s evolving business needs. Act as a trusted advisor to ensure that procurement initiatives are aligned with broader organizational objectives.
  • Guide and facilitate collaboration across cross-functional teams and regional stakeholders, ensuring that procurement strategies meet the diverse needs of the organization and are implemented effectively.
  • Ensure that all procurement activities in support of Full-Service CRO are managed in compliance with regulatory, contractual, and operational risk requirements. Partner with Legal, Compliance, Data Privacy, and Cybersecurity teams to maintain oversight of risk mitigation strategies and ensure alignment with best practices.
  • Collaborate with Global Procurement colleagues and relevant stakeholders to oversee the strategic approach to complex negotiations for CRO MSAs, Amendments, including support as necessary for Study-Level Agreements & Purchase Orders, providing guidance and ensuring appropriate processes and frameworks are in place for RFPs, supplier evaluations, and contract development.
  • Maturity to activate procurement resources and facilitate delegation of sourcing activities to drive category priorities while managing expectations with stakeholders and mitigating risk on behalf of Amgen.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The strategic procurement leader we seek is a collaborative and influential business partner with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications:

Doctorate degree and 3 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Master’s degree and 5 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 7 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Associate’s degree and 12 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 14 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with procurement platforms such as Ariba, as well as ERP systems and advanced analytics tools to support decision-making and process automation.
  • Excellent problem solving and organizational skills
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to analyze large datasets, identify trends, and derive actionable insights
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing complex global projects in a matrixed environment.
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (21 CFR Part 11, GxP, HIPAA, GDPR).
  • Extensive experience with and knowledge of the global vendor landscape in support of all phases of clinical trials, specifically Contract Research Organizations (CRO) and Site Management Organizations (SMO), Academic Medical Centers (AMC), and CRO-adjacent vendors.
  • Global Category Mgmt. with proven record of executive business partnering leading change and enterprise activation of sourcing initiatives driven from expert knowledge of marketplace capabilities
  • Deep understanding of category management principles, supplier relationship management, and contract lifecycle management.
  • Strong financial, legal, and contractual fluency to navigate sales services agreements and deliver business-aligned outcomes.
  • A track record of driving innovation in category strategy development, supplier engagement models, and internal stakeholder partnerships.
  • Exceptional ability to communicate complex category strategies, influence senior stakeholders, and manage change across functions and regions.
  • Capable of leveraging spend analytics and benchmarking to inform category strategies and uncover new value opportunities.
  • Understanding of regulatory landscapes with the ability to navigate and manage compliance requirements.
  • Ability to partner closely with Legal, Compliance, Cybersecurity, and Regulatory Affairs.
  • Strong contractual and regulatory navigation skills for healthcare technology agreements.

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

  • Stock-based long-term incentives

Regional Clinical Affairs Manager, Electrophysiology

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

The Opportunity


In Abbott’s Electrophysiology (EP) business, we’re advancing the treatment of heart disease through breakthrough medical technologies in atrial fibrillation, allowing people to restore their health and get on with their lives.

The EP Regional Clinical Affairs Manager is a field-based, strategic role in the clinical research space. Key responsibilities include clinical and strategic support to the Clinical Affairs Organization, with a specific focus on BU technologies and therapy areas. This role directly impacts key clinical trial and new technology approval timelines through study acceleration and enrollment driving efforts. Specific priorities include relationship development with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), leading new clinical site launches, identifying new clinical research partners, and developing strategic plans for research partnerships within territory.


What you’ll work on

  • Clinical Site Management & Enrollment: act as the primary point of contact for clinical trial sites, proactively driving patient enrollment and ensuring study milestones are met.
  • Prioritize engagements with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to foster strong clinical research relationships. Lead efforts to increase KOL engagements across study committees, publication efforts, and congress presentations.
  • Manage multi-cultural, multi-country relationships with customers and cross-functional internal teams.
  • Illustrate exemplary collaboration with commercial leadership, and across other BUs to foster a cohesive physician clinical experience across all of Abbott.
  • Manage new site launches, ensuring smooth and efficient implementation of clinical research studies. Lead debriefs, both internally and with physician study investigators, to action early procedure experiences into improved clinical study execution.
  • Identify and develop new clinical research sites to expand the territory and support future clinical trial execution and early feasibility studies.
  • Manage day-to-day priorities, scheduling, forecasting, and strategic planning for the assigned territory.
  • Serve as lead for clinical projects collaborating as an integral member of core teams.
  • Serve as key member of cross-functional groups leading knowledge transference between clinical and commercial realms supporting BU goals (ex. new product launches)
  • Maintain competency in technical support and troubleshooting for clinical research study procedures involving Abbott BU technologies.
  • Participate in high-profile presentations, advisory boards, and special projects that enhance FCA staff productivity and contribute to Abbott’s corporate goals.
  • Mentor and support FCS staff, with opportunity for direct-report management.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in engineering, biological sciences, or a related field, OR equivalent or related experience in cardiology or clinical research.
  • 9 or more years of progressively more responsible relevant clinical work experience in the cardiovascular field.
  • Recognized nationally as a leader/expert in the field.
  • Ability to travel up to 50%. May include international travel opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in engaging with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and managing clinical research sites.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to manage challenging conversations with multi-country, multi-cultural physicians and cross-functional partners.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities within a territory.
  • Leadership potential and experience in mentoring or people-management.

jobs.title: Senior CRM Manager - Conversion & Lifecycle
jobs.excerpt: Join our expanding Product Growth team!  We’re actively recruiting a Senior CRM Manager as we continue to scale at M-KOPA.
jobs.description:
Join our expanding Product Growth team! We’re actively recruiting a Senior CRM Manager as we continue to scale at M-KOPA. Most senior growth hires get one channel and one pod for years. This role is built differently: you’ll own two of our core growth pods in your first year, then land where you’ve had the most impact. It’s a fast track to pod leadership, not a support seat.

The Impact 💚

You’ll drive the conversion growth that turns customers into long-term, high-value ones, creating financial inclusion for Africa’s traditionally excluded. We’ve already helped over 10 million customers access over $2 billion in credit 🌍

The Opportunity

🏗️ Real ownership from day one. You'll be the one accountable for delivery in Repeat Phones, not shadowing or supporting someone else's plan.

🎒 Two growth motions, one year. You'll take on Digital Lending mid-way through, working directly with one of our strongest performers to understand cash loans end to end, then carry that pod solo for a defined stretch. Few people get this breadth this early.

🧭 A defined path, not indefinite floating. You'll build real expertise in our two conversion pods first, then move into Lifecycle in the second half of next year, reporting to the Lifecycle CRM Lead once you're there. The destination is set. What you bring to it is up to you. 🌍 Work inside a proven CLV engine. M-KOPA has helped more than 10 million customers access over $2 billion in credit. You'll be executing inside systems that already work, not guessing at what might.

What You'll Do

Phase 1: Repeat Phones. Take ownership of reactivation and upgrade campaigns in CleverTap, working closely with the Growth Lead there to understand what's driving the pod's numbers and where the next opportunity is. You'll be trusted to make real calls here, not just execute a checklist.

Phase 2: Cross into Digital Lending. Work directly with the Digital Lending lead, one of our top performers, to understand cash loan growth end to end before taking it on yourself.

Phase 3: Own Digital Lending. Carry primary responsibility for Digital Lending for a defined period, with the Repeat Phones lead available if you need a second opinion.

Phase 4: Move into Lifecycle. In the second half of next year, join the Lifecycle pod full-time, reporting to the Lifecycle CRM Lead. You'll bring a year of hands-on conversion experience into a pod that's still being built, real currency for shaping what Lifecycle does next. Throughout all phases, you will:

  • Build and run multi-channel campaigns (SMS, WhatsApp, push, in-app) in CleverTap against pod goals

  • Track funnel performance and flag drop-off points to the pod lead you're supporting

  • Run structured experiments (creative, audience, incentive, or timing) with clear hypotheses

  • Turn what works into documented playbooks the next person can pick up

  • Keep data quality and campaign tracking clean enough that leadership can trust the numbers

Key Metrics You'll Influence

Repeat Phones: Reactivation rate, upgrade conversion %, unit economics per sale

Digital Lending: Approval → disbursement rate, digital loan volume, approval quality

Campaign ROI and payback period across both

Your Environment

💼 Tech Stack: CleverTap (primary), Looker Channels: WhatsApp, SMS, push, in-app messaging

Markets: Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, Ghana

What You Need

  • 5+ years in growth, performance, or lifecycle marketing, ideally in fintech, telco, or e-commerce, with real ownership over what a campaign or a pod achieved, not just involvement in it.

  • Judgment as much as skill. You can walk into a pod, understand what's working and why, and make calls on where to push, not just follow a brief.

  • Genuine appetite for pod leadership. This is a deliberate path toward owning a pod outright, and the breadth here is designed to get you there faster than a single-channel role would.

  • Hands-on fluency in CRM platforms like CleverTap, Braze, or similar, and comfortable reading a funnel or cohort without translation.

  • Energized, not unsettled, by ambiguity. You'll work across two pods and land in a third decision point by mid-year. If that sounds like an opportunity rather than a risk, you'll thrive here.

  • Strong enough presence to build trust quickly with senior leads across two different pods.

Location & Benefits

  • 🌍 Fully remote role within UTC -1 to UTC +3 time zones

  • 🤝 Work with diverse teams across UK, Europe, and Africa

  • 📚 Professional development programmes and coaching partnerships

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family-friendly policies and flexible working arrangements

  • 💚 Well-being support and career growth opportunities

Our Mission 🌍

We create financial inclusion for the traditionally excluded through a fair, flexible, customer-centric financing model. We strive to drive greater inclusion of women, youth, and low-income communities.

Our Impact 💚

Our technology has created measurable change:

  • Connected 📱: 2.5 million first-time smartphone users connected

  • Prosperous 💰: 70% of customers use M-KOPA products for income generation, with 35,000+ livelihoods created for agents

  • Green 🌱: 2.1 million tonnes of CO₂ avoided through clean energy products, with over 127,700 circular economy products provided

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at .

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

jobs.title: Talent and People Partner - Part Time
jobs.excerpt: Goodwall. io is a mission-driven TIME100, WEF Global Innovator award winning platform that connects youth to skilling, opportunity and support alongside leading public and private institutions.
jobs.description:
Goodwall.io is a mission-driven TIME100, WEF Global Innovator award winning platform that connects youth to skilling, opportunity and support alongside leading public and private institutions. Goodwall has over 4 million members. Goodwall works alongside industry leaders such as Microsoft, Nestle, UNICEF, Accenture and SAP to build pathways into skills and careers such as financial literacy, AI, green jobs and entrepreneurship for Gen Z.

Working alongside foundations and market leading corporates means youth never pay for pathways and credentials into learning or earning.

Goodwall has a clear vision to engage 100 million youth over the next 5 years by leveraging incredible talent, technology and AI, being the most effective and efficient organisation in our industry and thereby creating the most impact. Our work has been featured on CNBC, CNN, Fast Company, the UN and UNESCO.

Goodwall believes that impact at scale comes from technology, financial sustainability and business rigour. We are a multicultural team across Europe, Africa and Asia, and have raised over $25M from leading strategic and financial backers.

Your Mission

As Talent & People Partner, you’ll attract and hire the people who will take Goodwall to its next stage, while ensuring our team of 35 feels supported, engaged and set up to do their best work. About 80% of your time goes to recruitment: we plan to hire around 8 people in 2027, from programme and partnerships roles to senior leaders. The rest goes to running our people operations so that every contract, onboarding and team conversation is handled well and on time.

Requirements

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Sourcing and recruitment: Own the hiring plan with the founders and fill each role end to end: write the job descriptions, source candidates directly on LinkedIn and through networks, screen, run interviews and case studies, and manage offers. Track every role in Recruitee so the pipeline is always current.

  • Senior hiring coordination: Run the process for senior hires with the founders, including shortlists, interview panels, references and offer terms.

  • Onboarding: Lead onboarding for every new joiner, with contracts, equipment, access and a clear first 90 days agreed with their manager.

  • Team relations: Be the person the team can speak to about their work, their questions and their concerns. Spot issues early and bring them to the right manager or founder.

  • People operations and contracts: Keep every employment and contractor contract current in Deel, RLabs and PeopleForce, along with the handbook, leave and the people side of the contract register. Pass pay changes to Finance for payroll.

  • Offboarding and employment matters: Manage offboardings and employee disputes with our employment counsel in South Africa, Spain, the UK and Switzerland, and prepare the documents and facts they need.

  • Performance and roles review: Run the performance cycle with each manager and the quarterly review of roles and responsibilities.

  • AI and systems: Work with the founders and our Head of Programs and AI to build AI tools and simple systems for hiring, onboarding and people admin, so the function stays light as we grow.

  • Special initiatives: Lead a few people initiatives each year, such as our team offsite, employer brand or a compensation framework.

Your Profile

You are a recruiter first, with the judgement of a people generalist. You like finding great people others missed, you keep a hiring process moving without being chased, and you are hyper-organised with the details that matter to the team. You bring the following:

  • 6 to 10 years of experience in talent acquisition, mostly in-house at scale-ups, plus some generalist HR

  • Experience building a people function for the first time at a company of 20 to 80 people

  • A track record of sourcing commercial, partnerships and senior roles directly, across South Africa, the UK, Europe and the US

  • Hands-on experience with onboarding, offboarding and employee disputes, working with employment counsel; working knowledge of South African labour law

  • Fluency with AI tools for sourcing, screening and admin; experience with Recruitee, Deel or PeopleForce is a plus

  • Excellent organisation: contracts, records and processes are always up to date

  • Discretion and sound judgement with confidential and sensitive matters

  • Clear, warm communication with candidates, managers and the team

  • A deliberate choice to work fractionally, with the time to commit 2 days a week

  • Strong interest in youth, skills, education and the future of work

What we offer

  • A mission you can be proud of and a meaningful opportunity and responsibility to impact the future of the next generation.

  • The chance to shape who joins Goodwall and how our team grows, working directly with the founders.

  • To leverage cutting edge, award winning technology and work alongside globally leading organisations to achieve outsized impact.

  • Autonomy to manage your time and efforts to achieve our goals.

  • A challenging, fast-moving environment working with an international team where change is constant and creativity is celebrated.

  • A position with the potential to evolve as you acquire new skills, grow, influence and take on new responsibilities.

  • Competitive compensation and a flexible work environment with a great team.

Highlights

As Talent & People Partner, you’ll attract and hire the people who will take Goodwall to its next stage, while ensuring our team feels supported, engaged and set up to do their best work.

Position Purpose:

Provides enterprise-wide leadership and strategic direction for third party risk management from a compliance perspective, including the audit, monitoring, and oversight of delegated healthcare functions. Establishes the governance model, risk framework, enterprise standards, and multi-year roadmap to identify, assess, monitor, escalate, and remediate third party compliance risk across Medicare, Medicaid, and Marketplace environments. Holds accountability for program effectiveness, risk-based audit and monitoring, regulatory and accreditation readiness, and executive and board reporting. Leads directors, other people leaders, and teams of audit, monitoring, compliance, and delegated oversight professionals, partnering with Compliance, Legal, Procurement, Operations, Enterprise Risk, and business owners to strengthen third party accountability and consistent enterprise execution.


Key Details: Applicants for this job have the flexibility to work remote from home anywhere in the Continental United States. A Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) certification is required for this role.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Establishes the enterprise strategy, governance model, risk framework, and decision rights for third party risk management from a compliance perspective, aligning regulatory expectations, accreditation requirements, contractual obligations, enterprise risk appetite, and business objectives.
  • Defines and sponsors the multi-year operating roadmap, investment priorities, performance measures, scalable processes and technology, and organizational capabilities needed to mature the program and meet enterprise demand.
  • Owns the design and effectiveness of the enterprise third party risk management framework, including risk segmentation, due diligence standards, control expectations, quality assurance, and program effectiveness evaluation.
  • Leads the enterprise delegated entity audit and monitoring program and directs risk-based audit plans for delegated entities, vendors, pharmacy benefit managers, third-party administrators, credentialing organizations, and other third parties.
  • Oversees audit planning, execution, reporting, and validation, ensuring audit methodologies meet regulatory expectations and industry standards.
  • Oversees auditing and monitoring of delegated operational, regulatory, clinical, pharmacy, claims, credentialing, utilization management, customer service, and other healthcare functions, including Medicare and Medicaid delegation oversight.
  • Directs enterprise oversight of the third party lifecycle, establishing consistent requirements for due diligence, risk assessment, compliance monitoring, performance oversight, issue management, corrective action, termination or transition risk, and regulatory readiness.
  • Directs audit issue identification, root cause analysis, corrective action validation, and closure. Establishes thresholds for risk acceptance, issue classification, escalation, remediation, and reporting, and serves as the senior escalation point for material, systemic, or cross-business third party compliance risks.
  • Chairs enterprise governance forums and directs cross-functional decisions that strengthen third party risk transparency, accountability, and mitigation across Compliance, Legal, Procurement, Operations, Enterprise Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Oversees regulatory, contractual, and operational reporting from third parties. Leads organizational responses to CMS audits, external quality reviews, other regulatory examinations, delegated oversight reviews, external audits, and compliance assessments related to third party performance, including responses to significant findings and systemic control deficiencies.
  • Advises executive leaders and business owners on regulatory change, emerging risk, third party concentration or dependency concerns, and significant control gaps, influencing enterprise priorities and corrective actions.
  • Directs executive and board-level reporting on risk exposure, trends, material issues, program performance, and remediation status, translating complex information into recommendations that support enterprise decisions and risk prioritization.
  • Leads directors, other people leaders, and teams of auditors, monitoring specialists, compliance analysts, and delegated oversight professionals. Establishes organizational structure, resource planning, succession and talent strategies, leadership expectations, and accountability for consistent enterprise outcomes.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Leadership experience leading managers or other people leaders and directing work across multiple business areas or operating units.
  • Experience advising executive leadership and presenting material risk, program performance, or regulatory matters to executive governance committees and/or boards.
  • Knowledge of healthcare regulatory requirements and government-sponsored programs, including Medicare, Medicaid, and Marketplace environments.

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) required
  • Certified in Healthcare Compliance (CHC) preferred:

jobs.excerpt: About the roleThe Leader of Product Operations builds the operating system that helps Xplor use AI responsibly, adopt it widely, and turn it into revenue and contribution margin, with clear governance and accountability for the results.
jobs.description:
About the role

The Leader of Product Operations builds the operating system that helps Xplor use AI responsibly, adopt it widely, and turn it into revenue and contribution margin, with clear governance and accountability for the results. The role covers three connected areas: AI-enabled productivity, adoption of AI features by our customers, and the commercialization of those features. You will own the shared layer that makes all three work including measurement, value tracking, portfolio governance, intake, cost visibility, and the operating cadence that keeps leaders aligned.

Our products and teams span a wide mix of tools and workflow methodologies. You will create a shared layer of measurement, visibility and improvement that works across them, and that product, engineering, go-to-market and executive leaders all trust, and speeds teams up without creating friction.

You will report to the Chief AI Officer and partner closely with BU presidents, product and R&D leaders, GTM, Finance, Security, Legal, Privacy and the People team. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will build the function and stay close to the data and the teams.

How we work: BUs are central's customers. We measure outcomes, not activity. We decide on a demo, an eval or a metric, not a deck. We keep forums and reporting to the minimum that supports a real decision.

What you'll do

Own the measurement and board scorecard

  • Build and run a single scorecard with Finance that records every AI benefit, in one engine, net of AI cost (inference, hosting, tools and support).
  • Produce the quarterly AI board scorecard covering value and risk measures, with a named owner and source system for every measure.
  • Run a repeatable prioritization and triage process for operations and tooling improvements, with clear owners, expected impact and follow-up on results.
  • Turn data into short, decision-ready narratives for the Chief AI Officer and C-suite.

Measure AI-enabled productivity

  • Build a measurement framework that links delivery and AI-SDLC productivity signals (cycle time, throughput, quality, adoption of AI tooling) to business outcomes such as idea-to-customer lead time, PR-to-production rate, change failure rate, escaped defects, rework and capacity moved to customer-facing work.
  • Help leaders see where AI productivity gains are real, where they are not, and where to invest next.
  • Act as a neutral orchestrator across teams that use different tools and methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe-style and hybrids; Jira, Azure DevOps and others), meeting each team where it is.
  • Find where gains stall before reaching customers (review wait, regression coverage, late QA, launch readiness) and route the fix.
  • Partner with function owners in support, revenue operations, finance and onboarding to baseline target workflows on fully loaded cost per resolved outcome, with quality held constant.

Measure AI product adoption and commercialization

  • Own the metrics and standardize reporting for how customers adopt and use AI features across the portfolio at 30-60-90 days, from activation and usage depth to retention and satisfaction.
  • Build the commercial view with Finance and BU leaders: AI and data ARR, paid attach, retention and expansion, win-rate uplift, gross margin per AI feature and cost per successful task.
  • Run the launch-readiness checklist with BU leaders before any AI price goes live: cost per task known, margin target met after inference, attribution rule and holdout set, sales and customer success enablement ready.

Govern Data and AI accountability

  • Operationalize and maintain decision rights, escalation paths and clear ownership for data and AI initiatives, so every investment has a named accountable owner, success measures, and a review date.
  • Maintain a portfolio-level register of Data and AI initiatives and risks, and surface issues early to the Chief AI Officer with recommended actions.
  • Run the Data and AI vendor and partner inventory and monthly review with Procurement, Finance and Security: spend, overlap, security review, data terms and knowledge transfer from consultants.
  • Track adherence to agreed standards and policies, and report exceptions without becoming a bottleneck for teams.

Lead the function

  • Hire, develop and lead a product operations team, and set its mandate, operating model and success measures.
  • Apply AI to product operations itself, including automated reporting, insight synthesis and workflow automation.

What you'll bring

Required

  • 8+ years in product operations, business operations, strategy and operations, technical program management, product management, or a similar role in a SaaS or technology company, with at least 3 years at a senior or director level.
  • A track record of building KPI and measurement frameworks that connect product or delivery data to business outcomes such as adoption, retention and revenue.
  • Experience working with Finance, Sales and Marketing on pricing, packaging, launch or go-to-market performance.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives across Product, Engineering, Customer Success and executive leadership, and influencing without direct authority, including establishing governance, decision rights and accountability mechanisms that teams actually follow.
  • Working knowledge of multiple delivery methodologies (Agile, Scrum, Kanban, SAFe) and the ability to support teams that use different ones.
  • Hands-on fluency with product and delivery tooling (Jira or similar), product analytics, BI and data integration across systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including presenting data and tradeoffs clearly to executives.
  • Experience building or leading a team, including hiring and coaching.
    •

Preferred

  • Experience with product adoption, monetization, or usage-based pricing.
  • Experience measuring the impact of AI-assisted development or other engineering productivity programs, including frameworks such as DORA and SPACE.
  • Experience in vertical SaaS or a multi-product portfolio, including products at different stages of modernization.
  • Comfort using AI tools and automation in your own daily operating workflow.
  • Experience with governance, risk classification or responsible-AI programs, working alongside Security, Legal and Privacy.
  • Experience managing a vendor and partner portfolio, including consolidation and contract standards.
  • Experience with cloud or AI cost management (FinOps): unit economics, cost per task.
    •

Success Measurement

1. First 30 Days: Inventory of AI tools, vendors, spend, pilots and production systems complete. Baseline scorecard and product readiness cards published. Steering cadence and decision log running.

2. 60 Days: Board scorecard reported on its first full quarter in partnership with FinOps and BU leaders. Cost visibility by BU and product in place. Adoption and cost per task tracked for every live AI pilot. Stage gates in use for new initiatives.

3. 90 Days: AI ARR, margin and retention-vs-holdout reported for launched features. Efficiency savings documented. Governance service levels published and met. Product operations running with its own efficiency and productivity measures.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Before you apply

To be considered for employment, you must be legally authorized to work in the country where the role is advertised. This applies to remote roles too. Xplor does not sponsor visas, either at the time of hire or at any later time. We're also not able to offer contractor arrangements or Employer of Record engagements for this position at this stage.

Please apply through our careers portal or external job boards only. We're unable to upload emailed applications, as our process requires you to answer screening questions directly.

Interview Recording and Background Checks

EEO and Artificial Intelligence

About Sunrise Group

Sunrise Group is building the future of sleep health by combining breakthrough technology with expert care. We started in 2015 with a straightforward idea: sleep diagnosis should happen in the comfort of your own home, not in a hospital. To make that possible, we created a first-of-its-kind chin sensor, carefully validated through clinical research, reviewed by leading sleep experts, and cleared by the FDA.

Since then, Sunrise Group has grown from a single innovation into a complete sleep health company. We now design advanced diagnostic and treatment solutions, and we deliver care directly to patients through Dreem Health, our digital sleep clinic. By serving patients in all 50 states with reimbursed care, we are making sleep treatment more accessible, more personal, and much simpler than it has ever been.

Your Opportunity

Reporting to the VP of Provider Partnerships, the Referral Coordinator is the first point of contact for patients entering the Dreem Health care journey. You will manage all incoming referrals from providers, ensure accurate and timely processing in our systems, and deliver high-quality patient communication with empathy and clarity. jobs.excerpt: ABOUT SYNERGY PRIVATESynergy Private is a multidisciplinary family office platform serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, founders, and executives.
jobs.description:
ABOUT SYNERGY PRIVATE
Synergy Private is a multidisciplinary family office platform serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, founders, and executives. We coordinate sophisticated financial matters across tax, investments, risk management, estate planning, and business affairs.
Our practice operates through three complementary service offerings:
• Advisory: Comprehensive planning and strategic advice across tax, investments, risk, and estate planning.
• Management: Ongoing coordination, project management, and oversight of the implementation of clients' personal financial strategies.
• Family Office Services (FOS): Execution of specialized services such as accounting, tax preparation, investment management, document drafting, and related services.

THE OPPORTUNITY
We are hiring two Family Office Operations Managers who will work as peers, supporting each other in managing the affairs of our family office clients and serving as central relationship and implementation managers for our clients.
Both positions share the responsibilities and qualifications below. Ideally, one will bring deep private banking and wealth management experience and the other deep tax and estate planning experience, so that the two complement each other.
This is not a traditional client service or administrative position. We need a multidisciplinary professional who understands how complex financial, tax, legal, and business matters intersect—and possesses the judgment, organizational ability, and professional fluency to coordinate their execution.
The ideal candidate has substantial experience serving affluent families, executives, entrepreneurs, or closely held businesses, preferably within a family office, private bank, wealth management firm, tax advisory practice, or private-client law firm.
Expertise or licensure in every financial planning discipline is not expected. Sufficient technical knowledge to identify needs, engage the right specialists, understand dependencies, and ensure completion is essential. This role will be supported by extensive AI tools and internal resources; comfort with AI and an exceptional ability to learn quickly are highly valued.

Key Responsibilities


1. Family Office Management
• Deliver ongoing Family Office Management alongside a peer Operations Manager, serving as a primary coordination and implementation resource for client families.
• Translate approved financial plans and strategies, client decisions, and advisory recommendations into actionable projects with clear ownership, timelines, and deliverables.
• Manage concurrent initiatives across tax, investments, insurance, estate planning, business structuring, lending, and other financial affairs.
• Anticipate dependencies, identify potential conflicts, and ensure activities occur in the appropriate sequence.

2. Client Relationship & Request Management
• Serve as the central point of coordination for inbound client requests, inquiries, and service needs.
• Evaluate and route matters requiring strategic advice, specialized professional expertise, or administrative execution.
• Maintain accountability for all outstanding client commitments, ensuring responsiveness, proactive communication, and timely resolution.
• Build trusted, long-term relationships through professional judgment, discretion, and exceptional follow-through.

3. Cross-Disciplinary Project Management
• Coordinate internal teams, affiliated companies, attorneys, CPAs, investment advisers, insurance professionals, lenders, and other external specialists.
• Manage implementation of complex financial transactions and planning strategies involving multiple professional disciplines.
• Ensure service providers have the necessary information, understand responsibilities, and meet deadlines.
• Oversee fulfillment of Family Office Services engagements, including for clients who do not subscribe to ongoing Family Office Management.

Example: When a client acquires an investment property, recognize the potential need for legal/entity structuring, financing, title coordination, insurance coverage, and tax-planning updates—and manage the relevant professionals through the transaction.

4. Advisory Coordination & Implementation
• Partner closely with the Principal Advisor to transition approved advisory recommendations into executable implementation plans.
• Coordinate information gathering, implementation status, outstanding decisions, and professional follow-up between advisory engagements.
• Escalate matters requiring professional advice or licensed expertise to the appropriate adviser or specialist.
• Own implementation without independently developing or delivering specialized tax, legal, investment, or insurance advice.

5. Operational Excellence, Technology & AI
• Maintain comprehensive oversight of client projects, commitments, deliverables, and communications within firm management systems.
• Review work products for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and readiness for professional review or client delivery.
• Use firm-provided AI agents, research tools, and workflow automation to manage requests, accelerate information gathering, support rapid learning, and improve service delivery.
• Critically validate AI-generated information and work products, safeguard confidential client information, and escalate judgment-sensitive matters to qualified professionals.
• Develop scalable procedures, continuously master new concepts and tools, and improve the Family Office Management function as the firm grows.

Qualification & Required Experience

Professional Experience
• 4–6 years in family office services, private banking, private wealth management, private-client legal services, tax advisory, or related professional services.
• Demonstrated experience with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth clients, executives, business owners, or complex family enterprises.
• Strong understanding of tax planning, business entities, estate planning, investments, insurance, and each discipline’s professional responsibilities.
• Experience managing multidisciplinary projects involving attorneys, accountants, financial advisers, and other service providers.
• Deep experience in either private banking and wealth management, or tax and estate planning, is especially desirable.
• Demonstrated proficiency with AI-powered tools, or a proven ability to rapidly learn new technology and unfamiliar subject matter, is highly desirable.

Professional Credentials
A CFP®, CPA, JD, EA, CPWA, or comparable professional credential is strongly preferred, although equivalent experience and demonstrated technical competence will be considered. Multiple licenses or designations are not required.

Personal Attributes
• Exceptional organization, ownership mentality, and attention to detail.
• Intellectual curiosity and the ability to grasp sophisticated financial and legal concepts without practicing in each discipline.
• Strong judgment, executive presence, and confidence engaging sophisticated clients and advisers.
• Proactive communication, discretion, accountability, and independent prioritization.
• Adaptability, resourcefulness, and a strong willingness to work alongside evolving AI-enabled resources.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
Every client request has a clear owner, every commitment is tracked, and every approved strategy progresses toward implementation. Clients experience one coordinated family office relationship, even when multiple specialized professionals are responsible for execution.
Advisory leadership remains focused on strategy and professional advice, while the Family Office Operations Managers ensure the work required to implement those decisions gets done.

Benefits

  • Paid holidays
  • Unlimited Vacation
  • Sick Time
  • Work from home
  • Medical, Dental, vision
  • 401k plus match
