jobs.description:
Field Sales Representative

Location: Kingston Upon Thames, covering Kingston or surrounding areas such as Esher, Weybridge, Walton, Richmond or Twickenham (fully field-based)

£50,000–£90,000 OTE (£30,000–£54,000 base salary + uncapped commission, based on experience) + £800 monthly car allowance and a comprehensive benefits package

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re ambitious, enjoy meeting new people and want to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We’re looking for ambitious, driven people to join our growing Field Sales team and help bring Teya to more local businesses across the UK.

As a Field Sales Representative, you’ll take ownership of your own territory, getting out into your local community, meeting business owners face-to-face and showing them how Teya can help their businesses thrive.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the field, building relationships and winning new business. You’ll have the freedom to manage your territory, the support of a team that wants you to succeed, and the opportunity to build a rewarding career in sales.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own your territory: Proactively identify and engage local businesses through face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals and other opportunities to generate new business.

  • Build meaningful relationships: Get to know business owners, understand their challenges and identify how Teya’s products and services can make their lives easier.

  • Win new Members: Use a consultative, value-led approach to demonstrate Teya’s solutions, build trust and turn conversations into long-term customer relationships.

  • Deliver results: Take ownership of your sales performance, maintain a healthy pipeline and consistently work towards your commercial targets.

  • See things through: Take responsibility for your Members’ experience from the first conversation through to onboarding, ensuring they’re set up successfully and ready to start using Teya.

  • Keep learning: Develop strong knowledge of our products, competitors and sales methodology through structured training, coaching and feedback.

  • Represent Teya: Be a trusted face of Teya in your local community, delivering the genuine care and hospitality that we want every Member to experience.

  • Help us improve: Share insights from the field to help us continuously improve our products, sales approach and Member experience.

Your Story

We believe great salespeople come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might already be an experienced field sales professional with a strong track record of winning new business. Or you might be earlier in your career, with the ambition, drive and potential to become an exceptional salesperson.

What matters most to us is your mindset, your ability to connect with people and your willingness to learn and improve.

We’re looking for people who bring:

  • Ambition and drive: You’re motivated to succeed, enjoy working towards challenging goals and take pride in delivering great results.

  • A competitive mindset: You enjoy winning, hold yourself to high standards and are always looking for ways to improve.

  • Resilience and determination: You’re comfortable with rejection, stay positive when things get tough and don’t give up easily.

  • Strong people skills: You enjoy meeting new people, build rapport naturally and can have meaningful conversations with business owners from all walks of life.

  • Curiosity and commercial awareness: You ask good questions, listen carefully and want to understand what makes a business successful.

  • Coachability: You’re open to feedback, willing to challenge yourself and committed to developing your skills.

  • Ownership and self-discipline: You’re organised, proactive and comfortable managing your own time and priorities in a field-based role.

  • A genuine care for others: You understand that great sales isn’t just about closing a deal. It’s about doing what’s right for the customer and building trust that lasts.

Experience in field sales, business development, payments or financial services is an advantage, but not essential for every level. We care just as much about your potential as your experience.

You’ll also need:

  • Fluency in English.

  • A full UK driving licence and access to a car.

  • The right to work in the UK.

  • Willingness to work in a fully field-based role, travelling regularly throughout your territory.

The Perks

We believe great performance should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

  • £30,000–£54,000 base salary, depending on your experience and demonstrated capability.

  • Uncapped commission.

  • £800 per month car allowance (£9,600 annually), on top of your salary and commission.

  • 25 days of paid annual leave, plus UK bank holidays.

  • Bupa private healthcare and life insurance.

  • Employer pension contributions through our company pension scheme.

  • Free gym membership through Wellhub, alongside one-to-one therapy sessions, meditation and digital fitness and nutrition apps.

  • Structured onboarding, practical sales training, ongoing coaching and opportunities to grow your career at Teya.

What Happens Next?

Our recruitment process is designed to help us get to know you, understand your strengths and give you a genuine opportunity to show us what you can do.

Stage 1 - Introductory conversation (30 minutes)
A conversation with our Talent team to learn more about you, your motivation and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2 - Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes)
An opportunity to explore your experience, how you approach challenges and what makes you successful.

Stage 3 - Final Assessment (60 minutes)
You’ll meet members of our Sales leadership team, present a short territory plan and take part in a practical sales role-play. We’ll share everything you need to prepare in advance.

We know interviews are a two-way process, and we’ll make sure you have plenty of opportunities to ask questions and get to know us along the way.

Teya is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, including those without a traditional sales or commercial track record.

Teya is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or background can thrive and do their best work. We believe that a diverse team leads to better ideas, stronger outcomes, and a more supportive workplace for all.

If you require any reasonable adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process whether for interviews, assessments, or other parts of the application—we encourage you to let us know. We are committed to ensuring that every candidate has a fair and accessible experience with us.

You'll help us find the right balance between what LLMs do well and the quality, review, and maintainability standards a regulated fintech business requires. jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityFutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadComparo, an AI-native residential appraisal venture.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadComparo, an AI-native residential appraisal venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Comparois an AI-native residential appraisal firm built for independent mortgage banks and private lenders. Today, a lender waits 5 to 10 days for an appraisal that takes under an hour of real analytical work. Comparo collapses that to 24 hours. Homeowners or data collectors capture the property with a phone scan, AI selects comparables, runs adjustments and drafts the full report, and a licensed appraiser reviews and signs. Comparo sells the finished, UAD 3.6-compliant appraisal rather than software, so it owns the workflow end to end and captures the full per-report fee. The same engine extends to tax appeals, insurance, estate valuations and continuous portfolio revaluation for lenders and mortgage-backed asset holders.

Market Context

The US residential appraisal industry is an $8.8-11.4B market, with roughly 5 million appraisals completed each year at $400-700 per report. Mortgage appraisals ordered by independent mortgage banks and private lenders represent a $1.5-2.1B serviceable market. The timing is sharp: UAD 3.6 becomes mandatory on November 2, 2026, expanding each report from roughly 700 to 3,600 data fields, while an aging workforce of 75,000–80,000 licensed appraisers shrinks.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

  • Investor and advisor network across fintech, proptech and early-stage capital markets

  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with independent mortgage banks and private lenders, convert them to paid engagements, secure approved-panel status, and build the go-to-market motion

  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback

  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction

  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement

  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

  • Direct exposure to mortgage lending, residential appraisal, AMC operations, or proptech

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

About Epic School Plus

Epic is the world's largest digital library for kids. Epic School Plus is the paid school and district version of Epic. It gives schools and districts administrator visibility through the Admin Portal, 24/7 and year-round access to 40,000+ books (including offline reading), more than 3,500 Spanish, Mandarin and French titles, and decodables for beginning readers aligned to 23 popular literacy curricula, including CKLA, UFLI and Benchmark Advance. When a district funds access, every family gets the same library at no cost to families.

Over one million teachers already use Epic School (free version) in their classrooms. Your job is to help the schools and districts behind them make Epic School Plus part of their reading plan.

About the Role

As a District Sales Specialist, you'll serve as one of the first points of contact for schools and districts interested in Epic School Plus. The role involves leading discovery calls and product walkthroughs with principals, curriculum and literacy directors, instructional coaches, and librarians, while following up on larger district opportunities to help move them through the district budget cycle.

This position works closely with our operations team, which handles quotes and provisioning, as well as our sales lead for the Northeast and Midwest.

This is apart-time contract role, working 20 to 30 hours per week, with approximately 25 to 30 hours a week from January through May, when districts plan budgets and approve purchases, and 20 to 25 hours a week from June through December.

What You'll Do

  • Run discovery calls and walkthroughs (about half your time):respond quickly to schools and districts that ask for a call, learn who champions, who builds the case and who signs, and show how Epic School Plus fits their reading goals.

  • Follow up on larger district opportunities (about a third of your time):re-engage open opportunities, find the decision-makers, keep stages and close dates accurate, and close out opportunities that aren't moving.

  • Keep the talk track sharp:maintain our discovery script, walkthrough and objection guide, and share what you hear from educators so our marketing and product teams can act on it.

  • Keep the CRM clean:log every call, contact and next step in Salesforce so the team can see what's happening in each account.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience in B2B sales, preferably within EdTech or the K–12 education industry.

  • Confidence leading video calls with school and district leaders.

  • Clear, warm writing for follow-up emails and notes.

  • Working knowledge of how districts buy: budget planning, board approvals and purchase orders.

jobs.excerpt: About Sundays for Dogs Sundays for Dogs is a founder-led, direct-to-consumer brand reimagining pet food so dog owners can spend more quality time with their dogs — now and later.
jobs.description:
About Sundays for Dogs

Sundays for Dogs is a founder-led, direct-to-consumer brand reimagining pet food so dog owners can spend more quality time with their dogs — now and later. We make human-grade, air-dried food that supports long, healthy lives, and we build our company around shared core values that guide how we work and how we treat each other.

We’re headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, with a primarily remote team of ~50 full-time employees across the U.S. While we work distributed day to day, we come together in person on a quarterly basis because relationships matter. Our business today is 100% DTC, with our subscription model at the core of how we serve customers — and we’re building to scale with intention. We’re just getting started...

About your team and position:

The Operations team at Sundays for Dogs spans supply chain, fulfillment, quality, and is responsible for getting a premium, perishable product into customers' hands reliably as we scale from roughly $110M toward $250M. We run on an EOS/L10 operating cadence, which means clear ownership, weekly accountability, and a bias toward solving root causes over patching symptoms. We're in the middle of standing up a formal S&OP process and rebuilding our co-manufacturing network, so there's real ground to break in this role rather than a process to simply maintain.

The Sr. Planner will own the S&OP process end to end: demand planning, supply planning, and the monthly cycle that brings them together into one forecast the business can trust. You'll build the demand forecast, translate it into supply and purchasing plans across our co-manufacturing network, and own the inventory and service level outcomes that follow. This is a highly analytical, highly cross-functional role. You'll be the person who can say with confidence what we expect to sell, what we need to make, and what that means for inventory and cash.

The Sr. Planner reports to the Sr. Director, Supply Chain. No direct reports today, with room to grow the team as the S&OP process matures. You'll work closely with Purchasing and Logistics on execution, with Finance on inventory and cash implications, with R&D and Quality on new recipe launches and co-manufacturing transitions, and Marketing on demand model inputs and levers. This is a contract position that concludes in mid-January.

Your day-to-day:

  • Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end, building the demand forecast, reconciling it with supply capacity, and driving the meeting where the business aligns on one number.
  • Build and maintain the demand forecast by SKU and channel, incorporating promotional activity, subscription trends, and new product launches.
  • Translate the demand forecast into a supply and purchasing plan across our co-manufacturing network, flagging capacity constraints before they become stockouts.
  • Own inventory targets and turns, balancing service level against working capital so we're neither out of stock nor overstocked.
  • Build the reporting that gives the business a clear, trusted view of forecast accuracy, inventory health, and supply risk.
  • Partner with Purchasing and Logistics to convert the supply plan into purchase orders and inbound schedules that actually land on time.
  • Flag and help resolve OOS risk early, working with Marketing, Fulfillment and Customer Care so the business isn't surprised by a stockout.

What success looks like:

First 30 days: Full visibility into current demand and supply data, forecast history, and open OOS risks, with a documented view of how planning works today across every SKU and facility.

First 90 days: A monthly S&OP cycle running on a fixed cadence with a documented process, feeding a single forecast that Purchasing, Marketing, Finance, and Supply Chain leadership all plan against.

Ongoing Metrics: Forecast accuracy, fill rate, and inventory turns tracked and reported on a consistent schedule, with OOS incidents caught and flagged before they hit the customer.

30/60/90 Plan: The scorecard (metrics of performance) and the 30/60/90 day plan for the Sr Planner role is met.

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • You have 5+ years of experience in demand planning, supply planning, or S&OP, ideally in a food, CPG, or DTC subscription business.
  • You have proven experience building or running an S&OP process, not just participating in one someone else designed.
  • You have strong Excel or modeling skills and are comfortable building your own forecasts rather than relying on someone else's output.
  • You have experience planning across a multi-facility or co-manufacturing network, including navigating capacity constraints and lead times.
  • You have the ability to work cross-functionally and hold your ground on the numbers when priorities compete.
  • You have a track record of catching risk early and communicating it clearly, rather than letting it surface as a surprise.
  • You have the ability to operate with real autonomy in a fast-growing environment where you're building process as you go.

jobs.description:
Spinwheel is the agentic API platform for real-time consumer credit data and payments. With just a phone number and date of birth, financial innovators get instant access to complete consumer credit data, attributes, and payments, all through a single, beautifully simple API.

We serve banks, lenders, fintechs, credit unions, and other financial services companies that need to verify identity, understand consumer debt, and execute payments at scale. Our platform combines Connect (identity and account authentication), Profile (real-time debt intelligence from all three bureaus), and Pay (payments and balance transfers) into a unified infrastructure layer.

We're a growth-stage company. The team is lean, the clients are sophisticated, and the market opportunity is large. The sales motion is enterprise B2B: complex, consultative, and technical.

The Role

We're hiring an Enterprise Account Executive to own new business. This is a full-cycle role. You'll run discovery, structure deals, navigate legal and technical procurement, and close new clients across our primary verticals: banks, lenders, and fintechs.

You'll work closely with SDRs, Product Marketing, and our technical team. You'll also carry commercial ownership for your largest accounts post-close, acting as the de facto account manager until a deal reaches the scale to warrant a dedicated handoff.

This is not a commodity sale. Spinwheel's buyers are product managers, payments leads, and engineering stakeholders, and are sophisticated about what they're buying. The AE who succeeds here can articulate infrastructure tradeoffs, navigate multi-stakeholder deals, and build executive relationships with financial institutions.

What You'll Own

New Business

  • Manage the full sales cycle for new clients, from inbound qualification and outbound prospecting through discovery, demo, negotiation, and close.
  • Run structured discovery to understand a prospect's consumer credit lifecycle, technical architecture, and current vendors before proposing a solution.
  • Navigate multi-stakeholder deals involving product, engineering, legal, compliance, and executive buyers.
  • Collaborate with SDRs on account strategy for target accounts; provide clear feedback to improve inbound qualification.
  • Build and maintain a pipeline with sufficient coverage to meet targets; forecast accurately and consistently in HubSpot.
Market Intelligence and Collaboration
  • Develop a working knowledge of the competitive landscape, including competition, bureau-direct options, and adjacent players, and apply it in active deals.
  • Share deal learnings, win/loss patterns, and buyer language with Product Marketing to sharpen positioning and enablement materials.
  • Flag product gaps and market signals to product and leadership as a trusted voice of the buyer.

What We're Looking For

Experience

  • 5+ years of full-cycle B2B sales experience, with at least 2 years direct Fintech, API, or selling into lending institutions (banks, lenders, fintechs, credit unions).
  • Experience and track record of success closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals rather than transactional volume sales.
  • Experience selling infrastructure, data, or API-based products is strongly preferred. You don't need to write code, but you need to understand how APIs are evaluated and bought.
  • Familiarity with the consumer credit ecosystem, including bureaus, identity verification, payments rails, or lending workflows, is a meaningful advantage.
  • Proven success meeting or exceeding quota

Skills and Attributes

  • Discovery-first mindset: you ask before you pitch, and you can translate a prospect's business problem into a product recommendation.
  • Technical fluency: comfortable in conversations that involve API integration, data normalization, compliance considerations, and technical architecture, even when you're not the technical expert in the room.
  • Intellectual honesty: you represent the product accurately, manage expectations clearly, and know when a deal isn't a fit.
  • Data-driven: you own your pipeline numbers, understand what they mean, and use them to prioritize your time.
  • Grit: the fintech sales cycle can be long, the buying committee is complex, and deals stall. You stay persistent and creative without becoming pushy.
  • Collaboration: you work well with SDRs, CSMs, and technical resources. You prepare properly before bringing in support, and you give credit freely.

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary and variable compensation (50% base, 50% commission).
  • Equity in a high-growth infrastructure company at an early and critical stage.
  • A lean, high-trust environment where your deals actually move the needle.
  • Direct access to leadership, product, and engineering with no bureaucracy between you and the answers you need.
  • Opportunity to help shape the sales process, not just execute it.

jobs.excerpt: Column is the software platform for public information.
jobs.description:
Column is the software platform for public information. We build automated tools and workflow solutions that help governments, law firms, and media organizations notify the public. Today, thousands of publishers and tens of thousands of agencies, firms, and individuals rely on Column to keep their communities informed every day. We’re reimagining how public information connects people, institutions, and media.

We're a remote-first team of engineers, designers, and builders who are committed to creating software that supports an informed public.

About The Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented compliance contractor to help rebuild our state and local compliance system over a 12-week project. The work covers an account register, state requirements research, a certificate and renewal tracker, and a 12-month compliance calendar with a runbook to go with it. You'll research and recommend, and we'll make the decisions and handle filings and payments. This is a project-based engagement with clear deliverables and a defined end date.

What You'll Do

  • Build a register of every state and local registration, tax account, and insurance carrier, with owners and renewal dates. Record account numbers only as masked references.
  • Research and document state requirements for each state where we have employees or other nexus: unemployment filings, withholding, new-hire reporting, required postings, paid leave, workers' comp, and local taxes. Cite a primary source and a verification date for each item, and list anything you couldn't verify as an open item.
  • Build a certificate and renewal database for insurance, licenses, permits, and registrations. Collect and check vendor certificates, and flag anything expiring within 90 days.
  • Build a 12-month compliance calendar with due dates, reminders at 30, 14, and 7 days, and an owner and approver for every item.
  • Write a short runbook for each recurring obligation, so the calendar can be run without you.
  • Deliver an evaluation memo recommending whether we should continue this work, hand it off internally, or outsource it after the term.

What Success Looks Like

  • All six deliverables will be delivered by the end of the 12-week term, owned by the contractor.
  • Compliance calendar will have an owner and an approver for every item by the end of the term, owned by the contractor.
  • State requirements will cite a primary source and verification date for every item, with any unverified items listed as open, owned by the contractor.
  • Certificates and licenses will each have an expiration date and document link, with nothing expiring within 90 days left unflagged, owned by the contractor.
  • Handoff will be confirmed before the term ends: the People Ops Manager updates one calendar item and one certificate renewal using only the runbook and records, without asking the contractor for help. Owned by the contractor, confirmed by the People Ops Manager.

Must Haves

  • Working knowledge of state unemployment, payroll tax, and workers' comp requirements, with experience across more than one state.
  • Experience building compliance calendars, trackers, or checklists in a spreadsheet.
  • Able to work without daily direction and to meet agreed due dates.

Nice to Haves

  • SHRM-CP, PHR, or equivalent certification.
  • Experience with insurance certificate tracking or vendor compliance programs.
  • Experience with state audit or claims processes.

Core Values

  • Be the person people can count on: You own the compliance calendar end to end and set clear expectations for every deadline.
  • Clear focus: You prioritize the filings and deadlines that matter most and communicate status in plain terms.
  • Grit and growth mindset: You take on the hard research questions, verify what you find, and improve the system as you learn.
  • T.E.A.M. (Together everyone achieves more): You leave a runbook and calendar the whole team can use, so the work doesn't stop when the project ends.

Why This Role Matters

Accurate compliance records protect us from missed filings, lapsed insurance, and avoidable penalties. Right now our account information, certificates, and deadlines are spread across several places. A clear calendar and a reliable certificate tracker mean nothing slips through, and our team can run the process with confidence after the project ends.

Terms of Engagement

  • Compensation: $1,000 – $2,000 per month, depending on the final agreed scope of work and jurisdictional coverage.
  • Hours: Up to 40 hours per month. No minimum hours are guaranteed, and you set your own schedule.
  • Work: You control your methods, location, and schedule, and you may serve other clients. There are no fixed daily or weekly meetings. We check in when each deliverable is delivered.
  • Equipment and tools: You use your own equipment and business tools.
  • Access and security: Access is only through a company-controlled password manager, limited to what the deliverables need, and removed at the end of the term.

jobs.description:
Field Sales Representative

Location: Chichester, covering Chichester or surrounding areas (fully field-based)

£50,000–£90,000 OTE (£30,000–£54,000 base salary + uncapped commission, based on experience) + £800 monthly car allowance and a comprehensive benefits package

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re ambitious, enjoy meeting new people and want to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We’re looking for ambitious, driven people to join our growing Field Sales team and help bring Teya to more local businesses across the UK.

As a Field Sales Representative, you’ll take ownership of your own territory, getting out into your local community, meeting business owners face-to-face and showing them how Teya can help their businesses thrive.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the field, building relationships and winning new business. You’ll have the freedom to manage your territory, the support of a team that wants you to succeed, and the opportunity to build a rewarding career in sales.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own your territory: Proactively identify and engage local businesses through face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals and other opportunities to generate new business.

  • Build meaningful relationships: Get to know business owners, understand their challenges and identify how Teya’s products and services can make their lives easier.

  • Win new Members: Use a consultative, value-led approach to demonstrate Teya’s solutions, build trust and turn conversations into long-term customer relationships.

  • Deliver results: Take ownership of your sales performance, maintain a healthy pipeline and consistently work towards your commercial targets.

  • See things through: Take responsibility for your Members’ experience from the first conversation through to onboarding, ensuring they’re set up successfully and ready to start using Teya.

  • Keep learning: Develop strong knowledge of our products, competitors and sales methodology through structured training, coaching and feedback.

  • Represent Teya: Be a trusted face of Teya in your local community, delivering the genuine care and hospitality that we want every Member to experience.

  • Help us improve: Share insights from the field to help us continuously improve our products, sales approach and Member experience.

Your Story

We believe great salespeople come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might already be an experienced field sales professional with a strong track record of winning new business. Or you might be earlier in your career, with the ambition, drive and potential to become an exceptional salesperson.

What matters most to us is your mindset, your ability to connect with people and your willingness to learn and improve.

We’re looking for people who bring:

  • Ambition and drive: You’re motivated to succeed, enjoy working towards challenging goals and take pride in delivering great results.

  • A competitive mindset: You enjoy winning, hold yourself to high standards and are always looking for ways to improve.

  • Resilience and determination: You’re comfortable with rejection, stay positive when things get tough and don’t give up easily.

  • Strong people skills: You enjoy meeting new people, build rapport naturally and can have meaningful conversations with business owners from all walks of life.

  • Curiosity and commercial awareness: You ask good questions, listen carefully and want to understand what makes a business successful.

  • Coachability: You’re open to feedback, willing to challenge yourself and committed to developing your skills.

  • Ownership and self-discipline: You’re organised, proactive and comfortable managing your own time and priorities in a field-based role.

  • A genuine care for others: You understand that great sales isn’t just about closing a deal. It’s about doing what’s right for the customer and building trust that lasts.

Experience in field sales, business development, payments or financial services is an advantage, but not essential for every level. We care just as much about your potential as your experience.

You’ll also need:

  • Fluency in English.

  • A full UK driving licence and access to a car.

  • The right to work in the UK.

  • Willingness to work in a fully field-based role, travelling regularly throughout your territory.

The Perks

We believe great performance should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

  • £30,000–£54,000 base salary, depending on your experience and demonstrated capability.

  • Uncapped commission.

  • £800 per month car allowance (£9,600 annually), on top of your salary and commission.

  • 25 days of paid annual leave, plus UK bank holidays.

  • Bupa private healthcare and life insurance.

  • Employer pension contributions through our company pension scheme.

  • Free gym membership through Wellhub, alongside one-to-one therapy sessions, meditation and digital fitness and nutrition apps.

  • Structured onboarding, practical sales training, ongoing coaching and opportunities to grow your career at Teya.

What Happens Next?

Our recruitment process is designed to help us get to know you, understand your strengths and give you a genuine opportunity to show us what you can do.

Stage 1 - Introductory conversation (30 minutes)
A conversation with our Talent team to learn more about you, your motivation and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2 - Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes)
An opportunity to explore your experience, how you approach challenges and what makes you successful.

Stage 3 - Final Assessment (60 minutes)
You’ll meet members of our Sales leadership team, present a short territory plan and take part in a practical sales role-play. We’ll share everything you need to prepare in advance.

Combining clinical industry knowledge with business acumen and digital marketing strategy, this role is responsible for building trusted client relationships, developing long-term marketing strategies, and ensuring campaigns align with each practice's business objectives.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Grant Reviewer, Educator Pipeline (SOAR Educator Pipeline)
Work Arrangement: Remote
Location: Remote, United States
Employment Type: Part-Time, Independent Contractor (1099)
Engagement Type: Short-term, per grant competition; paid per application reviewed
Final Interview:

Position Summary

Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring Grant Reviewers on behalf of the Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE), the District of Columbia's state education agency, for its Scholarships for Opportunity and Results (SOAR) Educator Pipeline grant competition. OSSE is seeking experienced elementary and secondary education professionals with grant, evaluation, or budget experience to evaluate applications that strengthen the educator pipeline.

Grant reviewers provide independent subject matter expertise to read, score, and comment on competitive grant applications submitted by local education agencies, schools, community-based organizations, and other eligible entities. All reviews are completed remotely in OSSE's online Enterprise Grants Management System (EGMS), and reviewer scores are used to recommend applications for funding. OSSE selects reviewers from the qualified pool and gives preference to reviewers who have satisfactorily completed reviews for its competitions in previous years.

Work Schedule

This is a remote, part-time assignment. Reviews are completed on your own schedule within each deadline. The approximate commitment for this competition is:

  • Orientation and EGMS training: a virtual webinar held approximately within two weeks of the engagement start date.
  • Review window: usually two weeks from the date applications are assigned, unless OSSE specifies otherwise.
  • Facilitated discussion (only if needed): a phone or video conference, usually about three business days after the scoring due date, held when panel scores differ significantly.
  • Approximate completion of reviewer work: June 4, 2027. Final dates are confirmed before orientation.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Complete OSSE's EGMS training and attend the virtual, grant-specific orientation webinar before reviewing any applications.
  2. Independently read and conduct a detailed review of each assigned application (typically two or more per competition) as one of three reviewers on an EGMS review panel, working remotely and separately.
  3. Assess program design, implementation plans, and budgets for applications focused on strengthening the educator pipeline.
  4. Complete a fully scored rubric for every section of each application, applying the established scoring criteria consistently and objectively.
  5. Write clear, constructive comments describing strengths and weaknesses that justify and align with the scores given. Reviews may be shared with applicants on request, with reviewer names and contact information removed.
  6. Base all scores and comments only on the content of each applicant's submission in EGMS.
  7. Submit all scores and comments in EGMS by the review deadline, usually two weeks from receiving the applications.
  8. Participate in a facilitated panel discussion by phone or video conference when scores differ significantly, then submit a final rubric with updated scores and comments reflecting any changes.
  9. Disclose any conflict of interest with applicant organizations and do not review any application where a conflict exists.
  10. Direct EGMS technical questions to the EGMS manual, the resources at grants.osse.dc.gov, or the EGMS call center at (202) 719-6500, and direct questions about the grant or about scoring to OSSE grant program staff.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Minimum of three years of school-based elementary or secondary education experience and/or relevant graduate-level study.
  • Prior grant, evaluation, and/or budget experience.
  • Ability to review and score applications objectively, applying established criteria and scoring rubrics consistently.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to provide clear, constructive, objective written feedback that helps applicants strengthen program design and implementation.
  • Reliable access to a computer, the internet, and a phone.
  • Availability for the full review process, including EGMS training, the orientation webinar, the complete review window, and a facilitated discussion if one is required.
  • No conflict of interest with any applicant organization in this competition, confirmed through a signed Conflict of Interest Form.
  • No unsatisfactory performance evaluation from past grant review work for OSSE or any other grant-making organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience reviewing competitive grant applications for OSSE or another government agency.
  • Experience with educator recruitment, preparation, or professional development programs.

Compensation

  • $150 per application successfully reviewed. Reviewers are typically assigned two or more applications per competition.
  • Payment is made only after OSSE verifies successful completion of the entire review process: EGMS training, the orientation webinar, timely review and rigorous scoring of every assigned application in EGMS, and, if required, participation in a facilitated discussion with final scores submitted.
  • Payment is issued by Dhaka Technologies Limited Company by direct deposit or check within 30 calendar days of OSSE's verification.
  • Failure to complete timely, high-quality reviews will affect payment and will disqualify a reviewer from future assignments.

How to Apply

Interested candidates who meet the qualifications should send their resume to with the job title in the email subject line. Your resume should show your degree and your experience in the field. Please also mention in your resume the grants you have reviewed previously, including the grant-making organization, the grant program, and the year. Qualified applicants will be asked to complete a Grant Reviewer Application and a Conflict of Interest Form before they are recommended to OSSE.

jobs.title: Senior QA Automation Engineer (Playwright)
jobs.excerpt: Why Valtech?  We’retheexperience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands.
jobs.description:
Why Valtech? We’retheexperience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands. To our people we offer growth opportunities, a values-driven culture, international careers and the chance to shape the future of experience.

The opportunity

At Valtech, you’ll find an environment designed for continuous learning, meaningful impact, and professional growth. Whether you're pioneering new digital solutions, challenging conventional thinking or building the next generation of customer experiences, your work will help transform industries.

We are proud of:

  • The work we do and the innovation we drive
  • Our values of share, care and dare
  • A workplace culture that fosters creativity, diversity and autonomy
  • Our borderless, global framework, which enables seamless collaboration

The role

You’ll be the person a squad trusts to make test automation reliable. You design and own the Playwright framework, work closely with developers and the client, and use AI agents as a normal part of how you build and maintain tests. You also help the engineers around you get better at all of it. You work independently, plan your own work, and influence how your team and the wider QA community operate.

Role responsibilities

  • Design, build and roll out Playwright (TypeScript/JavaScript) automation frameworks, and keep them stable as suites grow
  • Test APIs and microservice-based systems alongside the UI
  • Run BDD collaboratively with analysts, developers and the client
  • Diagnose flaky and intermittent failures, and find root causes instead of adding retries
  • Use AI coding agents to speed up test design, authoring and maintenance, and rigorously verify what they produce
  • Help define how AI-assisted and agent-driven testing is done on your project, including instruction files, reusable prompts and review gates
  • Extend automation coverage into mobile as the project needs, with support
  • Coach colleagues and share what works in the QA community
  • Explain quality risk and technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Must have qualifications

  • 5+ years in test automation, including 2+ years of hands-on Playwright with TypeScript/JavaScript in production
  • Strong command of Playwright’s core model: fixtures, locator strategy, auto-waiting, network interception and mocking, trace-based debugging, parallel execution
  • Experience testing responsive and mobile-web behavior with Playwright (device emulation, viewports, touch, cross-browser)
  • Proven experience defining and implementing a framework architecture, not only extending one
  • API automation and microservices testing, with HTTP and network inspection tools
  • CI/CD experience with any major pipeline tool
  • Practical BDD experience in an Agile team
  • A working AI-assisted practice: you can show how you generate tests with AI, and how you catch tests that pass but prove nothing
  • The confidence to question and challenge from a testing perspective, and the curiosity to become a subject-matter expert quickly

Nice to have qualifications

  • Hands-on native mobile automation on iOS and/or Android, ideally Appium with WebdriverIO
  • Experience with another automation stack (Selenium-based or a non-JS framework)
  • Experience building or orchestrating multi-step AI agent workflows for test generation, execution or triage
  • Performance or cloud testing exposure
  • Mentoring, conference talks, or blogging

If you do not meet all the listed qualifications or have gaps in your experience, we still encourage you to apply. At Valtech, we recognize that talent comes in many forms, and we value diverse perspectives and a willingness to learn.

Commitment to reaching all kinds of people

We design experiences that work for all kinds of people - and that starts with our own teams. At Valtech, we’re intentional about building an inclusive culture where everyone feels supported to grow, thrive and achieve their goals. No matter your background, you belong here. Explore our Diversity & Inclusion site to see how we’re creating a more equitable Valtech for all.

The benefits

This is a position based in Portugal.

Beyond a competitive compensation package, we offer:

  • Flexibility, with remote and hybrid work options (country-dependent)
  • Career advancement, with international mobility and professional development programs
  • Learning and development, with access to cutting-edge tools, training and industry experts

Our benefits are tailored to each location. Your Talent Partner will provide full details during the hiring process.

Your application process

Once you apply, our Talent Acquisition team will review your application. Your CV should cover key information on relevant experiences and expertise. We do not require information such as age, gender, marital status, or a headshot in your application. We review all candidates based on skills, experience, and potential.

⚠️ Beware of recruitment fraud!

We are committed to inclusion and accessibility. If you need reasonable accommodations during the interview process, please either indicate it in your application or let your Talent Partner know.

About Valtech

Valtech is the experience innovation company that exists to unlock a better way to experience the world. By blending crafts, categories, and cultures, we help brands unlock new value in an increasingly digital world.

At the intersection of data, AI, creativity, and technology, we drive transformation for leading organizations, including L’Oréal, Mars, Audi, P&G, Volkswagen Dolby, and more.

At Valtech, we don’t just talk about transformation. We make it happen. Our people are the heart of our success, and we foster a workplace where everyone has the support to thrive, grow and innovate.

Are you ready to create what’s next? Join us.

Current Employees:

If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet.

The University of Miami Information Technology & Systems Department has an exciting opportunity for a full-time Systems Administrator.


The Systems Administrator maintains and administers applications to ensure optimal performance and fast recovery from emergency situations. The incumbent ensures effective provisioning, installation, configuration, operation, and maintenance of software, and related infrastructure.


Core Responsibilities:

  • Monitors system logs and activity.
  • Installs, maintains, and updates project and task tracking tools.
  • Manages account maintenance, including additions, changes, and removals.
  • Maintains integrity of accounts and data.
  • Manages security features to protect confidential information while allowing appropriate access.
  • Researches, installs, and tests software updates and patches to support applications and various platforms.
  • Researches new technologies and presents recommendations on application purchases for the enterprise.
  • Updates application inventory and documents any changes.
  • Provides training and opportunities for learning systems to all enterprise employees and consultants.
  • Develops, supports and maintains applications for all clients.
  • Provides scripting and programming support to all major projects within the enterprise.
  • Develops and maintains service level agreements with the various user departments and enterprise business units.
  • Prepares and monitors budgets for each area of functional responsibility.
  • Works closely with others within the IT function to define metrics, which are used to measure and communicate efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

Department Specific Functions:

  • Responsible for the configuration, operational administration, security, access management, availability, and vendor coordination of enterprise applications supporting Enrollment Technologies.
  • Ensures assigned systems remain secure, reliable, compliant, and aligned with University IT governance standards.
  • Serves as a technical liaison among business stakeholders, software vendors, implementation partners, information security, infrastructure, and identity management teams.
  • Coordinate Slate support, incidents, upgrades, releases, maintenance, and stakeholder communications.
  • Configure and monitor enterprise SaaS applications, including configurations, integrations, service accounts, scheduled processes, performance, availability, and issue resolution.
  • Manage user access and account lifecycles, security roles, permissions, and access reviews according to least-privilege principles; support security assessments, audits, remediation, and evidence collection.
  • Follow University change-management and Change Advisory Board requirements for deployments and post-implementation validation; maintain system, configuration, support, security, and audit documentation.
  • Support disaster recovery and business continuity planning, testing, and remediation while coordinating with business units, vendors, information security, infrastructure, and identity management.
  • Gather requirements, recommend solutions, and design, document, test, and implement Slate functionality and integrations that improve admissions processes.
  • Strong emphasis on Agile/Scrum frameworks, including creating user stories, acceptance criteria, and promoting Agile values.
  • Administer Slate operations, including workflows, forms, rules, queries, portals, dashboards, datasets, communications, integrations, accounts, security roles, and scheduled tasks.
  • Support and train users; troubleshoot system and process issues; maintain business-process documentation, training materials, and user guides.
  • Monitor data accuracy and integrity across systems, recommend improvements, and participate in the Slate community to identify best practices and enhancement opportunities.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant field
  • Slate Certification preferred
  • Minimum 3 years of experience administering SaaS applications, preferably within higher education environment; Slate implementation experience preferred.
  • Applications and Security: experience with administration, integrations, access controls, audits, change management, and recovery.
  • Systems and Data: Requirements analysis, process and data design, and third-party application management
  • Operational Management: Prioritization, resource planning, timely delivery, problem-solving, and process improvement.
  • Communication and Service: Clear documentation, stakeholder communication, client support, and technical tools.
  • Professionalism: Initiative, reliability, accountability, confidentiality, integrity, respect, and collaboration.

Any appropriate combination of relevant education, experience and/or certifications may be considered.


The University of Miami is recognized as one of the nation’s premier research institutions and academic health systems and is among the largest employers in South Florida.

With more than 20,000 faculty and staff, the University is committed to excellence and guided by a mission to positively impact the lives of students, patients, and communities locally and globally.

We are dedicated to fostering a culture where every individual feels valued and empowered to contribute meaningfully. United by shared values, the University community works together to build an environment defined by purpose, collaboration, and service.

Job Title: Director, Local Study Operations Manager

Job Location: Washington D.C., District of Columbia, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Local Study Operations Manager (LSOM), Director

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the country LSOM organization and is accountable for the quality, timeliness, cost, and compliant execution of the country clinical study portfolio. The role achieves results through LSOM Senior Managers and their FTE and FSP teams, translating global clinical development strategy into country operating priorities. The role directs portfolio delivery, resource and capacity strategy, financial planning, quality and risk management, vendor performance, and inspection readiness from feasibility through study close-out. As a member of the country leadership team, this role influences study placement and portfolio decisions, leads the resolution of significant operational issues, develops organizational capability and succession plans, and represents LSOM operations in country, regional, and global governance forums.


Accountabilities

  • Lead the successful delivery of the country study portfolio through the LSOM management organization, ensuring alignment with global clinical development priorities.
  • Provides strategic direction and leadership to LSOM country organization across the full study lifecycle, including feasibility, study execution, and study close-out.
  • Establishes portfolio-level oversight of delivery, quality, risk, timelines, and performance, directing timely escalation and resolution of critical issues for LSOM management organization.
  • Manage LSOM and LSOM vendor performance to guarantee high-quality study execution, serving as the primary escalation point for local study challenges, driving solutions, and ensuring portfolio targets are met within the country.
  • Build leadership capability within the LSOM organization through targeted coaching, development, and succession planning, preparing LSOMs to lead increasingly complex trials and programs.
  • Establishes strong operating partnerships with Clinical Research Associate (CRA) organization to support study start-up, monitoring, issue resolution, and compliant trial execution across the country portfolio.
  • Cultivate a high-performing, accountable, and inclusive organization focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement.
  • Champion strong integration between study strategy and local execution teams to translate portfolio priorities into effective country-level delivery.
  • Strengthen cross-functional alignment and accountability across country teams to accelerate execution and deliver portfolio commitments.
  • Influences study-placement and portfolio investment decisions by providing strategic insight into country's capabilities, operational readiness, performance, and growth potential.
  • Anticipates portfolio-level delivery risks, quality trends, and evolving resource requirements, directing mitigation strategies and systemic improvements across country operations.
  • Sponsor initiatives that advance operational efficiency, digital innovation, organizational capability, and the adoption of leading practices.
  • Direct resource strategy, capacity planning, and workload allocation across FSP and FTE LSOM teams to optimize execution and align resources with global priorities.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, GCP, ICH, and organizational standards across the country's study portfolio.
  • Partner with the Regional Head/Country Head and senior cross-functional stakeholders to align priorities, establish accountability for trial deliverables, and resolve significant escalations.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the functional leader for LSOM Senior Managers and the broader LSOM team, including both FSP and FTE, to optimize trial execution and align with global priorities. including strategy and execution, managing risks and escalations
  • Partners closely with CRAs, CSPO, Quality, and FSP partners.
  • Leads the coordination among country functional teams to ensure successful delivery of the country portfolio.
  • Ensure inspection readiness and provide hands-on support during inspections, including responsibility for storyboards.
  • Sponsors continuous operational improvement initiatives and encourage sharing of best practices.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and quality standards.
  • Collaborate with the Regional Head/Country Head to engage cross-functional stakeholders, align on trial deliverables, and manage escalations as needed.

Capability Building and People Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop LSOM Sr Managers, including performance management, succession planning, and leadership bench development.
  • Build the organizational capabilities, resourcing needed to meet the current and future regional portfolio requirements.
  • Foster a high-performing, inclusive, accountable, and patient-focused culture across geographically distributed teams.
  • Lead organizational changes and enable adoption of new operating models, technologies

Authority

  • Accountable for country level oversight and delivery of clinical trials.
  • Manage the performance of LSOM Senior Managers and their teams
  • Holds line management authority for regional and country operations leaders, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and capability building.
  • Sets regional delivery goals, operating expectations, and performance standards across study start-up, site engagement, monitoring, execution, and closeout.
  • Capability build, talent and performance management, and acting as a liaison for cultural differences within region.

Outputs

  • Manage LSOM resources in accordance with the global study strategy.
  • Oversee resource allocation and workload balance across LSOMs.
  • Handle FSP supplier resource coordination and monitor performance through quality oversight metrics.
  • Identify and report any risks or compliance concerns related to FSP activities.
  • Escalate issues to the Regional/Country Head as necessary.

What we expect of you


Basic Qualifications:

  • Doctorate degree and 4 years of clinical research experience OR
  • Master’s degree and 7 years of clinical research experience OR
  • Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of clinical research experience

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4 years of direct managerial and/or leadership experience or equivalent
  • Deep knowledge of ICH GCP, ICH E6(R3), ICH E8(R1), and global regulatory expectations for risk-based monitoring and clinical trial oversight.
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead complex cross-functional initiatives within a global matrix organization
  • Strong Project Management experience
  • Experience managing multiple teams / direct reports across multiple clinical functions / trials
  • Experience at, or oversight of, clinical research vendors (CROs, central labs, imaging vendors, etc.)
  • Experience managing clinical operations across relevant geography / region, including strong understanding of local regulatory requirements around global clinical trials

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

Base Salary Range: $195,876-265,008


In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts
  • A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
  • Stock-based long-term incentives
  • Award-winning time-off plans
  • Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies.

Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team.

Sponsorship

jobs.excerpt: About Reserv Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims.
jobs.description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike.

We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need adjusters who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can’t wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the role

As a Team Lead at Reserv, you will be a working leader providing support to a Claims manager with leadership and claim technical responsibilities. Leadership responsibilities will include overseeing work done within the Commercial Auto Claims adjusting staff. We want your background and experience to deliver operational effectiveness, particularly in leveraging technology and analytics to drive better efficiencies and performance. You will serve a critical role with the team, the customers, and the client. This role will balance management responsibilities and individual contributor responsibilities when volume dictates the need for assistance with a claim.

What we need

We need you to do all the things typical to the role:

  • Flexibility - you will need to be able to switch from claims handling to coaching and feedback
  • Agility- you must have an agile mindset and the ability to pivot from focus to focus in a moment’s notice
  • Be consistently dependable in achieving or exceeding goals and overcoming obstacles
  • Implement and maintain best practices for claims handling, including claim intake, investigation, evaluation, settlement, and recovery
  • Align team with client and customer expectations of the claims process
  • Serve as a resource for escalated claims
  • Foster a positive work environment, promote teamwork, and encourage professional growth and development
  • Attract, hire, retain, and provide a high level of training with the support of the rest of the leadership team
  • Prepare and present comprehensive claims reports, metrics, and analyses to clients and customers; advise clients on claim trends and loss mitigation

Job Duties:

  • Serve as backup/leader when the Manager is out of office
  • Responsible for having direct reports
  • Responsible for initial onboarding tasks / access and new hire cultural immersion
  • SME for first-line questions, escalations, roundtable discussions
  • Increased reserve and payment authority with the ability to assist with moderate reviews
  • Identify topics and trends to discuss in team Huddles and Elevated Claims Experience Workshops lead/ co-lead by Team Leads, Managers, and other Reserv employees
  • Customer Obsession Champions - Active advocates who help leadership cultivate a customer-centric mindset

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of insurance claims experience in multiple lines of business, preference for an auto with some bodily injury experience
  • 3+ years of leadership experience with a preference for experience managing in a remote environment
  • Prior team lead, supervisor, or formal mentorship/QA experience required.
  • Active adjuster license: resident-state license where available, otherwise a Designated Home State (DHS) license. Willing to obtain any additional required licenses within 60 days, including state testing.
  • Comfortable with technology and the ability to evolve the claims systems and processes to drive better efficiencies and outcomes
  • Demonstrated commitment to quality, accuracy, and attention to detail
  • Integrity, ethics, and a strong sense of accountability in handling confidential and sensitive information
  • Proven judgment on reserves, authority, and settlement strategy on high-exposure claims.
  • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent industry experience, or professional insurance designations are a plus.

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • 100% remote (home-based) role designed to support your work-life balance
  • Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder!

Additionally, we will

  • Listen to your feedback to enhance and improve upon the long-standing challenges of an adjuster and the claims role
  • Work toward reducing and eliminating all the administrative work from an adjuster role
  • Foster a culture of empathy, transparency, and empowerment in a remote-first environment

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Radar Reinvented.

Echodyne offers the world’s first compact solid-state true beam-steering radar for a wide range of industries and applications. Our high-performance radars work in all weather and are designed for autonomous vehicles, uncrewed aircraft & drones, and security of borders, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. The company combines the patented technology of metamaterials with powerful software to create a radar sensor with unprecedented performance at commercial price points. Echodyne offers its radars to companies working in Automotive, Transportation, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Border Security, Smart Cities, Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Airspace Management including Urban Air Mobility (UTM).

Echodyne is seeking a Salesforce Administrator to join our fast-growing team.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Echodyne is seeking a mid-level Salesforce Administrator to manage and improve our Salesforce environment, including Salesforce CPQ and integrations with other business systems. This role will partner with Sales Operations, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and IT to support users, improve workflows, and deliver projects that help the business scale.

The ideal candidate brings broad Salesforce knowledge, proficient Apex skills, and familiarity with Salesforce CPQ. They are collaborative and thoughtful about how changes affect other teams, data, and connected systems. They can also work independently, manage competing priorities, and carry projects from requirements through rollout.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Salesforce Administration and User Support
    • Manage day-to-day Salesforce administration, including user setup, access, roles, profiles, permission sets, and user deactivation.
    • Maintain objects, fields, page layouts, validation rules, flows, reports, and dashboards.
    • Troubleshoot user issues, resolve support requests, and identify recurring problems that need a broader solution.
    • Maintain data quality through consistent standards, duplicate management, and appropriate controls.
    • Document system configurations and processes, and provide user guidance and training.
  • Projects and System Improvements
    • Lead Salesforce projects from requirements gathering and planning through configuration, testing, deployment, and user adoption.
    • Implement and improve Account Teams and Opportunity Teams to support collaboration, account coverage, and reporting.
    • Partner with Sales Operations to improve Salesforce CPQ, including product configuration, pricing, quote workflows, and approvals.
    • Translate business needs into practical, maintainable solutions using standard Salesforce capabilities where appropriate.
    • Read, troubleshoot, and update Apex code, coordinating with developers or external partners for more complex work.
    • Manage project timelines, communicate progress, and identify dependencies and risks early.
  • Integrations and Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Support Salesforce connections with systems such as NetSuite, Marketing Cloud, and integration platforms.
    • Understand how data moves between systems and help troubleshoot synchronization issues.
    • Evaluate downstream impacts before making changes, including effects on quoting, orders, reporting, Finance, and Marketing.
    • Coordinate with internal teams and external partners to validate requirements, test changes, and support releases.
    • Maintain clear documentation of integration dependencies and data mappings.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3 years or more of hands-on Salesforce administration experience.
  • Broad knowledge of Salesforce Sales Cloud, including data management, automation, reporting, and dashboards.
  • Experience managing users, roles, profiles, permission sets, and sharing settings.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce CPQ and the quote-to-order process.
  • Proficient Apex knowledge, including the ability to read code, troubleshoot issues, and make straightforward updates.
  • Experience building and maintaining Salesforce Flow.
  • Understanding of integrations between Salesforce and other business systems, such as NetSuite or Marketing Cloud.
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to assess how changes affect other teams and processes.
  • Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and deliver projects with competing priorities.
  • Clear communication skills and a collaborative, team-oriented approach.

PREFERRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE

  • Salesforce Certified Administrator certification.
  • Experience implementing Account Teams, Opportunity Teams, or territory and account coverage structures.
