Position Title: Senior Property Accountant

Work Setup: Work from Home

Schedule: 10:00 PM - 7:00 AM

Job Location: Clark Outsourcing - Building 35 Philexcel Business Park, Clark, Pampanga

Quick Rundown:

The Senior Property Accountant is responsible for managing property-level accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis for a portfolio of real estate entities and properties. This role ensures the accuracy and completeness of financial records, supports monthly and annual financial close activities, identifies financial discrepancies, and provides management with insights into property performance. The position also supports cash flow planning, operating expense analysis, loan monitoring, and owner reporting while coordinating with internal team members and property management stakeholders.

What You’ll Do:

Property Accounting and Financial Reporting

  • Prepare monthly property-level income statements, balance sheets, and financial reporting packages.

  • Prepare preliminary financial statements and complete monthly close checklists.

  • Review general ledger transactions to identify miscoding, unusual balances, and accounting discrepancies.

  • Explain variances related to accruals, account coding, billing periods, and property operating results.

  • Prepare monthly and quarterly financial reports, rent rolls, and supporting schedules for property owners, lenders, and management.

  • Review trailing 12-month financial results to identify unusual or missing revenue and expenses.

  • Monitor property tax, insurance, utility, and other operating expenses.

Budgeting and Financial Analysis

  • Prepare monthly cash flow forecasts.

  • Compile historical financial data to support annual budgeting.

  • Prepare annual property operating budgets in coordination with relevant

  • stakeholders.

  • Forecast utilities, property taxes, insurance, repairs, and other significant operating

  • expenses.

  • Prepare actual-versus-budget reports and investigate material variances.

  • Analyze net operating income (NOI) and trailing 12-month operating performance.

  • Identify missing recurring expenses, including quarterly water bills, taxes, and insurance payments.

General Ledger and Financial Controls

  • Review general ledger activity and investigate discrepancies.

  • Ensure financial transactions are recorded accurately and supported by appropriate documentation.

  • Reconcile mortgage balances against lender statements on a quarterly basis.

  • Monitor loan maturity dates, interest rate resets, and covenant deadlines.

  • Evaluate whether qualifying expenditures should be capitalized or recorded as repair expenses.

  • Maintain accurate accounting schedules, supporting workbooks, and financial

  • Records.

Accounts Receivable and Property Income

  • Record property-related customer payments, ancillary income, reimbursements, and other charges in QuickBooks Online.

  • Process tenant credits, adjustments, concessions, and approved late-fee removals.

  • Record and review bank transactions for assigned companies and properties.

  • Prepare owner-requested workbooks covering concessions, management fees,

  • mortgage payments, utilities, and capital expenditures.

Fixed Assets and Capital Projects

  • Collect and organize invoices related to capital projects.

  • Review capital expenditures and assess appropriate accounting treatment

  • Maintain supporting documentation for property improvements and related financial transactions.

Collaboration and Process Improvement

  • Coordinate with accounting team members and property management stakeholders to resolve outstanding accounting issues.

  • Support the timely completion of monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting requirements.

  • Identify potential financial risks, reporting discrepancies, and opportunities to improve accounting processes.

  • Maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready financial records.

  • Perform other related accounting and financial analysis duties as required.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

  • At least 3 to 5 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in property management, real estate, or US-based accounting operations.

  • Strong experience in general ledger accounting, financial statement preparation, account reconciliations, and monthly close processes.

  • Experience with budgeting, cash flow forecasting, and actual-versus-budget analysis.

  • Working knowledge of property-level financial reporting, operating expenses, mortgage accounting, and capital expenditure treatment.

  • Proficiency in QuickBooks Online and Microsoft Excel, including financial reporting

  • and data analysis.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to manage recurring deadlines and work independently in a remote or outsourced accounting environment

  • Experience supporting US real estate investors, property managers, or multi-entity

  • property portfolios.

  • Familiarity with net operating income, commercial tenant recoveries, CAM reconciliations, and real estate tax reconciliations.

  • Experience preparing annual property budgets and analyzing operating performance.

  • CPA or equivalent professional certification is an advantage.

Why You’ll Love Joining the CO Fam!

At Clark Outsourcing, we’re redefining what it means to work in a BPO. This isn’t your regular office setup - it’s where careers flourish, friendships grow, and fun is always part of the deal. Our culture is unmatched (seriously, our team swears by it), and we promise you’ll have to experience it yourself to believe it.

Here’s what’s in store for you:

Health and Welfare Benefits: HMO with prescription coverage, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, 13th-month pay, retirement benefits, and more.

Beyond Work: Enjoy our in-office swimming pool (lowkey flex!), CO Club gaming lounge, CSR involvement through CO Stars, scholarship programs, and access to CO Academy for growth.

Travel Opportunities: We send at least 20 staff per year to visit our clients in the US, UK, and Australia, giving you international exposure and experience.

Leave Benefits: Paid holidays, Earned PTO on your first month, Wellness leave (no questions asked), plus special leaves like bereavement, parental leave, and Magna Carta leave.

Extra Perks: Salary loans up to PHP 1M (via BPI), CO Swag Bag, birthday and anniversary tokens, and our COol & flexible workplace.

Growth and Recognition: Yearly performance appraisals, career advancement programs, CO League events, and guidance from our amazing Coaches!

At CO, it’s not just about work - it's about loving where you work. Ready to experience the best workplace ever? We can’t wait to welcome you to the team!

jobs.description:
Job Type: Full-time | Location: Remote, US | Department: Innovation | Reporting to: Vice President, Next Generation Data Center Architecture | Work Location: #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

The Director, Facility and OT Security will own operational technology security, security compliance, supply chain assurance and physical security engineering for the IREN fleet: one standard every site is designed, built and operated to, an IEC 62443 architecture for the standard module, the facility evidence the corporate certification programs depend on, the provenance standard for procured equipment, and a small group of specialists to build. IREN's facilities are industrial control systems hosting other people's most valuable computation, and the corporate security function covers enterprise information technology only. The position sits in the Next Generation Data Center Architecture function with an indirect line to the Chief Information Officer so that its authority reaches the fleet.

Responsibilities

  • Write and maintain the fleet operational technology and facility security standard and apply it to new sites through the design basis and to existing sites by assessment.
  • Own the IEC 62443 architecture of the standard module and its application to each site: zones, conduits, security level targets, component requirements and secure remote access.
  • Own the facility security compliance requirements and evidence package for the federal, defense and critical infrastructure regimes IREN's customers and jurisdictions impose.
  • Own the provenance and software bill of materials standard for the module's equipment and the exception process.
  • Own the physical security design basis for the standard module and the fleet.
  • Hold security criteria at the Architecture Review Gate and the security validation at Childress before each energized campaign.
  • Write the operations security logging, response and safe degradation requirements for Operations and the telemetry platform.
  • Hold the written boundary with corporate security and brief the Chief Information Officer monthly; hire, develop and lead the group.

Other important requirements
  • Pre-employment screening, including background check and substance testing may be required according to company policies.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or a related field; a master's degree is preferred. Equivalent professional experience is considered.
  • Fifteen or more years in security engineering with at least eight in operational technology or industrial control system security for utilities, energy, pipelines, process industry or critical facilities, including leadership of a security program across multiple sites.
  • Leadership of an operational technology or facility security program across more than one site, where you set the standard, assessed sites against it and owned the findings with operations leaders who did not report to you.
  • Operational technology security architecture depth sufficient to direct an architect's IEC 62443 work and read a supplier's evidence critically.
  • Direct experience with at least one federal, defense or critical infrastructure security regime from the facility side, including the assessment.
  • Supply chain and provenance assurance for procured equipment under country-of-origin or restricted-source rules; management of security engineers; budget ownership for assessments and external specialists.
  • Preferred: ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert, CISSP, GICSP, Physical Security Professional; working knowledge of NIST SP 800-82, NERC CIP, NIST SP 800-171, FedRAMP and DoD impact levels, and the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act; NERC CIP program leadership.

Benefits

At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth.

Compensation
  • Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications.

About Wander

Wander is a technology and hospitality company building a better way to discover, book, and operate premium vacation rentals. Our business includes a curated consumer marketplace, a white-glove property management service, and WanderOS, our software platform for short-term-rental and hospitality operators.

Wander combines high-quality vacation homes, a strong guest experience, and technology that helps property managers grow their businesses. The marketplace brings travelers and premium inventory together, while WanderOS gives operators the tools to build their own direct-booking channel, strengthen their brand, and grow beyond traditional online travel agencies.

About WanderOS

WanderOS is an all-in-one direct-booking platform for short-term-rental and hospitality property managers. It connects to a property manager’s existing PMS and transforms their listings, photos, pricing, and availability into a branded, conversion-focused website and booking experience.

The platform combines PMS integrations, direct booking and checkout, integrated payments, analytics, automated guest marketing, promotional tools, SEO for Google and AI search platforms, and AI-powered distribution. WanderOS helps operators increase direct bookings, build repeat guest relationships, attract new homeowners, and reduce their dependence on OTAs without replacing their existing property management system.

This role will help grow the paid marketing engine supporting Wander and WanderOS as we make it easier for property managers to compete with larger hospitality brands and grow their businesses.

About the role

We’re hiring a data-driven, hands-on Performance Marketing Manager to work closely with our Director of Performance Marketing to assist with planning, launching, and optimizing customer acquisition across paid channels.

This is a hands-on, in-platform role. You’ll be in Ads Manager every day building campaigns, reading the data, and helping to iterate on the next round of creative. You’ll work across Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, and emerging AI-surface channels like OpenAI Ads, marketing individual properties and portfolios to travelers who care about design, privacy, and the quality of the stay.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable building channel strategy, analyzing performance data, testing creative, and most importantly getting into the technical details of execution.

One thing to know up front: we use AI strategically here at Wander. Claude and similar tools are part of how this team works every day — analyzing performance data, drafting and iterating creative, auditing tracking, building reporting, and moving faster than a team our size otherwise could. We’re looking for someone who already works this way, or is genuinely excited to.

What you'll own

Campaign strategy and execution

  • Launch and manage full-funnel paid campaigns primarily across Meta and Google, while also being comfortable managing additional channels like LinkedIn ads, TikTok ads, and OpenAI Ads
  • Assist with developing channel strategies aligned to acquisition, revenue, and efficiency goals
  • Be comfortable owning campaign structure, targeting, audience testing, bidding, budgets, and creative.
  • Oversee budget pacing and allocation across channels and properties
  • Run both acquisition and retargeting programs, and know which lever the funnel actually needs

Creative strategy

  • Brief, concept, and iterate on ad creative — static, video, and UGC — for properties where the imagery is the product
  • Partner with in-house creative team to keep a steady flow of new assets in market, and identify creative fatigue before performance drops
  • Support on writing ad copy when needed

Feeds and catalogs

  • Build and maintain property catalogs and feeds powering dynamic and travel-format ads
  • Hands-on experience setting up Meta catalog ads and building product sets in Ads Manager — you've done this yourself, not just briefed someone else to
  • Work with direct-booking sites as the primary conversion destination

Analysis and reporting

  • Report monthly on the metrics that matter: ROAS, CPA, CTR, CPC, CVR - alongside the booking metrics specific to our business: cost per booking and booking value
  • Be able to pull reports and analyze top performing creatives on a monthly basis to inform the creative team on what’s working.

Systems and process

ABOUT DESCARTES UNDERWRITING

Join Descartes and contribute to our mission: Building Resilience in a World at Risk.

Descartes is a corporate insurance group for worldwide companies and institutions. Descartes was born from a conviction that the growing complexity of corporate and climate risks demands a new approach to insurance. At the forefront of AI and Data analysis, Descartes utilises cutting-edge technology combined with a new generation of data sources, to model, assess and manage risks.

Since 2019, Descartes has secured a leading position in parametric (re)insurance combining scientific & technological expertise with a new approach. Parametric insurance, also known as index-based insurance, indemnifies clients within days based on pre-defined payout structures when a specific triggering event occurs, the payout process is both fast and transparent. The company has been financed with over $141M by investors including Highland Europe, BlackFin, Serena, Cathay, Eurazeo and Battery Ventures.

Our highly diverse and specialized team of 250+ people includes the largest modelling team in the industry featuring tech and modeling innovators, scientists in physics and climatology, as well as insurance veterans and underwriters. With a global footprint and strong US presence, Descartes serves a diverse portfolio of clients in more than 60 countries, with 20+ offices spread across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin and North America.

Find out more on.

Descartes is hiring a Business Development Executive - Reinsurance (AVP or VP depending on experience) to grow our reinsurance and retrocession business in the Americas. Reporting to the SVP, Business Development – Reinsurance & Retrocession, you will originate and close new reinsurance business, deepen relationships with reinsurance brokers and cedents, and position Descartes’ parametric solutions as a strategic tool in their risk transfer programs.

This role calls for an experienced reinsurance professional with an entrepreneurial, builder’s mindset — someone who combines strong market credibility and technical understanding of reinsurance structures and Nat Cat risk with the energy to build a pipeline and win business in a fast-growing company.

  • Personally lead deals through the full sales cycle, from prospecting and submission to negotiation and binding.

4. Market Intelligence and Collaboration

  • Understanding of Nat Cat perils and catastrophe modelling concepts.

Preferred but not compulsory

Acting as the primary revenue Cycle liaison between designated between designated department(s), the Professional Billing office, third-party vendors, and all other stakeholders, to proactively identify opportunities to improve the revenue cycle and assist in the resolution of issues. Professional revenue cycle expertise and strong communication skills are required.

Position: Revenue Cycle Billing Liaison Manager – PB

Department: Professional Billing

Schedule: Full Time

jobs.excerpt: Job Title: Head of Customer Success Salary: Up to £60,000 About IMPAt IMP we help Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) take control of their finances.
jobs.description:
Job Title: Head of Customer Success

Salary: Up to £60,000

About IMP

At IMP we help Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) take control of their finances. Our MAT-first software is built by people who know the sector inside out. Former trust professionals, finance experts and product specialists are all part of our team. More than half of all MATs in the UK already use IMP to plan with confidence, simplify complex processes and make smarter decisions.

We’re proud to be independent, founder-led and growing fast. Alongside our award-winning products, we’ve built a culture we’re equally proud of. We are ranked as one of the UK’s Top 25 Great Places to Work for mid-sized companies. Respect, collaboration and personal growth sit at the heart of how we work. You’ll find flexibility, support and opportunities to develop here, alongside regular team socials and funded CPD.

Role Description:

The Head of Customer Success leads the team that makes sure our customers get the value they bought. Once a trust is live on an IMP product, your team is the one thinking about them: whether they are using what they have, whether they are getting results from it, what they will need next, and what might get in the way.

The job in one line: make sure our customers have what they need before they have to ask for it.

As IMP scales, Customer Success becomes its own department with its own Head, separate from Support. This role shapes how it works: what the team does, how it works with Account Management, Support, Implementations and our R&D team, and what good looks like for our customers. You will not inherit a fully formed process. You will take what exists today and build it into one that works as we grow.

You work closely with R&D to know what is coming for each product and what customers will need from it, and you decide what customers should hear, learn and do ahead of a launch, then make it happen. You build the retention plan with the Head of Account Management. This is not a commercial role: renewal and expansion sit with Account Management, and you own the customer health and adoption work behind them.

This is a leadership role. You are accountable for customer outcomes and for the team, and you report to the Chief Customer Officer.

What the role is accountable for:

  • Successful customers: every live customer getting the value they bought, with the Customer Success team in front of the ones who need it before they have to ask.

  • The health of every live customer: a current read across the whole customer base, so the trusts that need attention are found early and acted on before they tell us.

  • Adoption: customers using what they have bought, with depth measured and worked on, not assumed.

  • Escalations prevented: problems headed off by a named intervention, not just escalations handled well.

  • The go-live handover: the named receiver of each customer handed over from Implementations, with the right to accept it or send it back.

  • The retention plan, built jointly with the Head of Account Management: Customer Success owns the health and adoption actions in it; Account Management owns the commercial outcome.

  • Customers knowing what is coming: a customer-facing view of each product's direction, kept current with R&D, and a regular rhythm of sessions that keeps live customers engaged and informed.

  • Customers staying successful through every product launch: what they need to hear, learn and do, planned and delivered before the launch lands on them.

  • A well-led team: clear portfolios, clear priorities, every person managed and developed.

Key responsibilities:

  • Have a view of every live customer: what they bought, how they are using it, who at IMP they deal with, and where they are heading.

  • Build and run the customer health framework using the data the business already holds: usage, support contact, engagement, renewal timing. Keep the read current across the whole customer base and act on what it shows.

  • Set priorities across the Customer Success team's portfolios and move effort to the customers who need it.

  • Receive every go-live handover from Implementations: agree the criteria, accept the customer or send the handover back with what is missing.

  • Build and run the retention plan with the Head of Account Management, and design how the two teams work together: who contacts which customer, when, and about what.

  • Give early warning to Support when a customer pattern shows a product or knowledge problem, and to Account Management when it shows a commercial one.

  • Work directly with R&D to understand what is coming for each product, and turn it into something customers can plan around.

  • Decide, for each launch and release, what customers need before it reaches them, and get the right people in to deliver it, from Customer Success, Support, Implementations or R&D.

  • Run a regular customer-facing rhythm of sessions on product direction and adoption, and own their content and attendance.

  • Give Support the customer demand signal ahead of a launch: what customers will ask, when, and in what volume.

  • Lead, manage and develop the Customer Success team: portfolios, objectives, one-to-ones, development plans.

  • Report monthly to the Chief Customer Officer on customer risk, health, adoption and launches supported, and feed the senior leadership team's view of customer risk.

  • Work through tooling rather than by hand: our CRM, our work management tools and AI, so the health picture stays current and the admin stays out of the job.

Skills, experience, and attributes:

  • You are customer obsessed. You have either led a customer success team in a B2B software business, or you have been an outstanding customer success lead and are ready and hungry to lead a team. Either way, you can show what changed for customers because you were there.

  • You think ahead of the customer. You can show where you spotted what customers would need, built it, and delivered it before they asked.

  • You are comfortable in a non-commercial seat: you can work alongside a commercial team, build a shared plan with them, and not need to own the number to care about it.

  • You have run customer-facing sessions at scale, such as webinars, user groups or product briefings, and you know what makes people turn up and come back.

  • You can hold a picture across a whole customer base, spot the ones drifting before they tell you, and act early.

  • You can build a process with a peer, agree the boundaries, and hold both teams to them.

  • You have worked closely enough with a product team to translate a roadmap into what it means for a customer, and to carry the customer's voice back without losing it.

  • You work through tooling and AI by default; a CRM such as HubSpot is an advantage, and appetite matters more than the track record.

  • You can lead a small team: set direction, give honest feedback, develop people.

  • Experience in education, MAT finance or a comparably regulated sector is welcome, but not essential.

Benefits:

  • 27 days of holiday per year plus bank holidays (with a buy option up to an additional 5 days)

  • Enhance Maternity and Paternity leave

  • AXA Health insurance including dental, optical and mental health

  • Broadband allowance

  • Home office stipend

  • Life assurance (4 x basic salary)

  • Encouraged and funded CPD

jobs.description:
CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. At CCC, we’re making life just work by empowering more than 35,000 businesses with industry-leading technology to get drivers back on the road and to health quickly and seamlessly. We’re pushing boundaries with innovative AI solutions that simplify and enhance the claims and repair journey. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at .

The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer you will own LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows for our customers. These systems automate the routine parts of a claim and guide customers on the rest, so they have to earn that trust with a measured accuracy you can defend as models change and usage grows. Agents run as steps inside deterministic workflows, and privacy and security are design baselines, not review gates. Agentic coding tools are how you move fast. What you add is what they are worst at: system architecture, code quality, security, and the debugging nobody else gets to the bottom of. You own a product area end to end and define the eval bar it ships against.

Salary range is:

$180,000 - 225,000

This position is bonus eligible.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the delivery of LLM-powered systems in Python and TypeScript, from an ambiguous customer problem, scoped with product managers and data scientists, through production operation.
  • Set the evals and guardrails strategy for your area: what gates a release, what production signals the team watches, and how a change is simulated against historical claims before it ships.
  • Raise the bar for how the team works with agentic coding tools: sharpen the specifications, instruction files, hooks, and permission policies they run under, and hold generated code to the same review standard before it merges.
  • Design the NLP pipelines that turn unstructured claim data into structured data customers can act on, choosing where semantic search, classical NLP, or an LLM fits.
  • Build and operate durable, event-driven, multi-tenant systems in which agents run as steps inside deterministic workflows, designing their failure modes, replay semantics, and cost profile before they show up under load.
  • Own tracing and audit for your area: every model call and agent step recorded, so any recommendation can be reconstructed and cited back to its sources by on-call and auditors alike.
  • Set the privacy and security baseline every system in your area starts from: tenant isolation, least-privilege access for agents and their tools, redaction, retention, and what data may reach a model provider.
  • Author the design documents for complex systems to get feedback and buy-in, review other engineers' designs and code with the same care, and mentor the engineers in your area.
  • Take part in a shared on-call rotation for the systems you own.

Requirements:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including an LLM-powered system you architected, shipped to external customers, and carried through at least one model or prompt migration.
  • Python and TypeScript at the level of setting a team's conventions: the async model, typing strictness, and test strategy for a shared codebase, plus a performance problem you profiled and fixed.
  • An evals and guardrails strategy you set for a product area others built in: where human approval was required, and how production corrections re-entered the evals.
  • A clear account of how you constrain an agentic coding tool's context and verify its output, from daily use of Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar on production work, plus changes you turned back, and why.
  • Pipelines you designed that blend LLMs, semantic search, and classical NLP, including a retrieval design you can defend and a case where a classical technique beat an LLM on cost, latency, or reliability.
  • Durable, event-driven systems you designed with deterministic orchestration around non-deterministic model steps: compensating actions, idempotency, backpressure, and event-sourced replay.
  • Data modeling and development across relational, document, and graph databases such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Neo4j, including when each type fits and the partition-key, consistency, and tenant-isolation calls you made.
  • Systems architected and operated on Azure or AWS, with CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and hands-on time with a durable workflow engine such as Temporal or the Durable Task Scheduler.
  • Technical design documents you have authored for systems that span more than one team, used to get feedback and buy-in before building, and that those teams then built to.
  • Clear writing and discussion for technical and non-technical audiences: drawing out a customer's real problem and explaining the trade-offs back to them.

Even Better if You Have:

  • React and TypeScript experience, so you can deliver a full-stack feature end to end, especially chat, streaming, and citation-heavy AI experiences.
  • Experience with agent frameworks, LangGraph, PydanticAI, and the Microsoft Agent Framework among them, and with the ways agents reach their tools: the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, command-line tools, and microservices.
  • Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tooling such as LangSmith, Arize, or Braintrust, and with OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
  • Experience designing A/B tests for AI features.
  • Exposure to the insurance, claims, or automotive repair domains.

What Success Looks Like:

  • In your first six months, every model change in your area is gated by evals you designed, regressions are caught before a customer sees them, and you can show the accuracy number held or moved.
  • You are trusted with the high-stakes, ambiguous problems, and you turn them into a roadmap, a shipped system, and a number you can put in front of a customer.
  • You are energized by what agentic coding tools make possible. Your team ships more than its headcount suggests, and your specifications and reviews are why the output survives production.
  • You have a passion for systems that last: the ones you design have their failure modes understood in advance, and when one fails anyway, the trace says exactly where.
  • Privacy and security reviews of systems in your area find nothing that was not already designed in.
  • Standards you set for evals, reviews, and design documents outlive the project they started on.
  • Engineers you mentor ship LLM-powered features with evals and guardrails in place without your direct involvement.
  • You enjoy getting a product manager, a data scientist, and a customer's team into one room and coming out with a single agreed scope, and you can argue a position without needing to win it.
  • You embrace our ambitious, collaborative, and empathetic values, and you like problems where the answer has to be measured rather than argued.

Interview Policy & Privacy Notice:

A video interview is required for this position. Video interviews are transcribed. Transcriptions are retained and may be reviewed by CCC and our recruiters. Candidates are not permitted to use generative AI or automated assistance during the interviews unless explicitly allowed by the interview team for a specific exercise. Through diverse perspectives, purposeful innovation, and the strength of connections, our technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most.

locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Our client builds an all-in-one booking and park-management platform for outdoor hospitality. Campground, RV park, and glamping operators use it to manage reservations, availability, rates, payments, guest messaging, and reporting in one place. It also runs a traveler-facing marketplace that brings operators more bookings.

Many customers are small and mid-sized businesses whose busiest days depend on the software running smoothly. They choose this platform for its ease of use and for the real, hands-on support behind it.

Your Role

As a Sales Assistant Representative on the demo pipeline, you're the first contact for park owners who ask for a demo. You reply to each request, call the owner, and book the demo. A park owner who asks for a demo is usually comparing software, and a slow reply gets passed over quickly.

This is a junior, full time role, fully remote from Latin America on U.S. business hours. You report to the company owner and sales leadership in Texas, and the sales team there runs the demos.

Success means replying to new requests within minutes, booking demos with confirmations and reminders sent, and handing the sales team clear notes, the right time zone and a confirmed attendee.

You'll

  • Reply to demo requests from campground and RV park owners within minutes

  • Call owners to confirm interest and ask about fit and urgency

  • Offer demo times that suit the owner's time zone and the sales team

  • Send a confirmation and a reminder for every booked demo

  • Write CRM notes after each call with what was said and the next date

  • Follow up with quiet leads until they book or decline

  • Hand booked demos to the sales team with notes and a confirmed attendee

  • Report objections and lead quality patterns to sales leadership, with examples

You Bring

  • Regular live phone calls in English with customers or leads, such as support or reservations

  • Your own follow-up list, with a next contact date and second or third calls

  • Notes kept in a CRM, ticketing tool or tracker that other people used

  • Clear spoken and written English, including calls with U.S. business owners at normal speed

  • Experience booking and confirming appointments across time zones

  • Good judgement about when a lead or a handoff looks wrong, and telling the team early

  • Full time availability on U.S. business hours, working remotely from Latin America

Bonus Points

  • HubSpot or Salesforce used day to day

  • Outbound calling or appointment setting against a daily call target

  • Taking bookings by phone in hotels, resorts, tours or travel

  • Having sat in on or run a software demo

What's Offered

  • What we'd estimate for a role like this: $1,000 to $2,000 USD a month, based on experience. Share the range that fits your level and we'll go from there.

Interview Process

1️⃣ First call: 30 minutes with us at atomic✳HR on what you have built, working terms and what you want next.
2️⃣ First interview: a conversation with our client on the work itself: how you reply to a new demo request, how you talk with a park owner on the phone, and how you write up a call so someone else can act on it. It can include a short role-play call to a busy campground owner, a written confirmation and follow-up, and a scheduling exercise across U.S. time zones. Each one is explained before you do it, and each is read for clarity, speed and clean notes.
3️⃣ Second interview: a further conversation with our client on how you would work with the sales team, hand over a booked demo, and report back on objections and lead quality.
4️⃣ Offer: rate, start date and schedule, in writing.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Medical Director - Oncology , Sponsor Dedicated (12 Months Fixed Term Contract)

Job Location: Reading, Berkshire, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Overview

The medical department consists of a Chief Medical Officer, Medical Directors, Sr Medical Directors, Medical Writers, and Safety Associates. The Medical Director provides medical and scientific support to clinical research programs, study teams and investigators. The Medical Director also provides review, advice, and leadership for potentially or awarded clinical research programs.

The Medical Director role is a team member participant role and functions in a matrix report to project teams much like other members of the project teams. The primary role of Medical Director is to provide medical oversight for clinical trials by serving as Medical Monitor for studies conducted by IQVIA Biotech Clinical on behalf of sponsor companies. The principal function of a Medical Monitor is to serve as primary contact for the sponsor medical team and to serve as front line medical resource to support the project team. The Medical Monitor is customarily available 24/7 to answer questions from site coordinators and investigators on protocol inclusion/exclusion criteria, protocol clarifications, and compliance issues, and to provide review of alert labs per sponsor preference. Major duties of the Medical Director are outlined below:

Essential Functions

Functions as project team member:

  • Provides medical and scientific input to clinical research programs including review of new business proposals, preclinical and/or clinical data, study protocols, training materials, informed consent, Investigator Drug Brochures, eCRFs, analysis plan designs, clinical study reports, regulatory approval submissions, serious and non-serious adverse event evaluation, and reporting.
  • Ensures medical activities run according to GCP and operate with highest efficiency.
  • Establishes and maintains a network of medical/scientific consultants, etc.
  • Supervises and manages Medical Director activities.

Clinical Activities:

  • Interacts with clients regarding drug development programs, study design and protocol.
  • Reviews and provides input for protocol development. Interacts with key thought leaders and/or sponsor representatives to develop inclusion/exclusion criteria and study endpoints.
  • Interacts in team approach to develop statistical and data management sections of the protocol.
  • Reviews the final protocol for clinical, safety and efficacy variables.
  • Provides project team training on protocol and/or therapeutic areas.
  • Assists team with developing criteria for investigator site selection and networking for potential investigators for study participation. Aids in review and final selection.
  • Participates in subject recruitment and retention activities including individual calls to key opinion leaders, investigators, and site staff and/or participation in teleconference and WebEx presentations.
  • Presents protocol and/or safety reporting information at investigator meetings.
  • Develops project medical monitoring plans as requested.
  • Provides on call coverage for protocol queries and site support.
  • Provides first line contact for investigators and monitors regarding study related medical/safety issues and resolution of study protocol and patient eligibility issues.

Safety Monitoring and SAE Reporting Activities:

  • Verifies the medical accuracy of patient safety data and maintains an ongoing assessment of the safety profile of the study.
  • Provides medical review of SAE reporting, writes and/or reviews SAE narratives, and works with the Safety Management Department to track SAEs and follow-up on outstanding safety queries, interacts with sponsor and discusses safety issues with site as needed.
  • Reviews IND/SUSAR Safety Reports (per sponsor preference), updates to Investigator Brochures, and annual IND reports with sponsor data.
  • In consultation with the sponsor, follow procedures for acquiring knowledge of subject treatment assignments (i.e. breaking the blind).
  • Interact with appropriate FDA officials concerning safety and other study related issues, as requested.

Data Activities:

  • Provides medical review of eCRFs for clinical accuracy.
  • Provides medical review of data analysis plan.
  • Reviews safety fields at case freeze for reconciliation (if needed).
  • Works with data group to reconcile SAE events as needed.
  • Reviews medical coding of adverse events, laboratory data and concomitant medications for accuracy, coherence, consistency, and trends.
  • Reviews data tables, listings, and figures.
  • Reviews and/or writes portions of final clinical study report.

DSMB/Adjudication Committee Activities:

  • May assist sponsor in choosing committee members.
  • May serve as a non-voting member to convene and organize proceedings.
  • May develop operating guidelines in conjunction with committee members and submits these to sponsor for review.
  • May determine data flow with sponsor to ensure reporting accuracy.
  • Can ensure DSMB feedback is given to sites for IRBs.
  • All DSMB activities are usually managed by the IQVIA Biotech Oversight Management Group and not the IQVIA Biotech medical monitor.

Business Development Activities:

  • Work with Business Development to actively solicit new business for Novella Clinical, including assistance with marketing presentations and proposal development.
  • Supports business development activities with proposal development and sales presentations.
  • Participates in feasibility discussions relating to specific project proposals.

Special Projects:

  • Obtain literature searches to acquire background information for study proposals, preparation of training sessions, and interpretation of clinical data, report writing, etc.
  • Assists with drafting of standard operating procedures and working practices regarding all Medical Director activities.
  • Participate in a variety of team quality improvement efforts as necessary.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned or requested by the Chief Medical Officer.

Qualifications

  • Medical Degree from an accredited and internationally recognized medical school with a curriculum relevant to general medical education.

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since 2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably.

Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

About the role:

We are hiring for a dedicated Google Acquisition function to drive scalable customer growth across both our personal and business banking products. This Senior Manager will own the end-to-end Google performance channel — from campaign architecture and technical infrastructure to economic modelling and channel governance.

This is not an execution role dressed up as a leadership role. We need someone who thinks in systems, works from first principles, and has the depth to make credible judgements on strategy, technology, and economics simultaneously.

Responsibilities

  • Campaign Architecture & Execution
    • Design and own the full Google channel strategy across UAC / App Campaigns, Performance Max, and Search for both personal and business banking acquisition
    • Build and maintain campaign structures optimised for Moniepoint's dual-product funnel — separating signals, audiences, and bidding logic appropriately across segments
    • Set bidding strategies, budget allocation frameworks, and creative testing cycles that reduce dependence on any single signal or format
    • Own campaign performance end-to-end: from brief to launch to optimisation to reporting
  • Tracking, Attribution & Technical Infrastructure
    • Architect and own the full measurement stack: Firebase / GA4 event taxonomy, Google Tag Manager configuration, and server-side event pipelines
    • Lead the implementation and ongoing integrity of Conversion APIs and enhanced conversions to maximise signal quality sent back to Google
    • Define the attribution model — evaluate last-click, data-driven, and custom models against Moniepoint's funnel reality, and own the decision with clear reasoning
    • Partner with engineering and data teams to ensure event data flowing to Google is accurate, complete, and timely — treating signal quality as a competitive asset
    • Build audit protocols for tracking coverage and attribution consistency; surface gaps before they distort decisions
  • LTV/CAC Economics
    • Own the economic model for Google acquisition: define CAC targets by product, segment, and channel variant; set the inputs, assumptions, and review cadence
    • Understand the LTV/CAC relationship at a structural level — not just as a ratio to optimise, but as a function of product retention, monetisation curves, and cohort behaviour
    • Build and iterate on payback period models that account for Moniepoint's emerging market context: irregular income patterns, higher churn risk, and longer monetisation timelines
    • Design bidding and budget logic that reflects true LTV signals rather than proxy metrics, working closely with data science to enrich Google's Smart Bidding with offline conversion data
    • Proactively identify when CAC is drifting against LTV thresholds and lead the diagnosis — channel mix, audience quality, creative fatigue, product-market fit — before it becomes a financial problem
  • Governance & Reporting
    • Build a channel reporting system that surfaces reality clearly — not dashboards that flatter performance, but views that drive better decisions
    • Establish review cadences with clear owners, metrics, and follow-through mechanisms
    • Translate channel performance into business language for senior stakeholders: what is the cost of growth, is it sustainable, and what would change the trajectory
  • Emerging Market & Fintech Context
    • Adapt Google acquisition strategy for the realities of emerging market users: variable device penetration, low-bandwidth environments, trust barriers to financial services, and diverse
    • language/literacy contexts
    • Navigate platform constraints specific to fintech advertising on Google: financial services policies, verification requirements, and creative compliance
    • Bring genuine insight into what acquisition patterns distinguish sustainable fintech growth from subsidised growth in markets like Nigeria

To succeed in this role, you should have:

  • 6+ years of hands-on paid acquisition experience, with the majority of that time spent on Google UAC / App Campaigns at meaningful scale
  • Deep, demonstrable technical knowledge of Google's campaign infrastructure: bidding algorithms, audience signals, creative specs, and the mechanics of Smart Bidding
  • Proven ability to architect and own the full measurement stack — Firebase, GA4, GTM, Conversion APIs — not just configure it but understand why each component matters
  • Fluency in LTV/CAC modelling: you have built the models, owned the assumptions, and used them to make real budgeting and bidding decisions
  • Experience operating in a fintech or financial services context, with direct knowledge of the acquisition compliance and trust dynamics unique to financial products
  • Strongly Preferred
  • Experience managing budgets larger that 10 Million USD annually
  • Experience running Google acquisition in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable emerging markets — Nigeria specifically is a significant advantage
  • Familiarity with server-side conversion APIs, offline conversion imports, and enhanced conversions as mechanisms for improving signal quality in cookieless or app-first environments
  • Experience working with data science or analytics teams to build custom bidding signals and offline LTV imports into Google's systems
  • Prior work on dual-product or dual-segment acquisition (e.g., consumer and SME / business) with separate funnel logic

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days

  • Full audit of existing Google campaign structure, tracking integrity, and attribution model completed — with a written assessment and prioritised improvement plan
  • Measurement stack gaps identified and remediation underway with engineering
  • LTV/CAC baseline model built with documented assumptions, reviewed with Growth and Finance
  • First governance cadence established — weekly performance review with clear owner, metrics, and follow-through log

In the first year

  • Google channel operating as a reliable, scalable growth engine with predictable CAC across both personal and business banking segments
  • Signal quality measurably improved — higher match rates, cleaner conversion data, reduced reliance on last-click proxies
  • Attribution model validated against actual cohort data and actively used in budget allocation decisions
  • Playbook documented: campaign architecture, bidding logic, audience strategy, and economic model all institutionalised — not living in one person's head
  • A team (or foundations for one) built with clear ownership, development paths, and no single point of failure

What to expect in the hiring process

  • A preliminary phone call with the recruiter
  • A technical interview with the hiring manager
  • A Case Study
  • A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team
  • All interview stages are virtual

jobs.excerpt: The Relationship Manager (RM) serves as the primary point of contact for high-net-worth (HNW) and ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) private risk management clients.
jobs.description:
The Relationship Manager (RM) serves as the primary point of contact for high-net-worth (HNW) and ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) private risk management clients. The RM is responsible for delivering elite, personalized client service, providing technical expertise in personal lines insurance, and proactively managing complex risk exposures across a sophisticated book of business. This role operates at the intersection of client advocacy, carrier relationship management, and strategic risk consulting — and is critical to driving retention, satisfaction, and growth within the Private Risk Management (PRM) practice.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Client Service & Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for an assigned book of HNW/UHNW clients, delivering proactive, white-glove service across all touchpoints — phone, email, and in-person.
  • Anticipate client needs and surface coverage recommendations, risk alerts, and market changes before clients ask.
  • Conduct annual interactive client reviews, presenting renewal proposals and agendas that reflect a deep understanding of each client's exposures and lifestyle.
  • Build trusted advisor relationships that drive long-term retention and organic growth through referrals.

Risk Analysis & Coverage Consulting

  • Review client exposures, underwriting memos, loss experience, and current coverages to identify gaps and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Advise and counsel clients on complex risk exposures including high-value homes, fine art and collectibles, watercraft, aircraft, excess liability/umbrella, and specialty lines.
  • Review inspection reports for coverage accuracy and potential loss prevention issues; provide proactive direction to resolve outstanding items and minimize E&O exposure.
  • Remain current on industry offerings, carrier appetite changes, and HNW market trends — making proactive recommendations to clients and leadership.
  • Understand and introduce the holistic Baldwin platform as appropriate, including employee benefits, commercial lines, and asset protection services.

Market Placement & Carrier Relations

  • Act as a market placement specialist, remarketing existing programs as needed to ensure competitive positioning and alignment with client needs.
  • Cultivate strong relationships with carrier partners including PURE, Chubb, AIG Private Client, Cincinnati, Berkley One and specialty markets.
  • Maintain thorough knowledge of insurer contracts, underwriting guidelines, proprietary systems, and appetite to optimize placement decisions.
  • Collaborate with carrier representatives to advocate for favorable outcomes on complex risks, renewals, and claims.

Operational Excellence & Compliance

  • Maintain accuracy, timeliness, and completeness in all client and carrier interactions to minimize errors and omissions exposure.
  • Ensure all policy activity — new business, renewals, endorsements, cancellations — is documented accurately in agency management systems (Epic preferred).
  • Adhere to Baldwin's established workflows, service standards, and compliance requirements across all client interactions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, workflows, and the overall client experience; surface recommendations to leadership.
  • Manage a high-volume workload with strong organizational discipline and attention to detail.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

Required Qualifications

  • Active Property & Casualty insurance license in the state(s) where business is conducted, or the ability to obtain all required licenses within 90 days of hire.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in personal lines insurance, with demonstrated knowledge of HNW carrier contracts, underwriting guidelines, and claims processes.
  • Proven ability to manage complex client relationships with a high degree of professionalism, responsiveness, and discretion.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to sophisticated clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and agency management systems; experience with Epic highly preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Risk Management, Finance, or a related field preferred.
  • Professional designations strongly preferred: CPRIA (Chartered Private Risk and Insurance Advisor), CPCU, CAPI, CPRM, CIC, or equivalent.
  • Prior experience working with UHNW clients, family offices, or within a dedicated private client/PRM practice.
  • Familiarity with specialty lines including fine art, jewelry, watercraft, aviation, and excess/umbrella liability.

CORE COMPETENCIES

What We Look For

  • Client Obsession — You treat every client interaction as an opportunity to exceed expectations and build loyalty.
  • Technical Depth — You bring genuine expertise in HNW personal lines and can translate complex coverage concepts into clear client guidance.
  • Ownership Mentality — You manage your book like a business — tracking details, anticipating renewals, and driving outcomes without waiting to be asked.
  • Collaborative Spirit — You partner effectively with, advisors, insurers, and leadership to deliver seamless client experiences.
  • Continuous Improvement — You actively look for ways to sharpen your skills, improve processes, and contribute to the growth of the PRM practice.

ABOUT THE BALDWIN GROUP

Why Baldwin PRM

The Baldwin Group (NASDAQ: BWIN) is a leading insurance brokerage and risk management firm committed to delivering innovative solutions for individuals, families, and businesses. Our Private Risk Management practice serves high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients with a concierge-level approach to personal risk — backed by deep carrier relationships, market expertise, and a team that genuinely cares about client outcomes.


Baldwin offers a collaborative, growth-oriented environment where colleagues are empowered to build meaningful careers while making a real impact for the clients they serve.

Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at .

Role Summary

Incident Response Consultants play a key role in supporting customers through cybersecurity incidents by coordinating the response between the customer, DFIR consultants, and other technical teams.

This is a customer-facing role focused on incident coordination, communication, and ensuring that response activities progress effectively from initial engagement through to resolution. You will work closely with DFIR consultants who conduct the technical investigation, while helping customers understand what is happening, what information or actions are required, and what the next steps are.

You do not need to be a digital forensics specialist. However, you will need a strong understanding of enterprise technology and cybersecurity concepts, combined with excellent communication, organisation, and stakeholder management skills. Previous experience supporting or coordinating cybersecurity incidents will be highly valued.

What You Will Do

    • Act as a primary coordination point between customers and DFIR consultants during active cybersecurity incidents.

    • Coordinate and host incident scoping calls with customers to understand the incident, establish requirements, and support the engagement of the appropriate DFIR resources.

    • Coordinate incident response activities from initial engagement through investigation, remediation, and closure.

    • Work with DFIR consultants to understand investigation progress, priorities, dependencies, and customer requirements.

    • Maintain clear communication with customers throughout an incident, including investigation status, next steps, outstanding actions, and information requirements.

    • Coordinate meetings, incident updates, deliverables, and follow-up activities between customers and internal technical teams.

    • Help customers gather and provide the information, logs, system access, and technical context required by DFIR consultants.

    • Track actions, decisions, dependencies, and outstanding items throughout the incident lifecycle.

    • Identify potential delays, communication gaps, or blockers and work with the appropriate stakeholders to resolve or escalate them.

    • Translate technical investigation updates into clear, customer-appropriate language without changing the technical findings or conclusions of the investigation.

    • Translate incident reports, investigation updates, and other customer communications from English into Japanese when required, ensuring technical meaning and context are accurately maintained.

    • Support the preparation and delivery of customer updates, investigation reports, and incident debriefing sessions.

    • Coordinate with other cybersecurity teams, including Threat Intelligence, Technical Testing, Managed Detection and Response, and other relevant specialists when required.

    • Help ensure customers receive a consistent, professional, and well-coordinated experience during what can be a highly stressful situation.

What You Will Bring

    • 3+ years of experience working in cybersecurity, information technology, security operations, incident management, technical support, or a related technical environment.

    • Experience supporting, coordinating, or working with cybersecurity incidents will be highly valued.

    • Strong understanding of cybersecurity fundamentals and common security technologies.

    • Good understanding of enterprise IT environments, including Windows, networking, identity, cloud services, and security technologies.

    • Ability to understand and discuss cybersecurity incidents with technical specialists without needing to personally conduct digital forensic investigations.

    • Strong customer-facing communication skills and experience working with customers during technical or security incidents.

    • Experience coordinating technical activities involving multiple teams and stakeholders.

    • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple activities, priorities, and dependencies during time-sensitive situations.

    • Ability to communicate complex technical information clearly to stakeholders with different levels of technical knowledge.

    • Confidence working with customers during high-pressure or business-critical situations.

    • Native-level Japanese language proficiency, with professional proficiency in English.

    Desirable

    • Experience working in a Security Operations Centre, Managed Security Service, Incident Response, cybersecurity consulting, technical account management, or similar environment.

    • Previous experience coordinating cybersecurity incidents, major IT incidents, or other technical response activities.

Job Title: Campaign Organizing Director

Department: Campaigns

Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.

Scope: The Campaign Organizing Director is responsible for achieving all organizing objectives and for the effectiveness of the Club's organizing activities within assigned national campaigns and programs. The Campaign Organizing Director works with organizing staff and volunteer leaders to determine and implement strategies to build the number of supporters in the community, key partnerships with community leaders, government officials, donors and volunteer leadership to accomplish organizing objectives and win campaign goals and national priorities at the local, regional, and national level. The Campaign Organizing Director coaches and develops each program department staff organizer to maximize skills, ability and effectiveness. The Campaign Organizing Director ensures that programmatic commitments and objectives are met, that financial, operational and legal compliance standards are met regarding all activities in assigned communities.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

    1. Organizing Strategy: Serves as the lead strategist for Campaign organizing approaches, plans, metrics, and tactics that will achieve the Sierra Club’s national campaign outcomes. Works closely with managers and campaign directors to design organizing strategies unique to each campaign.

    2. Organizer Support: Mentors, coaches, trains, and supports, in partnership with staff managers, the Campaign Organizers in the Program Department. Provides support for Chapter Organizers and other staff who are funded to carry out organizing activities to achieve national campaign goals. Develops career progression for Campaign Organizers and ensures a consistent approach to skill advancement and growth.

    3. Cross-Department Collaboration: Represents the Program Department with the Field Department to design and execute organizing trainings that will support the entire Sierra Club. Leads cross-departmental projects and initiatives to increase organizing effectiveness, data tracking, and consistency across different parts of the Sierra Club’s organizing infrastructure.

    4. Management: Effectively manages, guides, and coaches direct-reports as assigned.Ensures professional development for staff, establishes performance objectives and expectations, evaluates accomplishments and effectiveness. Takes appropriate disciplinary action when needed, makes hiring and termination decisions for direct-reports.

    5. Spokesperson: Serves as a spokesperson on issues related to campaign organizing; lifts up stories of organizing success to contribute to a robust narrative about the Sierra Club’s work as a grassroots organization with organizing as a core approach to how we achieve our work. Represents the Sierra Club in organizing coalitions as assigned.

    6. Volunteer Engagement: Works closely with volunteer co-leads in the department and provides organizing support to volunteer leaders working on national priorities.

    7. Fundraising and Budgeting: Supports the Campaign Directors, organizational leaders, and the Advancement Department in fundraising activities. Participates in soliciting gifts, reporting on progress, and preparing formal materials that showcase the organizing work funded through the Program Department.Supports Responsible for good fiscal management, fiscal controls and administrative practices in all aspects of assigned operations. Ensures compliance with Club financial, employment and operations policies and with external regulations in all aspects of assigned operations.

    8. Department Leadership: Serves as a member of the Program Department’s leadership team. Holds organizing expertise on behalf of the department and weighs in and contributes to Departmental priority-setting, planning, and implementation.

The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

    • Significant organizing experience, including leading grassroots organizing initiatives in a campaign environment. In depth knowledge of the craft of organizing and the political system.

    • Experience managing organizers and managers, with a demonstrated ability to develop, train, mentor, and coach organizers.

    • Demonstrated ability to plan and execute effective campaigns across multiple states and venues.

    • Successful track record with fundraising for campaigns and for organizing strategies as part of campaigns.

    • Demonstrated effectiveness in using the media; excellent oral and written communication skills.

    • Prior responsibility for fiscal and business operations management.

    • Committed to evolution.You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.

About Epiconcept:

Epiconceptis a small-medium enterprise of approximately 110 people with a wide expertise in

epidemiology and in the development of information and communication tools for public health.

  • Certified research organisation ;

  • Certified data centre for hosting personal and medical data ;

  • Certified training company.

Our current partners are institutions and organisations in charge of Public Health programmes: WHO, ECDC, European Commission, Ministries of Health, NGOs, Foundations, etc.

The Epidemiology Department is a diverse and dynamic multi-disciplinary international team of approximately 20 individuals working mostly in infectious diseases with specialism in vaccination and vaccine policies, the development of guidance at national and international levels, and development and delivery of training courses. The epidemiology team has a wide expertise in different study methodologies (e.g. systematic literature reviews, case-control and cohort studies as well as cross- sectional surveys) and different applications to field epidemiology (e.g. vaccine effectiveness studies, outbreak investigation and pandemic response).

Post overview:

The successful candidate will provide high quality epidemiological research and data management support in all aspects of establishing, conducting, analysing and reporting on studies and projects.

The successful candidate will collaborate with senior epidemiologists who coordinate a variety of projects being led by the Epidemiology Department at Epiconcept.

The successful candidate will work on European multi-country projects (funded by international and European organisations).

The post-holder will:

  • draft of documents (e.g. protocols, statistical analysis plans etc) to support the on-going implementation of studies and projects ;

  • help manage, analyse and interpret epidemiological data, ensuring data are appropriately managed and analysed in a reliable and timely way ;

  • develop and maintain R scripts for data management, data checking, data analysis, data visualisation and automatisation of the project data and output in compliance with good data management rules ;

  • conduct analyses, prepare results and contribute, including as lead author, to peer-reviewed publications and other outputs (e.g. reports, conference abstracts) for wider dissemination ;

  • use evidence generated from project results and other research to identify current and future public health priorities and needs ;

  • establish a strong working relation with the senior epidemiologist to jointly ensure timely deliverables and to ensure that projects are managed in an effective way ;

  • support project management and maintain good scientific collaboration with key partners through regular interactions with participating and client representatives ;

  • prepare training material and provide training, as and when needed, including training of epidemiological concepts, analysis and software (R) ;

  • handle any other activities commensurate with the post.

There is also the possibility to participate in projects in other disease areas or activities such as training, applied research projects locally and overseas and related project management.

Pay will be commensurate with skills and experience. The contract duration for the post is a long-term contract.

Essential skills and experience

  • Postgraduate degree: MSc in biostatistics, epidemiology, data science or another related subject ;

  • Relevant experience in a similar position, working in surveillance, observational or other epidemiological research studies ;

  • Proficient R user, with demonstrable experience in data management and visualisation (e.g. dplyr, ggplot2), reproducible reporting (e.g. R Markdown, Quarto), and collaborative coding using Git and GitHub/Gitlab ;

  • Strong knowledge and experience of statistics as applied to epidemiological studies ;

  • Strong knowledge of epidemiological studies and methods ;

  • Excellent English level (minimum C1).

Desirable skills and experience

  • Postgraduate research degree: PhD in biostatistics, epidemiology, data science or another related subject ;

  • Experience of working with R Shiny to create interactive dashboards ;

  • Experience using other languages, such as Python or SQL, for data management and/or analysis ;

  • Experience of working on multicentre studies ;

  • Experience of working on European public health projects ;

  • Experience of using scientific evidence to inform and develop public health programmes ;

  • Experience of vaccine effectiveness, evaluation of surveillance systems, burden of disease or vaccination impact studies ;

  • Experience of using generative AI tools, including familiarity with the use of AI coding assistants like Claude code ;

  • Good knowledge of French ;

Essential abilities:

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills ;

  • Attention to detail ;

  • Work proactively and independently with a remote management ;

  • Strong interpersonal skills able to collaborate within a team and with partners from different countries ;

  • Work in time-sensitive environment without compromising the quality of work ;

Company Overview

Our client is a marketing team that works inside businesses with many locations, such as senior living communities, med spas, dental and healthcare groups, cannabis retailers, and schools. Its clients are in the US and Canada, and they pay a flat fee instead of a percentage of ad spend.

The company runs on Claude and has built its own operating system and client portal. AI agents do most of the production, so a small team can run a lot of client work.

Your Role

As Head of Growth, you're the final decision-maker on 6 to 10 client accounts, across paid media, websites, CRM, and creative. Agents and teammates bring you options, and you pick one, approve it, or send it back with the exact fix.

You report to the CEO and work as a peer to the founders. You'll start by taking over the approval queue on every active account. By day 90, delivery runs without the CEO in the loop, and you've built the tool or process that lets the team take on 5 more accounts with the same people.

Part of the job is building. You'll release features to the internal platform by directing Claude Code: you write the spec, test it on staging, and merge it. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to know exactly what you want and check that you got it.

This isn't an account manager role. If you've mostly passed the calls on spend, creative, or pricing to someone else, or you'd rather delegate to a team of specialists, it probably isn't the right fit.

You'll

  • Run the client relationship with owners, executive directors, and sales teams

  • Approve Google Ads and Meta builds before launch

  • Adjust budgets and bids, and cut the search terms that bring no leads

  • Own conversion tracking across GTM, GA4, and offline imports from the CRM

  • Direct WordPress rebuilds, then own go-live, redirects, and Search Console

  • Connect CRMs, call tracking, and forms so each lead can be followed to the sale

  • Approve client pricing changes, promotions, and policy pages

  • Sign off on weekly and monthly client reports before they go out

You Bring

  • 7+ years running marketing or growth for clients or at an agency

  • Final say on a client's ad spend, creative, or pricing, and you can name the decision

  • Google Ads and Meta campaigns you built and managed yourself

  • Daily work with Claude or a similar tool, and something real you released through it, like a site, an ad build, an automation, or code

  • The habit of checking AI output before it goes live

  • Comfort with tag managers, CRMs, DNS, and webhooks

  • Near-native English, and confidence saying no to a client on a call

  • The drive to grow with the company as it takes on more accounts

Bonus Points

  • Marketing work in senior living, med spas, dental, healthcare, cannabis retail, or education

  • Experience with industry CRMs such as ALIS, Pagoda, or Dutchie

  • Advertiser verification, A2P 10DLC registration, or HIPAA and cannabis ad rules handled yourself

  • WordPress beyond the editor, like themes, plugins, or a staging-to-production deploy

  • SQL, GitHub pull requests, or Supabase

What's Offered

  • Fully remote, full-time contractor role from LATAM

  • Working hours on US business hours

  • Paid in USD as a contractor. Share the range that fits your level and we'll go from there

  • Unlimited PTO, used responsibly, and you choose which holidays to take

  • A direct line to the CEO, with the founders as your peers

  • Room to grow as the company takes on more accounts

Interview Process

1️⃣ First Call: A 30-minute conversation with atomic✳HR
2️⃣ CEO Interview: The accounts you've run and the decisions that were yours
3️⃣ Co-founder Interview: How you'd work as a peer, and the final decision
