jobs.excerpt: DescriptionAbout the RoleZenity is looking for a Senior Technical Product Marketing Manager who understands agentic AI and cybersecurity and loves making complex technology clear, relevant, and compelling.
jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Zenity is looking for a Senior Technical Product Marketing Manager who understands agentic AI and cybersecurity and loves making complex technology clear, relevant, and compelling. You’ll help bring Zenity’s story to life, connecting the technical details of AI agent security to the decisions and business outcomes our customers care about.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who enjoys creating. You’re comfortable digging into a technical conversation with product and engineering, finding the story, and turning it into an article, a product demo, or a video people want to watch. You can speak credibly with security practitioners and explain the same idea clearly to a business leader.

This role reports to the Head of Product Marketing.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop positioning and messaging that explain what Zenity does, who it helps, and why it matters. Connect product capabilities to specific customer problems and support the story with evidence.
  • Create written content, including technical explainers, thought leadership, customer stories, solution briefs, and launch materials. Own work from the first idea through the finished piece.
  • Bring the story to video through product walkthroughs, short explainers, interviews, and demos. Help shape the format, write the script, and present on camera.
  • Build a deep understanding of Zenity’s products and the environments where customers deploy AI agents. Work closely with product, engineering, and security research to translate technical insights into useful content.
  • Develop demos and use cases that show how the technology works and why it matters to an organization.
  • Partner with sales to create presentations, competitive messaging, and practical answers to buyer questions.
  • Help lead product launches, connecting new capabilities to a clear customer need and a consistent story across channels.
  • Stay close to customers and developments in agentic AI and cybersecurity. Use those insights, along with content performance and sales feedback, to improve our messaging.

Requirements

  • Approximately 10 years of overall professional experience across product marketing, technical marketing, product management, solutions engineering, or related roles, including meaningful ownership of product messaging and content.
  • A focused body of work in AI over the past 3 to 4 years, with a strong understanding of generative AI and agentic systems.
  • A solid understanding of cybersecurity fundamentals, including identity and access management, data protection, threat detection, and risk management. You understand the priorities of security teams and can connect technical risks to business consequences.
  • Practical understanding of how AI agents use tools, access data, and take actions, and the security risks those behaviors introduce, including prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unintended data exposure.
  • The ability to translate technical information into business terms while preserving the details that matter. You can explain a capability, its limitations, and its value to different audiences.
  • Strong writing and editing skills, with examples of content you personally created.
  • Experience creating video content and enthusiasm for communicating on camera, demonstrating products, and trying new formats.
  • The judgment and independence to set priorities, work with subject matter experts, and take projects through publication.

Experience marketing enterprise software to CISOs and security teams would be especially useful. Hands-on experience building or configuring AI agents would also help you develop credible demos and ask better questions.

About Zenity

Zenity is the leader in AI Agent Security and the first company to bring an agent-centric security platform to market. As enterprises accelerate AI agent adoption, we are establishing the security framework for how AI agents are secured and governed at enterprise scale.

We deliver full-lifecycle visibility, governance, detection, prevention, and response for AI agents from build time to runtime, across SaaS, home-grown platforms, and end-user devices. Backed by $180M+ in total funding, including a $125M Series C led by Norwest, with participation from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Microsoft's M12, Zenity is trusted by Fortune 500 and Global 2000 enterprises worldwide.

Gartner named Zenity a Market Shaper in its inaugural Emerging Market Quadrant for AI Application Security, Startup Vendors, one of only two vendors placed in the Market Shapers quadrant among nearly 20 startup vendors assessed. This follows Gartner naming Zenity the Company to Beat in AI Agent Governance earlier this year.

Join us in shaping how AI agents are secured at enterprise scale.

What We Look For At Zenity

  • You take ownership of outcomes, not just activity, and you don't need a detailed brief on what to create.
  • You move fast and hold a high bar for your own work.
  • You're comfortable building where the playbook is still being written.
  • You work easily with researchers, executives, and the field team, and pick up technical topics quickly.

Interview Process

  • Recruiter Screen (30-45 minutes minutes) – Learn more about Zenity, the role, and how we work.
  • Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes) – An intro discussion about your technical and PMM background.
  • Sales Engineering Leadership Interview (30 minutes) – A conversation focused on collaboration and technical awarness around security teams and marketing to CISOs
  • Product Leadership Interview-(30 minutes)- A conversation about building and developing with AI agents.
  • Leadership Interview – CRO or CEO (30–45 minutes) – Discussion focused on technical depth, security expertise, and cross-functional execution.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $180,000-$200,000, depending on experience, skills, and location. In addition to the base compensation, this role may be eligible for equity and performance-based incentives.

jobs.description:
Company :

Allegheny Health Network

Job Description :

GENERAL OVERVIEW:

This job is responsible for the reliability, availability, and performance of critical healthcare IT systems, principally in the Environment of Care (EOC), enabling seamless access to essential services for patients, providers, and the people we serve. Proactively identifies and mitigates potential disruptions to maintain the highest standards of care and operational efficiency. This role blends software engineering, clinical engineering, and security principles with a deep understanding of healthcare operations to minimize downtime, improve system resilience, and to support clinical workflows and continuity of hospital operations. Works cross-functionally with AHN site leaders and teams to navigate and to monitor and support building automation and facility systems, clinical engineering / IoT, healthcare delivery technology architecture, infrastructure and platform operations, and cybersecurity. Fosters a culture of automation, continuous improvement, collaboration, and patient safety. Responsible for developing and delivering reporting systems in order to monitor and maintain system health metrics (e.g., latency, traffic, errors, and saturation) leveraging industry practices, manufacturer guidance, and other service delivery objectives.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively engages with clinical engineering, cybersecurity, device manufacturers, suppliers, and Information Technology SMEs to oversee and to implement and deliver on activities which manage, monitor, and secure a diverse range of clinical devices and other technology equipment (e.g., IoT), ensuring compliance with HIPAA and other relevant regulations (e.g., FDA, TJC, PCI). Keeps current on healthcare IT trends, including AI, security patching, and best practices for device hardening. Assists with network segmentation, access control, and other configuration and monitoring activities whichisolate and to protect clinical and other critical devices. Automates monitoring tasks to improve efficiency and reduce errors. Identifies and remediates vulnerabilities in clinical devices and related infrastructure. Identifies and reports issues with assets, devices, integration services, and other equipment. Consults the appropriate parties to develop and deploy a fix/solution or oversees ownership of resolution actions. Utilizes observability practices to gain deep insights into system behavior, enabling faster identification and resolution of issues.20%

  • Troubleshoots technical issues related to medical equipment and systems in partnership with Clinical Engineering and Cybersecurity Engineering. Assists with maintaining assets throughout their medical device technology lifecycle – from product/device evaluation, discovery, to implementation, maintenance, and through retirement. Maintains documentation related to the IT infrastructure supporting clinicaland other critical devices according to company frameworks, standards, etc. Participates in the planning and executes preventative maintenance activities as directed. Demonstrates the ability to analyze complex problems and develop effective solutions, how to troubleshoot system outages and performance issues, and how to work collaboratively with other IT, cybersecurity, facility, AI and application teams to resolve issues and to conduct root cause analyses.20%

  • Supports activities and initiatives affecting their assigned area of responsibility including, but not limited to platform / product management, disaster recovery services, infrastructure and architecture, storage management, and release management. Participates in the planning and execution of downtime drills and system / device recovery exercises. Supports other emergency preparedness drills and exercises, as needed. Leads or participates in post-incident reviews to identify root causes and implement corrective actions. Works with cross-functional stakeholders to Implement and to maintain redundant systems and failover mechanisms to minimize downtime. Reviews and provides feedback on emergency operations plans and other materials which are used to respond to emergency situations (e.g., Continuity of Operations Plans, Incident Response Guides, Downtime Procedures). Actively supports the planning and execution of system migrations, releases, and upgrades to ensure minimal disruption to clinical operations. Executes on assigned migration or installation plans, including risk assessments, rollback procedures, and communication strategies. Assists local site leaders with navigating shared services (e.g., AI, IT, Information Security, Clinical Engineering, Platform Operations, Technology Acquisition).20%

  • Actively engages with facility leaders to optimize the performance and monitoring of building automation systems (BAS), including HVAC, lighting, fire suppression, security systems, etc. Executes activities and assists with the development or maintenance of procedures used to monitor BAS performance metrics and proactively identifies potential issues. Engages with facilities management to implement improvements to the BAS infrastructure. Engages with cybersecurity, vendors/manufacturers, et. al. to ensure the security of building automation systems and oversees monitoring of performance, service delivery, and support.20%

  • Maintains detailed documentation of systems, device inventories, processes, and procedures.Leads by example by sharing knowledge and best practices with other staff and cross-functional teams. Stays current with the latest technologies and trends in site reliability engineering. Leads or participates in briefings with cross-functional stakeholders to understand assignments, priorities, support tickets, customer needs, etc.15%

  • Other duties as assigned or requested.5%

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Management Information Systems, IT, or related field or relevant experience and/or education as determined by the company in lieu of bachelor's degree.

  • 3 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Systems Administration, or DevOps particularly in healthcare IT

Preferred

  • Master's degree inComputer Science, Engineering, Management Information Systems, IT, or related field.

  • 3 years of experience in Medical device management lifecycle, network / device segmentation, vulnerability and patch management

  • 3 years of experience in Healthcare IT experience in architecture, automation, IoT, telemetry, telehealth, security, system development lifecycle, capacity planning, networking, continuous integration / continuous delivery pipelines (CI/CD), incident management, scripting, metrics, monitoring, redundancy, etc.

  • 3 years of experience in working in highly regulated environments

  • 3 years of experience in Progressive roles, preferably inclinical engineering, IT, business continuity, backup and storage management, building automation, or cybersecurity discipline in healthcare

SKILLS:

  • Problem-Solving: Excellent analytical and troubleshooting skills; High capacity to think analytically, interpret information / observations, apply judgment and to assist with making effective, strategic decisions.

  • Collaboration: Ability to work effectively in a team environment; demonstrated ability to support multiple sites and locations while maintaining consistency in service delivery processes and procedures.

  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Flexibility: Willingness to participate in activities or incidents which may occur outside of regular work schedules.

  • Leadership: Demonstrated resource and project planning capabilities, decision making skills, history of results-oriented delivery, and effective team building across multiple locations and a diverse team of staff, partners, and stakeholders.

  • Security Awareness: Understanding of security best practices and how to apply them in a healthcare IT environment.

  • Delivery and Execution: Demonstrated competency in the execution of multiple projects, including managing resources across multiple projects to meet goals.

  • Relationships: Strong relationship building skills and ability to influence with and without authority in a matrixed organization.

As a component of job responsibilities, employees may have access to covered information, cardholder data, or other confidential customer information that must be protected at all times. jobs.description:
A NOTE ON HOW TO REACH US

We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others. That said, due to the high volume of direct messages and emails we receive, cold outreach isn't the preferred way to be considered for a role, and we're not able to prioritize applications submitted this way. To apply for open positions, please visit our careers page, which is the fastest and most effective route to being considered.

About Foundant

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Role Overview

The Billing & Collections Specialist keeps our cash flow healthy by managing the billing-to-cash cycle for a portfolio of customer accounts. You’ll review and bill approved sales orders, apply client payments, follow up on past-due balances, resolve billing questions, and partner with Customer Success, Sales, and Support to keep customer relationships strong while we get paid on time.

Where You’ll Work:
  • As a remote-first workplace, we believe in offering flexibility and the freedom to work where it suits you best, while staying connected through technology. Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
  • With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Whether you're working remotely or from one of our office locations, you'll be contributing to a vibrant, collaborative culture focused on driving meaningful impact across the world.
WhatYou’llDo:
  • Review and invoice all approved sales orders in NetSuite accurately and on schedule
  • Apply incoming client payments promptly and accurately
  • Research and resolve billing disputes, short-pays, and unapplied cash, working with internal teams as needed
  • Contact customers by phone and email to collect past-due balances and secure payment commitments
  • Own every past-due account in your portfolio through resolution or escalation, reviewing AR aging daily to prioritize by balance, age, and risk
  • Document all collection activity and customer communications in the AR ticketing system
  • Escalate high-risk accounts, such as those nearing suspension per our collections policy, to the Billing & Collections Manager with a clear summary and recommendation
  • Support month-end close by reconciling AR aging to the trial balance
  • Track down the correct billing contact when invoices aren't reaching the customer, partnering with Sales and Customer Success
  • Perform other ad hoc tasks/projects related to your role as directed by the Billing & Collections Manager and/or Global Controller.
WhatYou’llNeed:

Required

  • At least 3 years of accounts receivable, collections, or billing experience, including SaaS or subscription billing
  • Experience with an ERP system like NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or Great Plains
  • Track record of identifying the root cause of a recurring billing or collections problem and fixing it
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort having firm but professional conversations about overdue balances
  • Solid attention to detail and accuracy with numbers
  • Intermediate Excel skills (e.g., lookups, pivot tables)
  • Ability to manage a high volume of accounts (hundreds per month) and shifting priorities
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Preferred

  • Experience with NetSuite
  • Experience with Salesforce
  • Experience with collections automation or payment portal tools
Why You’ll Love Working at Foundant:
  • At the heart of everything we do is a commitment to innovation and making a positive impact. Whether you’re working on projects that empower not-for-profits, community foundations, or corporations, your contributions will help drive real-world change.
  • We offer competitive salary and benefits, including tuition, and lifestyle reimbursements, and bespoke mindfulness and fitness initiatives.
  • With our Flexible PTO policy, you’ll have the freedom to manage your time in a way that supports your personal well-being and professional success.
  • We’re committed to your professional and personal development. With our merger, you'll have the chance to collaborate across teams, giving you exposure to diverse ideas, expertise, and projects that span multiple industries.
  • As part of a larger organization, you’ll have even more opportunities to grow your career. Whether it’s exploring new roles, leadership opportunities, or shifting to a different department, we support internal mobility to help you achieve your career goals
  • You’ll enjoy autonomy and responsibility, empowering you to approach your work creatively and independently, fostering innovation and independent thought.
  • Employee recognition is a core part of our culture. When you do a great job, we make sure everyone knows about it!

Foundant is an equal opportunity employer, committed to building a diverse workforce that represents the communities we serve. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, and will consider all applicants without regard to race, color, citizenship, religion, sex, marital/family status, sexual orientation, gender identity, Indigenous status, age, disability, or individuals who may require accommodation.

We’re Hyve, a global events company that does things differently.

Our events deliver game-changing impact for people, businesses and beyond. That might mean winning a major contract, securing transformational investment, getting on the shelves of a giant retailer or hearing from thought leaders who are changing the future.

The purpose of every one of our events is to bring the people who power major industries together – and open a world of potential.

At the same time, we’re using our events as platforms for progress, to drive the conversation across the world’s biggest industries on crucial topics like sustainability, diversity and ethical business.

These moments can change lives. And making those connections motivates us every single day.

But creating those human connections doesn’t just happen at our events. It’s part of everyday life when you work at Hyve. There are all sorts of socials, inclusion workshops and professional development opportunities to get your teeth into. And then there are the benefits. From gym memberships to private medical care, season ticket loans to healthy pensions, we’ve got you covered in all kinds of ways. (We’ll even give you an extra day off on your birthday!)

The bit about you
First of all, whatever your background and whatever your beliefs, there’s a culture of belonging here at Hyve and everyone is welcome. The question isn’t where you are from – it’s where you want to go.

We’re a positive bunch and if you’re a “glass half full” kind of person you’ll fit right in. Our values are brilliant work, fresh thinking, rich connections, and collective buzz. And just to be clear, these aren’t just words we put on the walls and forget about. They pull everyone together and help us all produce work that we’re proud to put our names to. If that resonates with you, great: we’re on the same page.

  • Clear, personable written and verbal communication, with persistence and good judgment in follow-up.
  • Highly organised and detail-focused, with the ability to manage multiple events and deadlines.
  • Comfortable using spreadsheets, CRM systems, email and online research tools, and quick to learn new systems.
  • Self-directed, adaptable and collaborative, with a strong sense of ownership for recruitment outcomes. Additional information Occasional travel to events may be required.

jobs.description:
1. Role Summary

The Chief Experience Officer (CXO) is responsible for developing and executing the organization's overall experience strategy across customer, client, employee, and stakeholder touchpoints. The role focuses on building a customer-centric culture, improving service quality, strengthening customer relationships, and ensuring consistent, seamless, and positive experiences across all insurance and investment products and services.

The CXO will lead customer experience (CX), service delivery, customer engagement, and experience transformation initiatives. The position will work closely with business, operations, technology, sales, marketing, claims, underwriting, and investment teams to improve satisfaction, loyalty, retention, and long-term business performance.

2. Key Responsibilities

Customer Experience Strategy

  • Develop and implement an enterprise-wide customer experience strategy aligned with the organization's business objectives.
  • Establish a customer-first culture across insurance, investment, and financial service operations.
  • Define customer experience standards, service principles, and performance benchmarks.
  • Identify opportunities to differentiate the organization through superior customer service and engagement.

Customer Journey Management

  • Map and optimize end-to-end customer journeys across product discovery, onboarding, policy issuance, premium payments, claims, renewals, investment services, and account management.
  • Identify service gaps, customer pain points, and process inefficiencies.
  • Simplify customer interactions and reduce friction across digital and traditional service channels.
  • Ensure consistent experiences across branches, call centres, websites, mobile applications, and relationship management teams.

Customer Satisfaction and Retention

  • Develop initiatives to improve customer satisfaction, loyalty, retention, and lifetime value.
  • Monitor customer feedback, complaints, service requests, and customer sentiment.
  • Establish customer feedback mechanisms, including surveys, NPS, CSAT, and customer interviews.
  • Lead initiatives to reduce customer attrition and improve policy renewal and investment account retention rates.

Digital Experience and Innovation

  • Collaborate with technology and digital teams to improve online platforms, mobile applications, customer portals, and self-service solutions.
  • Drive digital adoption and improve accessibility of insurance and investment services.
  • Leverage customer analytics, automation, AI, and CRM platforms to personalize customer interactions.
  • Champion innovative solutions that improve customer convenience and operational efficiency.

Customer Service and Relationship Management

  • Oversee customer service standards and service excellence initiatives.
  • Ensure timely resolution of customer inquiries, complaints, claims-related concerns, and investment service requests.
  • Strengthen relationship management practices for individual, corporate, institutional, and high-net-worth clients.
  • Establish service-level agreements (SLAs) and escalation procedures across customer-facing departments.

Employee Experience and Organizational Culture

  • Develop initiatives that improve employee engagement and internal service culture.
  • Promote collaboration between departments to deliver consistent customer experiences.
  • Support employee training and development in customer service, communication, relationship management, and service excellence.
  • Align employee experience initiatives with customer experience objectives.

Governance, Risk and Compliance

  • Ensure customer experience practices comply with applicable insurance, investment, consumer protection, data privacy, and financial services regulations.
  • Work with compliance and risk teams to address customer-related regulatory concerns.
  • Promote transparent communication, fair treatment, responsible product information, and ethical customer engagement.
  • Establish processes for monitoring and resolving customer complaints and service-related risks.

Leadership and Performance Management

  • Lead and develop customer experience, customer service, and service transformation teams.
  • Establish departmental objectives, budgets, KPIs, and performance management frameworks.
  • Present customer experience performance reports and strategic recommendations to the CEO and Board.
  • Collaborate with senior executives to integrate customer experience priorities into business strategy.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Finance, Management, Customer Experience, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA) or a relevant discipline preferred.
  • 10–15+ years of progressive experience in customer experience, customer service, operations, client relationship management, or business transformation.
  • At least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive management position.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, wealth management, financial services, or other regulated service industries.
  • Demonstrated success in developing and implementing customer experience strategies.
  • Strong knowledge of customer journey mapping, CRM platforms, customer analytics, NPS, CSAT, and service quality management.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams and large-scale service improvement initiatives.
  • Strong strategic thinking, communication, stakeholder management, and leadership capabilities.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

- Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT).

- Net Promoter Score (NPS).

  • Customer retention and policy renewal rates.
  • Customer attrition and churn reduction.
  • Customer complaint resolution time and satisfaction.

- First Contact Resolution (FCR) rate.

  • Digital channel adoption and self-service utilization.
  • Customer onboarding and service turnaround time.
  • Customer lifetime value and relationship growth.
  • Employee engagement and service culture improvement.
  • Compliance with customer service standards and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Data & AI Platform Engineer Remote
jobs.excerpt: ORDERYOYO – Senior Data & AI Platform EngineerRemote · Quarterly team gatherings in one of our global offices Join OrderYOYO’s Data team to build the data pipelines and lakehouse that power executive reporting and merchant insights across our platform, and automate how we deliver finance data and AI-driven data products to the rest of the business.
jobs.description:
ORDERYOYO – Senior Data & AI Platform Engineer

Remote · Quarterly team gatherings in one of our global offices

Join OrderYOYO’s Data team to build the data pipelines and lakehouse that power executive reporting and merchant insights across our platform, and automate how we deliver finance data and AI-driven data products to the rest of the business.

You’ll own complex changes from technical design through release and production operation, working closely with the leadership team, Finance, Product and fellow engineers. Your work will improve the accuracy and reliability of our reporting, merchant insights and finance data, while reducing routine manual Finance work.

Our data platform runs in a Microsoft Azure cloud environment, and we’re moving it to Microsoft Fabric. We value transferable experience: strong Azure Databricks or Synapse engineers who can quickly develop deep Fabric expertise are encouraged to apply. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a pure architecture, BI or people-management position, and you’ll regularly design, code, troubleshoot and operate production data solutions.

Role Mission

Build and evolve OrderYOYO’s data platform into a single source of truth for executive reporting, merchant insights, finance automation and AI, leading the move to a modern Microsoft Fabric lakehouse. You’ll help strengthen the reliability and quality of our data in production while building AI into how we deliver data products and supporting our growing international restaurant platform.

Core responsibilities

•Design, build and operate production-grade data solutions in Microsoft Fabric across Lakehouse, Warehouse, notebooks, pipelines and related platform capabilities.

•Build and run production pipelines in Fabric, Python and PySpark that are tested and maintainable, not just notebooks.

•Design ingestion and transformation patterns that scale across multiple source systems, databases and business domains while controlling source impact, concurrency and platform cost.

•Manage Fabric capacity and cost, and retire redundant legacy layers.

•Lead migrations from legacy to modern platforms with metric parity, stakeholder sign-off, change control and safe decommissioning.

•Run the platform in production: monitoring, alerting, incident triage, root-cause analysis, data-quality checks, lineage and runbooks.

•Diagnose and resolve production issues across SQL, Spark, pipelines and semantic models, including performance degradation, data failures and capacity/resource constraints.

•Support and evolve governed semantic models and reusable metric definitions, working closely with analytics and business stakeholders to ensure performance, consistency and reliability.

•Build AI into the platform and our delivery: RAG, Azure OpenAI and agents, with prompt and version management.

•Deliver applied data science such as churn, recommendations, personalisation, fraud or risk models, and show the results.

•Work with executives, Finance, Product and engineering, and judge when to move fast, standardise, automate or hold.

Must-have requirements

•6+ years of relevant data experience, including substantial recent hands-on data engineering or data-platform engineering responsibility in production environments.

•Demonstrated ability to independently take a data-engineering problem from requirements and technical design through implementation, production deployment, monitoring and ongoing operation.

•Deep hands-on Microsoft Fabric, or strong Synapse, Databricks or Delta experience with a clear path to Fabric.

•Strong understanding of lakehouse architecture and Delta-based data engineering, including partitioning, schema evolution, file optimisation and performance considerations.

•Expert SQL and T-SQL, including complex modelling and tuning.

•Production-grade Python or PySpark.

•Strong experience designing and implementing incremental data ingestion patterns, including approaches such as CDC, change tracking or watermarks, with reliable merge/upsert, replay and idempotent processing.

•Experience with analytical and semantic data modelling, ideally with Power BI/Fabric semantic models, including performance optimisation, governance and reusable business metrics.

•Working knowledge of Azure platform fundamentals including Azure SQL, ADLS/OneLake, Entra ID, managed identities, RBAC and Key Vault.

•A track record of leading a legacy-to-modern migration.

•Real, hands-on AI engineering beyond out-of-the-box Copilot.

•Concrete data science or ML models you delivered, with results.

Strong-to-have experience

•Strong Power BI/Fabric experience, including Direct Lake, DAX, semantic model performance tuning, incremental refresh and capacity considerations.

•Infrastructure-as-Code experience with Terraform, Bicep or equivalent tooling.

•Data platform experience in SaaS, marketplace, fintech, payments, e-commerce or multi-region businesses.

Who We Are

At OrderYOYO, company culture comes first. We create a positive, inclusive environment where people are trusted to do their best work and take ownership of what they build. We look for engineers who take ownership, raise risks early, explain decisions clearly, collaborate respectfully and follow through on commitments.

Our values describe what that looks like day to day:

  • Passion: Adaptable and positive in a fast-moving environment, proactive about improving how things work.

  • Action: Leads by example and takes the initiative rather than waiting to be asked.

  • Compassion: Supports colleagues and considers the impact of decisions on merchants and teammates.

  • One Team: Communicates clearly in writing and in person, stays calm under pressure and shares information openly.

We help restaurants succeed online by providing branded websites, mobile apps and tailored marketing solutions, giving them full control of their business. By removing high commission fees charged by third-party platforms, we empower restaurants to grow sustainably.

What we offer

•A salary of up to £80,000 per year (or local equivalent).

•A remote role, with quarterly in-person gatherings at one of our global offices.

•Ownership of a business-critical data and AI platform.

•A collaborative, international engineering team.

jobs.excerpt: The Director, People AI Engineering & Innovation is Assurant’s hands-on AI technical and product leader for the People Organization.
jobs.description:
The Director, People AI Engineering & Innovation is Assurant’s hands-on AI technical and product leader for the People Organization. This leader establishes the People Organization’s technical AI strategy, architecture, platform roadmap, engineering standards and delivery framework while partnering with SLT sponsors, People Organization teams and the Execution COE to shape and evaluate demand. The Director determines the right solution path and turns prioritized opportunities into secure, production-grade AI products with measurable value. The Director brings deep experience from outside traditional HR and works directly in discovery, prototyping, design review, troubleshooting and delivery when needed. Safety, security, privacy, roles and access, infrastructure readiness, responsible AI and human controls are built into every stage with enterprise technology and control partners. The role establishes clear operating interfaces and decision rights across AI Innovation, Workday and People Technology, People Data and Analytics, ERIN/Unify Experience, the Execution COE, People functional teams and enterprise partners.


What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?


People AI Technical Strategy, Architecture & Delivery Framework


  • Establish and evolve the People Organization’s technical AI strategy and roadmap, translating priorities and emerging capabilities into a clear architecture, platform direction and sequenced capability roadmap.
  • Define reusable technical patterns, engineering standards, decision frameworks and delivery practices that move solutions securely from concept through production, stabilization and formal transfer.
  • Partner with SLT sponsors, People teams and the Execution COE to help teams understand what is technically possible, shape opportunities and determine when AI is the right solution versus Workday, automation, process simplification or another platform.
  • Maintain a clear point of view on architecture, platform choices, security, roles and access, responsible AI, production readiness and long-term supportability.

Hands-On AI Architecture, Engineering & Delivery


  • Serve as the technical and architecture authority for People AI solutions across approved platforms.
  • Participate directly in prototyping, architecture, workflow and integration design, technical reviews, evaluations and troubleshooting.
  • Lead approved solutions from discovery through design, build, validation, launch and a defined stabilization period.
  • Establish reusable patterns, grounded-solution approaches, evaluation methods, documentation and engineering standards.

Safety, Security, Access & Responsible AI


  • Build safety, security, privacy, identity, roles, permissions, least-privilege access and People-data protection into every stage of the lifecycle.
  • Partner at every stage with IT, Infrastructure, Information Security, Privacy, Legal and enterprise AI-governance teams.
  • Ensure appropriate human oversight, escalation, monitoring, auditability and controls for sensitive decisions and higher-risk use cases.
  • Retain approval authority over architecture, security, access, integrations, model changes and production readiness and pause changes that do not meet required standards.

Value Realization, Governance & Product Lifecycle


  • Define success measures for adoption, quality, capacity released, experience improvement, control effectiveness and sustained ROI.
  • After stabilization, complete a formal transfer to a named business or product owner who owns adoption, business priorities, backlog and value realization.
  • Retain technical governance over architecture, security, access, integrations, model or platform changes, evaluations, monitoring and production readiness.
  • Partner with the Execution COE and product owners on quarterly results readouts and recommendations to scale, improve, hold or retire solutions.

Operating Model, Decision Rights & Cross-Functional Partnership


  • Establish and maintain clear operating interfaces across AI Innovation, Workday and People Technology, Data and Analytics, ERIN/Unify Experience, the Execution COE, functional teams and enterprise partners.
  • Define and uphold decision rights, design authorities, service expectations, escalation paths, technical ownership and lifecycle accountabilities.
  • Partner with SLT sponsors and functional teams on business problems; partner with the Execution COE on education, show-and-tells, discovery, intake, prioritization and portfolio governance.
  • Partner with the Workday leader when solutions touch Workday data, processes, roles, integrations or transactions, preserving Workday as the authoritative system of record.
  • Contribute technical perspective, demonstrations and reusable examples that help leaders recognize opportunities, without sole accountability for generating organizational demand.

Talent & Team Leadership


  • Build a high-performing, hands-on AI product and engineering team by setting a clear talent standard and meaningful accountability for outcomes.
  • Develop talent through direct coaching, technical reviews, differentiated development, stretch assignments and clear expectations.
  • Build bench strength and succession capability and prepare team members for broader product, technical and leadership responsibility.
  • Evolve roles and hire capabilities where gaps exist, with emphasis on architecture, engineering, security, evaluation, responsible AI and production delivery.
  • Use external partners selectively while maintaining internal architecture authority, technical knowledge, accountability and ownership.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, data science or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 10+ years of progressive technology, software, data or AI experience, including leadership of production and enterprise-grade solutions and teams.
  • 3+ years of deep hands-on experience designing and delivering AI products, agents, grounded solutions, workflows, integrations and enterprise applications in production.
  • Demonstrated technical depth in solution architecture, APIs, data flows, identity, roles and access, security, monitoring, evaluations and production readiness.
  • Experience developing technical AI strategies, architecture roadmaps, reusable patterns and engineering frameworks.
  • Experience with Microsoft Copilot, UnifyApps, Leena AI, Claude or comparable enterprise AI platforms.
  • Experience embedding security, privacy, responsible AI, human oversight and auditability throughout a product lifecycle.
  • Strong product judgment and experience translating ambiguous business problems into practical solutions and measurable outcomes.
  • Ability to personally prototype, inspect designs, review technical work, troubleshoot complex issues and lead alongside engineers.
  • Experience establishing decision rights and operating interfaces across business, product, platform, data, portfolio and control teams.
  • Demonstrated talent leadership, including differentiated development, bench building, succession planning, hiring and effective use of external partners.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Advanced degree in computer science, engineering, AI, data science or a related field.
  • Experience building AI products outside traditional HR or People Technology environments.
  • Experience with enterprise copilots, agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation, orchestration platforms and model evaluation.
  • Experience operating in highly regulated or data-sensitive environments.
  • Familiarity with People processes or People technology is helpful but not required.

jobs.excerpt: We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast-growing team building an agent-native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast-growing team building an agent-native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google search, but for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing these systems to search and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval, ranking and passage extraction under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24/7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production. In the first year, you will own a specific part of the search stack, e.g. ranking or iterative retrieval.

What you'll work on:

  • Designing an agent-native search system that handles everything from low-latency single-hop search to complex deep search tasks requiring iterative planning, querying, refinement and reasoning.

  • Training ranking and retrieval models optimized for agent-driven workflows under real world constraints

  • Bringing the latest advances from the research community to our search stack and ship it to production.

Your responsibilities:

  • Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

  • Design and evolve multi-stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, retrieval, reranking and iterative retrieval)

  • Lead experimentation on modern retrieval approaches (embedding research, sparse and hybrid retrieval, reranking, context compression) and bring them into production

  • Develop methods for grounding LLMs in real-time web data at scale, using trust, quality and freshness signals to surface reliable sources

  • Partner with the evaluation team to define new metrics for agentic systems, where correctness is not reducible to clicks

  • Analyze trade-offs across relevance, latency, and cost, and work closely with engineering to deploy systems that operate at web scale

  • Mentor researchers and engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

Must haves:

  • 8+ years of experience in applied AI, ML, or software engineering

  • Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

  • Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking or building RAG-based assistants

  • Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

  • Experience with LLM-integrated or knowledge-intensive systems

  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

  • Strong programming skills in Python

  • Top-tier publications (ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, AAAI, EMNLP, ACL)

  • Ability to operate in a fast-moving, product-driven environment with high ownership and autonomy

Nice to haves

  • Background in agentic AI systems (agents, tool use, autonomous workflows)

  • Experience with RL post-training of LLMs or VLMs

Coinstar’s Security Engineer II is responsible for the design, implementation and maintenance of security solutions to include email security, network security including firewall management, endpoint protection, and vulnerability management. Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee Coinstar’s email security controls and respond to potential phishing scenarios as well as help conduct phishing tests.
  • Manage ongoing endpoint protection services including patching and incident response when required inclusive of mobile device management.
  • Spearhead addressing vulnerabilities across all applicable layers using severity and impact to prioritize response.
  • Expand monitoring and alerting where applicable using Coinstar’s observability solutions.
  • Participate in technical design reviews and security assessments during project execution.
  • Respond to third party risk assessment questionnaires.
  • Perform off hour support activities when required.
  • Work with team members in support of evolving Coinstar identity services and data protection services.

Education & Experience

  • Knowledge of feeding applicable logs to SIEM for event management.

The typical starting salary range for this position is between $117,308-$146,635 per year. jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityFutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadRiuso, an AI recommerce venture.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadRiuso, an AI recommerce venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Riusois the operating record for electronics returns and liquidation benches. Owner-operated resellers and refurbishers spend around eleven minutes identifying, grading and pricing each returned or liquidated unit by hand. When the bench backs up, units default to the liquidation pallet, the lowest-value exit.Riusoidentifies and grades each unit from photos in seconds and prices every disposition route, from resell and refurb to part-out, wholesale and pallet. It then routes the unit to the highest-recovery option. Every decision becomes memory the bench owns: repeat models price instantly, seller manifest accuracy builds over time, and outbound IMEI records turn mismatched returns into winnable claims. It runs on a phone and a label printer, with no integration.

Market Context

US consumers returned an estimated $849.9B of merchandise in 2025, and North American refurbished electronics is a roughly $17B market growing at double digits. Riuso addresses a $2.2B TAM across North American returns and recommerce benches. Its beachhead is 12,000 electronics-focused owner-operators, a $144M SAM. Right-to-repair laws now in force across California, New York, Texas, Oregon and five other states are deepening the parts market. Tariffs on new devices are pulling more buyers toward refurbished. Both make every unit on the bench worth more to price correctly.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

  • Investor and advisor network across supply chain tech and early-stage capital markets

  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with owner-operated electronics resellers and refurbishers, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion

  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback

  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction

  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement

  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

  • Direct exposure to electronics resale, liquidation, refurbishment or reverse logistics

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

The Director is responsible for translating strategic priorities into operational execution, developing leaders, monitoring program performance, supporting budget stewardship, and advancing whole-person care models that improve member outcomes, promote community integration, and support housing stability. The Director partners closely with Senior Leadership to identify risks, opportunities, and innovative approaches that improve quality, outcomes, and operational effectiveness.

This position is required to reside in North Carolina within 40 miles of one of the counties within the Alliance catchment areas (Mecklenburg, Wake, Durham, Orange, Johnston, Harnett, or Cumberland).

This position will allow the successful candidate to work a schedule that will be primarily remote. While there is no expectation of being in the office routinely, they will be required to come into the Alliance Office for business and team meetings as needed.

Responsibilities & Duties

People Leader

  • Work with Human Resources to attract, maintain, and retain a highly qualified and well-trained workforce
  • Ensure staff are well trained in and comply with all organization and department policies, procedures, and business processes
  • Provide direct clinical and administrative supervision of team members. This may include routine clinical review of cases, interpretation of census data, and advising team members regarding outreach to network providers regarding cases where care teams are engaged

  • Support a learning environment to advance team skills and professional development

Program Leadership & Strategic Planning

  • Translate departmental strategic initiatives into measurable operational plans and program objectives
  • Monitor emerging trends, regulatory changes, and best practices impacting care management, housing stability, integrated care, and population health
  • Collaborate with Senior Directors to support implementation of divisional strategic plans
  • Lead operational planning activities related to program compliance and process improvement
  • Develop recommendations to improve member outcomes, program effectiveness, and staff efficiency
  • Identify opportunities to expand innovative approaches supporting integrated care and community living

Leadership Development & Workforce Management

  • Provide direct oversight, coaching, and development of managers and supervisors responsible for TCL and TCM functions
  • Establish leadership development plans and succession planning strategies for emerging leaders
  • Foster a culture of accountability, engagement, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement
  • Monitor workforce capacity, staffing ratios, workload distribution, and employee engagement
  • Ensure managers effectively supervise, mentor, and develop staff
  • Promote cross-functional collaboration and professional development opportunities across programs
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, retention, and talent development initiatives
  • Partner with Human Resources regarding performance management, disciplinary actions, and workforce planning activities

Operational Oversight & Performance Management

  • Oversee daily operations across TCM and TCL programs to ensure compliance with regulatory, contractual, accreditation, and organizational requirements
  • Monitor key performance indicators, productivity metrics, quality outcomes, timeliness standards, and program deliverables
  • Ensure appropriate member assignment, risk stratification, care management activities, and caseload management practices
  • Monitor escalations, critical incidents, member grievances, housing barriers, and other high-risk situations
  • Develop corrective action plans and performance improvement initiatives when performance expectations are not met
  • Ensure operational consistency through standardized workflows, desk references, policies, and procedures
  • Evaluate operational effectiveness and implement improvements to increase efficiency and service quality

jobs.description:
Job Title: Grant Reviewer, K-12 Education (Direct Investment in Students)
Work Arrangement: Remote
Location: Remote, United States
Employment Type: Part-Time, Independent Contractor (1099)
Engagement Type: Short-term, per grant competition; paid per application reviewed
Final Interview:

Position Summary

Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring Grant Reviewers on behalf of the Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE), the District of Columbia's state education agency, for its Direct Investment in Students grant competition. OSSE is seeking experienced K-12 education professionals who have served as grant reviewers for OSSE in the past.

Grant reviewers provide independent subject matter expertise to read, score, and comment on competitive grant applications submitted by local education agencies, schools, community-based organizations, and other eligible entities. All reviews are completed remotely in OSSE's online Enterprise Grants Management System (EGMS), and reviewer scores are used to recommend applications for funding. OSSE selects reviewers from the qualified pool and gives preference to reviewers who have satisfactorily completed reviews for its competitions in previous years.

Work Schedule

This is a remote, part-time assignment. Reviews are completed on your own schedule within each deadline. The approximate commitment for this competition is:

  • Orientation and EGMS training: a virtual webinar held approximately within two weeks of the engagement start date.
  • Review window: usually two weeks from the date applications are assigned, unless OSSE specifies otherwise.
  • Facilitated discussion (only if needed): a phone or video conference, usually about three business days after the scoring due date, held when panel scores differ significantly.
  • Approximate completion of reviewer work: November 6, 2026. Final dates are confirmed before orientation.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Complete OSSE's EGMS training and attend the virtual, grant-specific orientation webinar before reviewing any applications.
  2. Independently read and conduct a detailed review of each assigned application (typically two or more per competition) as one of three reviewers on an EGMS review panel, working remotely and separately.
  3. Apply K-12 education expertise to assess the quality, feasibility, and expected student impact of each applicant's proposed activities.
  4. Complete a fully scored rubric for every section of each application, applying the established scoring criteria consistently and objectively.
  5. Write clear, constructive comments describing strengths and weaknesses that justify and align with the scores given. Reviews may be shared with applicants on request, with reviewer names and contact information removed.
  6. Base all scores and comments only on the content of each applicant's submission in EGMS.
  7. Submit all scores and comments in EGMS by the review deadline, usually two weeks from receiving the applications.
  8. Participate in a facilitated panel discussion by phone or video conference when scores differ significantly, then submit a final rubric with updated scores and comments reflecting any changes.
  9. Disclose any conflict of interest with applicant organizations and do not review any application where a conflict exists.
  10. Direct EGMS technical questions to the EGMS manual, the resources at grants.osse.dc.gov, or the EGMS call center at (202) 719-6500, and direct questions about the grant or about scoring to OSSE grant program staff.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Past service as a competitive grant reviewer for OSSE.
  • Professional experience in K-12 education.
  • Reliable access to a computer, the internet, and a phone.
  • Availability for the full review process, including EGMS training, the orientation webinar, the complete review window, and a facilitated discussion if one is required.
  • No conflict of interest with any applicant organization in this competition, confirmed through a signed Conflict of Interest Form.
  • No unsatisfactory performance evaluation from past grant review work for OSSE or any other grant-making organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Satisfactory reviewer performance in OSSE's previous grant competitions.
  • Experience applying scoring rubrics and writing evidence-based reviewer comments.

Compensation

  • $150 per application successfully reviewed. Reviewers are typically assigned two or more applications per competition.
  • Payment is made only after OSSE verifies successful completion of the entire review process: EGMS training, the orientation webinar, timely review and rigorous scoring of every assigned application in EGMS, and, if required, participation in a facilitated discussion with final scores submitted.
  • Payment is issued by Dhaka Technologies Limited Company by direct deposit or check within 30 calendar days of OSSE's verification.
  • Failure to complete timely, high-quality reviews will affect payment and will disqualify a reviewer from future assignments.

How to Apply

Interested candidates who meet the qualifications should send their resume to with the job title in the email subject line. Your resume should show your degree and your experience in the field. Please also mention in your resume the grants you have reviewed previously, including the grant-making organization, the grant program, and the year. Qualified applicants will be asked to complete a Grant Reviewer Application and a Conflict of Interest Form before they are recommended to OSSE.

About CDMS

CDMS has helped California businesses stay compliant with environmental, health and safety (EHS) regulations for more than 35 years. Our clients are mostly manufacturers, metal finishers, warehouses and transportation companies with 15 to 300 employees. We run their compliance programs: hazardous materials and hazardous waste, stormwater, air permits, spill prevention, Cal/OSHA programs and employee training. Our field team works out of offices in Pleasanton (San Francisco Bay Area) and Long Beach (Los Angeles area), supported by a remote technical team.

The Role

We are hiring Remote EHS Project Managers to run the engine behind our clients' compliance programs: the planning, the regulatory work and the coordination that keep California factories and warehouses compliant and their people safe.

Our local EHS specialists and field staff in California work on site at client facilities: site visits, inspections, sampling and in-person training. You will do and manage everything that can be done remotely: the regulatory analysis, the filings and reports, the compliance calendars and the data. You will plan and coordinate the work our local EHS specialists and field staff perform, turn their field notes into finished deliverables, and make sure nothing a client owes a regulator is late.

This is a project management role with real technical depth. Client contact stays with our California team, and you run the work behind it: planning it, doing it and coordinating the people who do it in the field. Our Senior Project Managers handle knowledge management, project reviews and our most complex projects. You will work with them on reviews and help decide how our remote EHS work gets done. You will report to our CEO.

Why You Will Want This Job

  • You run real projects from your first months. You plan the work, do the technical analysis, coordinate the field team and deliver the finished product.
  • Your work has visible impact. The plans and filings you prepare keep chemicals stored safely, stormwater clean and workers trained at real facilities across California.
  • You will master some of the toughest EHS rules in the world. California's environmental and safety requirements are among the most demanding anywhere, and expertise in them is valued by employers everywhere.
  • Your ideas shape how we work. We are a close team of about 17 people. You work directly with our CEO and help design the templates, checklists and tools our remote practice runs on.
  • A tech-forward team. We use cloud software, AI tools and automation to cut repetitive work, and we want people who will push that further.
  • Stable, long-term work. Full time, paid twice a month in U.S. dollars, with a team that values continuity: members of our remote team have been with us for three years and counting.
  • Mentors who know the work. Our Senior Project Managers review your projects and share what they have learned from years of California compliance work.

What You Will Do

Manage remote project delivery

  • Keep track of each assigned client's permits, plans, deadlines and open items.
  • Build and run compliance calendars so every filing, renewal, inspection and training happens on time.
  • Prepare clear status updates and questions for the California team to take to clients.
  • Prepare client-ready deliverables and bring them to Senior Project Manager review.

Do the remote technical work

  • Prepare and update Hazardous Materials Business Plans in CERS (California Environmental Reporting System), including chemical inventories, site maps and emergency plans.
  • Prepare hazardous waste program documents and reports, and review manifests and records.
  • Prepare stormwater documents (SWPPPs, annual reports in SMARTS) and track sampling results against limits.
  • Prepare spill prevention (SPCC) plans, air permit applications and renewals, emissions calculations and recordkeeping.
  • Read regulations and agency guidance, and summarize what applies to a given facility.

Coordinate local EHS specialists and field staff

  • Plan and schedule site work with our local EHS specialists and field staff: what to inspect, collect and photograph. Assign their tasks, track them to completion and follow up on anything outstanding.
  • Turn field notes, photos and data into finished, client-ready reports.
  • Review drafts from junior and remote team members before they go to clients.

Run the projects

  • Scope tasks, track hours and budgets, and keep project records current in our project management system (Accelo).
  • Flag risks early: a slipping deadline, an agency notice, a scope change.
  • Improve how we work: templates, checklists, SOPs and automations that make the remote team faster and more accurate.

What You Bring

  • 5 or more years in EHS, environmental, engineering or quality assurance (QA/QC) roles that included regulatory or compliance work.
  • Project management experience: at least 2 years running projects with deadlines, budgets and several stakeholders.
  • Tech forward with strong data skills. You pick up new software fast and look for ways to automate repetitive work. You are advanced in Excel or Google Sheets (formulas, lookups, pivot tables) for chemical inventories, emissions calculations and sampling data, and comfortable using cloud tools and AI assistants for research, drafting and analysis.
  • Client service experience: you have supported external clients or internal customers and know what responsive, accurate service looks like.
  • Hands-on regulatory work: you have prepared permits, plans, regulatory reports, audits or compliance documentation yourself, for example EHS programs, environmental permits, ISO management systems or GMP/QA documentation.
  • Quick to learn new regulations. You can read a regulation you have never seen and work out what it requires of a specific facility. We will teach you the U.S. and California programs we work with.
  • A bachelor's degree in engineering (environmental, chemical, civil or industrial), environmental science, chemistry, industrial safety or a related field.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. You will write client-ready reports and work daily with our U.S. team.
  • Strong organization. You run many deadlines across many projects without dropping any.
  • A reliable home office: stable high-speed internet, a backup power or connection plan, a quiet space for video calls.

Nice to Have

  • Professional EHS credentials recognized in your country, such as an accredited pollution control, environmental or safety officer designation, or a professional license in engineering, chemistry or environmental planning
  • ISO 14001, ISO 45001 or ISO 9001 internal or lead auditor training
  • Experience with California systems such as CERS or SMARTS, or with California agencies (CUPAs, DTSC, Water Boards, Air Districts, Cal/OSHA)
  • Experience at a U.S. EHS consulting firm or supporting U.S. clients remotely
  • Experience supervising or reviewing the work of junior staff
  • Familiarity with project management or CRM tools (Accelo or similar), and with AutoCAD or GIS for site maps

Schedule, Location and Engagement

  • Location: fully remote, from your home country.
  • Hours: full time on California business hours, 8 am to 5 pm Pacific, Monday to Friday, with a lunch break from 12 noon to 1 pm Pacific. Depending on your time zone, this may mean working evening or overnight hours.
  • Engagement: full-time independent contractor, paid twice a month in U.S. dollars through Deel.
  • Tools: we provide accounts for the software you need, including Microsoft 365 and Accelo.
  • Travel: none required.

Pay and Benefits

  • Pay: $1,000 to $3,000 USD per month, depending on experience, paid twice a month through Deel.
  • Growth: hands-on experience across a wide range of California regulatory programs and industries.
  • Training: support for EHS certifications and continued education.

How to Apply

If you enjoy turning complex regulations into clear, finished work, and you like being the person who keeps a project moving, we would like to hear from you.

Apply with your resume and a short cover letter (under 200 words) describing one compliance program you managed from start to finish: what the regulation required, what you prepared and how you kept it on schedule.

After you apply, we will email you two short online assessments (about 20 minutes in total). Please complete them so we can move your application forward.

CDMS is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace.

Salary: $1,000-$3,000 USD per month

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

Senior Product Manager, Risk

As a Senior Product Manager on the Risk team within the Consumer & Business group, you'll own the product strategy and roadmap for how Coinbase detects, prevents, and responds to fraud, account takeover, and scam risk across our platform. This team builds the products and risk controls that protect millions of customers and billions in assets. You'll partner with Engineering, Data Science, and Risk Analytics to ship products that stay ahead of evolving threats while keeping the customer experience fast and frictionless.

What you'll do:

  • Own the product roadmap for one or more risk domains (e.g., ATO prevention, scam detection, payment fraud), defining the vision, priorities, and success metrics that reduce customer losses and improve detection accuracy
  • Drive cross-functional execution with Engineering, Data Science, and Design to ship risk products from concept through launch, making trade-offs between speed, coverage, and user experience
  • Partner with Risk Analytics and ML teams to translate fraud signals, model outputs, and emerging threat patterns into product requirements and control strategies
  • Lead experimentation and measurement of risk interventions, using data to quantify impact on fraud rates, false positive rates, and customer friction
  • Shape the long-term risk product strategy by analyzing industry trends, regulatory shifts, and crypto-specific threat vectors to keep Coinbase ahead of adversaries

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 7+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years focused on risk, fraud, trust and safety, or payments in a consumer fintech or e-commerce environment
  • Proven track record shipping risk or fraud products that measurably reduced loss rates, improved detection precision, or scaled risk controls across multiple product surfaces
  • Deep fluency in data-driven decision-making, including defining metrics, running experiments, and interpreting ML model performance to inform product direction
  • Experience partnering with engineering and data science teams to build and iterate on real-time risk systems, rules engines, or ML-powered detection pipelines
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex risk trade-offs to senior leadership, translating technical fraud concepts into clear business impact narratives
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

jobs.description:
Director / VP of Debt Enrollment Operations

Location: 100% Remote. However, relocation to Tampa, FL is expected once the operation is established.

Company / Opportunity

Our client is a large-scale performance marketing company currently generating and selling approximately 3,000 consumer debt leads per day to established debt relief companies.

Today, the company primarily monetizes these consumers by selling the lead to a debt company, which then handles the sales process and enrollment.

We are now looking to build our own internal debt enrollment operation.

The goal is to move from:

The Company generates lead sells leads to debt company

to:

The Company generates lead The Company contacts consumer The Company enrollment rep signs consumer enrollment is handed off/sold to debt relief partner

We are starting this operation from zero. We currently have no debt enrollment reps, call-center infrastructure, dialer, scripts, or enrollment management team.

We need an experienced debt industry operator who can come in and build and own the entire operation from the ground up.

What This Person Will Own

This is not a role for someone who has simply supervised an existing sales team. We need someone who has previously built, launched, scaled, and managed a debt enrollment floor and understands the entire operation end-to-end.

They will be responsible for:

  • Designing the debt enrollment operation from scratch.
  • Determining initial staffing requirements based on our lead volume.
  • Recruiting and hiring the first team of experienced debt enrollment reps.
  • Building a repeatable recruiting pipeline as the operation scales.
  • Designing rep compensation plans, quotas, KPIs and performance standards.
  • Working directly with our debt relief partner(s) to get the team trained and certified on their enrollment process.
  • Developing the day-to-day sales process from lead receipt through signed enrollment and partner handoff.
  • Selecting and implementing the appropriate dialer, CRM, phone system, lead-routing technology, reporting and other call-center technology.
  • Understanding lead distribution and capacity planning — e.g. how many fresh leads each rep can effectively work per day and how many reps are required at different lead volumes.
  • Establishing dialing cadence, follow-up sequences, callbacks and lead-aging strategy.
  • Building scripts, objection handling, coaching and sales-training processes.
  • Establishing QA, call monitoring and performance-management systems.
  • Managing contact rate, qualification rate, enrollment conversion, average enrolled debt, first-payment rate and other critical funnel KPIs.
  • Identifying bottlenecks and continuously improving unit economics.
  • Building management layers as the team grows: team leads, trainers, QA, etc.
  • Ultimately owning the P&L and performance of Isla's debt enrollment business.

Candidate Requirements

Must have direct debt settlement / debt relief enrollment experience.

Comparable large debt enrollment organizations are acceptable, but we specifically want someone coming from the debt settlement industry, not a general call-center executive.

Candidate should have:

  • Personally managed a debt enrollment sales floor.
  • Experience taking an enrollment operation from early stage to meaningful scale, or played a senior role in building one from the ground up.
  • Proven ability to recruit and hire successful debt enrollment reps.
  • Experience training and developing enrollment reps.
  • Deep understanding of debt settlement sales funnels and KPIs.
  • Strong understanding of dialers, CRMs, lead routing, call-center reporting and the technology required to operate a high-volume enrollment floor.
  • Experience managing high-volume inbound and/or outbound consumer leads.
  • Ability to determine appropriate lead-to-rep ratios and staffing requirements.
  • Experience designing sales compensation plans.
  • Strong understanding of QA/compliance requirements within debt enrollment.
  • Ability to manage both strategy and execution — this person needs to be willing to personally build the operation before eventually managing a larger leadership team.
  • Strong analytical/P&L orientation. We want someone who thinks in terms of CAC, conversion rate, enrolled debt, revenue per lead, revenue per rep and contribution margin, not simply call-center activity metrics.
