jobs.description:
See something that should exist? Build it.
See a better way? Do it.

At Terrific, every role directly impacts how we grow from product to revenue to customer experience. We’re building the next generation of social commerce through live shopping powered by real-time data and AI.

And we believe customer data should belong to the brands who earn it — not third-party platforms.

Terrific is hiring Account Executives to work remotely from multiple locations to help shape the future of social commerce.

The Role

    We are hiring a builder to own and close revenue across mid-market and enterprise customers. We have strong product momentum and market interest. Now we need someone who can turn that into consistent, high-quality deals.

    This role exists to drive new business while helping define how Terrific sells.

    This is not a maintenance role. This is a creation role.

What You Will Build

    You will help define and execute Terrific’s go-to-market motion across mid-market and enterprise.

    Your work will directly shape:

    • How we position Terrific to different customer segments

    • How we run discovery and uncover real business needs

    • How we move deals efficiently from first conversation to close

    • How we expand accounts and drive long-term value

    • How Terrific wins in competitive sales cycles

      • You’ll help build the messaging, sales approach, and deal strategy that drives revenue.

What You Will Own

    You will own the full sales cycle end-to-end:

    Pipeline → Discovery → Solution → Close → Expansion

    Revenue Ownership

    • Own a pipeline of mid-market and enterprise opportunities

    • Run full-cycle sales from first meeting through close

    • Consistently meet or exceed revenue targets

    • Manage deal strategy, negotiation, and closing

      • Sales Execution

      • Lead high-quality discovery conversations with decision-makers

      • Translate customer needs into tailored solutions

      • Run product demos and articulate clear business value

      • Navigate multi-stakeholder sales cycles

        • Pipeline Generation (with support)

        • Partner with SDR/marketing/product to build pipeline

        • Proactively source and develop new opportunities when needed

        • Maintain strong pipeline hygiene and forecasting accuracy

          • Product & Feedback Loop

          • Act as the voice of the customer internally

          • Provide feedback to Product and Engineering on gaps and opportunities

          • Help refine positioning based on real market conversations

            • Expansion & Account Growth

            • Identify upsell and expansion opportunities

            • Build strong relationships with customers post-close

            • Drive long-term revenue growth within accounts

              • You will have real ownership and autonomy.

Who You Are

    You are a strong closer who understands how to run thoughtful, structured sales processes while adapting to a fast-moving product and market.

    Requirements

    • 4–8+ years in SaaS sales (closing role)

    • Experience selling to mid-market and/or enterprise customers

    • Proven track record of meeting or exceeding quota

    • Strong discovery, qualification, and deal management skills

    • Ability to run complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

    • High ownership and ability to operate independently

      • Nice to Have

      • Experience selling into eCommerce, media, or digital platforms

      • Experience with PLG or product-led sales environments

      • Familiarity with tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, Gong, or similar

      • Experience selling technical or data-driven products

Why This Role Matters

    You won’t inherit a rigid sales playbook.

    You’ll help define how Terrific sells.

    Your work will directly impact revenue, product direction, and how we scale.

Why Terrific?

    Terrific is a focused, execution-driven company where strong operators have direct impact.

    You’ll work closely with leadership to shape how we grow.

    We move fast, operate with high ownership, and value people who build.

    Please note: We review every application carefully. While we may not be able to respond to everyone, we will reach out to candidates whose experience aligns with what we’re building.

Required:
  • Deep experience in at least one of Terrific’s three commercial pillars — eCommerce, Marketing, or Media — and enough fluency across the other two to contribute credibly from day 1.
  • Terrific operates as a global company, and English is our primary business language. As such, all roles require fluency in written and spoken English.
Be part of the change that’s quietly reshaping how people discover and buy online.
Passionate about social media and e-commerce? Come build what’s next at Terrific.
Please note: We review every application carefully. While we may not be able to respond to everyone, we will reach out to candidates whose experience aligns with what we’re building.

jobs.title: Global Controller
jobs.excerpt: About Splash Splash is an international development organization founded in 2007 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, USA.
jobs.description:
About Splash

Splash is an international development organization founded in 2007 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, USA. Splash supports local leaders, institutions, and partners to drive lasting change on the ground. We believe local capacity to solve problems at scale exists, and our role is to strategically support and magnify the impact of local governments, nonprofit and for-profit actors for the good of children and families in the cities where we work.

Our core values guide everything we do, including every hiring decision. They are:

  • People — People first. People second. People third.
  • Quality — Beautiful products that function and last.
  • Honesty — No drama, no surprises, no BS.
  • Joy — Kids at heart, seeing potential everywhere.
  • Mistakes — Make them, don’t repeat them.

Splash values the unique skills and experiences everyone brings to the organization and is committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment. Splash provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants.

The Job

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States, preferably on the East Coast. The Global Controller leads Splash’s global accounting operations and maintains the accounting standards, close processes, reporting controls, and financial systems needed to produce accurate, timely, and consistent financial information across the US headquarters and country offices in Ethiopia, Malawi, and Zambia.

Position Overview

Reporting to the CFO, the Global Controller is accountable for the integrity of Splash’s accounting records and financial reporting. The role directly oversees the Country Finance Officers and sets consistent global expectations for general ledger management, month-end close, reconciliations, grant accounting, revenue recognition, financial controls, audit readiness, and statutory reporting oversight. The Global Controller partners with country directors, program and operations colleagues, and the global finance team to ensure that financial transactions are recorded accurately, supported by appropriate documentation, and handled in accordance with applicable accounting standards, donor agreements, organizational policies, and local requirements.

The Global Controller focuses on accounting integrity, financial reporting, and control. Organization-wide budgeting, forecasting, portfolio financial analysis, and forward-looking financial performance management are owned by the CFO and the FP&A/Grants Finance function.

Roles and Responsibilities

Global Accounting and Month-End Close

  • Lead the global accounting close process and establish a common close calendar, standard country close packages, and clear deadlines for the US and country offices.
  • Oversee general ledger integrity, chart-of-accounts consistency, journal entries, accruals, prepayments, allocations, foreign-currency accounting, interoffice balances, and period-end adjustments.
  • Consolidate and review country-level financial results, investigate unusual balances and variances relevant to accounting integrity, and ensure that material issues are resolved or escalated promptly.
  • Maintain accounting policies and procedures consistent with the applicable US GAAP framework, relevant donor requirements, and Splash’s legal and organizational structure.
  • Lead the preparation of accurate, complete, and timely financial statements and supporting schedules for management, auditors, and other authorized stakeholders.

Direct Oversight of country finance staff

  • Directly manage and develop the country finance team in Ethiopia, Malawi, and Zambia, setting clear expectations for performance, deadlines, documentation, and internal controls.
  • Establish consistent global accounting procedures while ensuring that country processes address applicable local tax, payroll, banking, statutory, and regulatory requirements.
  • Review country close packages, reconciliations, grant ledgers, accounts payable and receivable schedules, payroll reconciliations, fixed-asset records, and compliance calendars.
  • Partner with country directors and local teams to resolve accounting issues, strengthen financial processes, and clarify the distinction between operational budget ownership and finance control responsibilities.
  • Build continuity across country offices through documented procedures, cross-training, designated backups, and structured handovers for critical finance processes.

Grant Accounting, Revenue Recognition, and Cost Allocation

  • Oversee grant accounting methodology and ensure that grant transactions are coded consistently and can be reconciled to the general ledger, approved budgets, donor reports, and supporting documentation.
  • Evaluate and document accounting treatment for grants and contributions, including revenue recognition, advances, deferred or refundable balances where applicable, donor restrictions, receivables, and grant closeout.
  • Maintain consistent cost-allocation methodologies and ensure that shared costs are supported, applied consistently, and treated in accordance with applicable grant terms and cost principles.
  • Review grant financial report reconciliations for accounting accuracy and completeness; coordinate with the FP&A/Grants Finance Manager on reporting schedules, financial assumptions, and timely resolution of discrepancies.
  • Maintain accounting support and records needed for indirect-cost rate submissions, including a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) where applicable, in coordination with the CFO and relevant colleagues.
  • Monitor accounting compliance with applicable US government award requirements and other donor rules relevant to Splash’s funding agreements; escalate ambiguous or high-risk matters to the CFO and obtain specialist advice where appropriate.

Financial Controls, Treasury Accounting, and Risk

  • Oversee the design and consistent application of internal financial controls across headquarters and country offices, including transaction authorization, segregation of duties, journal approvals, bank reconciliations, vendor controls, and financial-system access.
  • Ensure that bank and balance-sheet reconciliations are completed, independently reviewed, supported, and resolved within established deadlines.
  • Oversee accounting processes for accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, fixed assets, inventory where applicable, cash, and interoffice transactions.
  • Coordinate with the CFO on the accounting and reporting of cash, restricted funds, and unrestricted resources; provide accurate reconciled information to support liquidity oversight.
  • Identify control weaknesses, document exceptions, recommend corrective actions, and track remediation to completion.
  • Ensure that financial records and supporting documents are maintained in a secure, organized, and retrievable manner in accordance with organizational retention requirements and donor obligations.

Audit, Statutory Reporting, and Compliance

  • Coordinate the financial statement audit and relevant grant, country, and entity audits, working with the CFO, external auditors, country teams, and local advisers.
  • Prepare and review audit schedules, reconciliations, confirmations, and supporting documentation; track audit requests, findings, management responses, and corrective actions.
  • Maintain a consolidated calendar of statutory filings, tax and payroll remittances, and other financial compliance deadlines, with named country owners and escalation procedures.
  • Coordinate with qualified local accounting, tax, and legal advisers when country-specific requirements exceed the expertise or authority of the internal finance team.
  • Support the CFO in responding to internal control reviews, donor inquiries, and other financial compliance requests.

Financial Systems, Procedures, and Staff Capacity

  • Own accounting-process standards and the accounting requirements for Splash’s financial systems, including Sage Intacct, chart-of-accounts structure, dimensions, user roles, and reporting outputs.
  • Maintain and improve standard operating procedures, close checklists, reconciliation templates, journal-entry controls, and country reporting packages.
  • Review accounting workflows and recommend practical improvements that reduce manual effort, strengthen controls, and improve data quality without creating unnecessary administrative burden.
  • Provide accounting guidance and training to Country Finance Officers and non-finance colleagues on financial policies, documentation, coding, approvals, and compliance responsibilities.
  • Translate technical accounting requirements into clear instructions and practical tools that colleagues across countries and functions can follow.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting is required.
  • At least 10 years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 3 years in a Controller or equivalent senior accounting leadership role. This experience threshold is intended to ensure the candidate has both hands-on accounting depth and demonstrated ownership of close, reporting, and control outcomes.
  • Prior Controller experience in a nonprofit organization is required.
  • Experience overseeing accounting across multiple countries is required, including coordination with country-based finance staff and familiarity with different local compliance environments.
  • International nonprofit grant accounting experience is required, including grant coding, cost allocation, donor financial reporting, audit support, and interpretation of grant terms and donor cost requirements.
  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience using Sage Intacct is required.
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and internal controls; experience with US government awards and other institutional donor requirements is strongly preferred.
  • Experience leading or coordinating multi-country month-end close, consolidated reporting, balance-sheet reconciliations, external audits, and statutory compliance oversight.
  • Ability to communicate technical accounting matters clearly to finance and non-finance colleagues across cultures and time zones.
  • Strong judgment, attention to detail, organization, follow-through, and the ability to prioritize competing deadlines in a lean, distributed team.
  • Commitment to collaborative leadership, continuous improvement, transparent communication, and Splash’s mission and values.

Preferred

·CPA license is preferred.

The Ideal Candidate

  • You are a technically strong accounting leader who combines sound judgment with a practical, service-oriented approach.
  • You value accuracy, reliable processes, and clear accountability, and you know how to establish consistent standards without losing sight of country context.
  • You develop people through clear expectations, useful feedback, coaching, and documented processes that strengthen team independence.
  • You communicate directly and respectfully, surface risks early, and work constructively with colleagues across countries, functions, and time zones.
  • You are comfortable improving systems and workflows in a changing organization and can balance attention to detail with a broader view of organizational risk.
  • You appreciate data-driven decision-making, welcome constructive feedback, and help build a culture in which mistakes are addressed transparently and not repeated.
  • You thrive in a workplace culture that is playfully professional.

Benefits

  • The salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000, in line with experience.
  • Splash operates across time zones with flexible work schedules. Team members can set standard hours within their time zone and should be available for occasional off-hours work, balanced with a self-managed schedule.
  • Benefits include 18 days of paid time off, increasing by 2 days each year up to 28 days; 11 paid holidays; Wellness Fridays with reduced hours; two weeks of paid time off mid-year during July 4th week and the last week of the year; medical, dental, and vision insurance; and a 401(k) plan with a 3% match.
  • Benefits are subject to current organizational policies and plan terms.

React Developer – Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: React Developer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)

Experience Required: 5+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

This role focuses on building highly responsive, scalable, and maintainable Single Page Applications (SPAs) using React while integrating seamlessly with enterprise APIs, cloud services, and microservices-based backend platforms.
You will collaborate closely with product managers, UX/UI designers, backend engineers, cloud architects, QA teams, and DevOps engineers to deliver exceptional user experiences across large-scale enterprise applications. Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with OpenAPI (Swagger), GraphQL, Apollo Client, and API Gateway integrations.

Project Environment
You will be joining a digital engineering team responsible for modernizing enterprise applications and delivering cloud-native customer experiences. Current initiatives include:

This is a hands-on engineering role where you will contribute to front-end architecture, UI development, API integration, testing, performance optimization, cloud deployments, and continuous enhancement of mission-critical enterprise applications.

jobs.description:
Overview: The Service Delivery Manager is a senior operations position providing leadership for rotational team and collaborate with duty managers supporting 100+ clients on a rotating shift pattern, responsible for the efficient and professional execution of activities associated with providing an exceptional level of hospitality for clients' mission-critical systems. The Service Delivery Manager also serves as the accountable owner of Change Management governance for the entire business unit under the Altera Cloud Operations Change Management Process (v2.1) — chairing the Technical Review Board (TRB), overseeing implementation and validation, and holding final closure authority across all towers and shifts.

Change Implementation, Validation & Closure

  • Facilitate TRB meeting for change reviews across cloud BU.
  • Staff and lead the Hosting Response Bridge (HRB), providing 24x7 monitoring across the post-change stability window; trigger swarms the moment an anomaly is detected.
  • Enforce alert-suppression discipline and confirm pre-change baseline capture and post-change comparison before closure.
  • Oversee validation against Validation Test Library pass/fail criteria and evidence — including mandatory application and technical validation for production changes.
  • Hold final closure authority: confirm the 24-hour or TRB approved closure window with HRB observation if the change was clean and evidence is complete before authorizing closure; refuse closure otherwise.
  • Invoke rollback directly against a pre-agreed trigger without further approval; escalate exceptions to the Tower Leader.
  • Carry open items into shift handover with clear owners so closure is never missed across a shift boundary.

Operational Leadership & Incident Management

  • Major incident / critical issue early detection and fast remediation for all matters during their shift.
  • Ensure all client requests, incidents, and problems are addressed in a timely and professional manner.
  • Run stand-up calls with their team, managing proper hand-over of activities and client status between shifts and teams.
  • Allocate resources as necessary across teams to provide efficient, effective resolution of issues.
  • Identify and implement operational process improvements across teams.
  • Assist Shift Site Reliability Engineers with client communication and escalations.
  • Drive results through agreed KPIs for alerts, monitoring tools, and case/ServiceNow (SNOW) metrics.

TRB Ownership & Change Process Governance

  • Chair the Technical Review Board: the final gate reviewing risk classification, architectural impact, rollback adequacy, and monitoring plan for every change; approve, send back for rework, or escalate.
  • Pre-agree and record rollback triggers at TRB, each with a maximum time-to-decide.

Job Description

Purpose of the role

To identify potential vulnerabilities within the banks IT systems using penetration testing tools and techniques to ensure security of computer systems, applications, servers, and networks.

Accountabilities

  • Collaboration with stakeholders to understand their security requirements and controls in business processes, application/services, to enhance overall security posture and assurance.
  • Identification of emerging vulnerabilities, exploit codes and cyber-attacks to develop testing methodologies and assurance activities.

Vice President Expectations

  • To contribute or set strategy, drive requirements and make recommendations for change. Plan resources, budgets, and policies; manage and maintain policies/ processes; deliver continuous improvements and escalate breaches of policies/procedures..
  • If managing a team, they define jobs and responsibilities, planning for the department’s future needs and operations, counselling employees on performance and contributing to employee pay decisions/changes. They may also lead a number of specialists to influence the operations of a department, in alignment with strategic as well as tactical priorities, while balancing short and long term goals and ensuring that budgets and schedules meet corporate requirements..
  • If the position has leadership responsibilities, People Leaders are expected to demonstrate a clear set of leadership behaviours to create an environment for colleagues to thrive and deliver to a consistently excellent standard. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others..
  • OR for an individual contributor, they will be a subject matter expert within own discipline and will guide technical direction. They will lead collaborative, multi-year assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will train, guide and coach less experienced specialists and provide information affecting long term profits, organisational risks and strategic decisions..
  • Advise key stakeholders, including functional leadership teams and senior management on functional and cross functional areas of impact and alignment.
  • Manage and mitigate risks through assessment, in support of the control and governance agenda.
  • Demonstrate leadership and accountability for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work your team does.
  • Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the organisation functions to contribute to achieving the goals of the business.
  • Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies.
  • Create solutions based on sophisticated analytical thought comparing and selecting complex alternatives. In-depth analysis with interpretative thinking will be required to define problems and develop innovative solutions.
  • Adopt and include the outcomes of extensive research in problem solving processes.
  • Seek out, build and maintain trusting relationships and partnerships with internal and external stakeholders in order to accomplish key business objectives, using influencing and negotiating skills to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

We’re looking for a Senior Red Team Operator to join a skilled, close-knit team that genuinely loves this work. You’ll plan and lead full-scope Red Team operations – cyber, physical, social engineering, and everything in between – emulating real-world adversaries to test how our defences actually hold up under pressure. When you find the gaps, you’ll help close them.

This is a hands-on role for someone who’s happiest with a shell, a payload, and a hard target. You’ll have real autonomy over how you approach engagements, time to research new tradecraft, and a team of talented operators who’ll look to you to set the technical standard, pressure-test their thinking, and lead from the front.

What you’ll be doing

  • Scoping and leading full-scope Red Team engagements against well-defined adversarial objectives across cyber, physical, social engineering, and process attack surfaces.
  • Leading on methodology: shaping how the team scopes, runs and reports engagements and driving continuous improvement in how you all operate.
  • Designing and delivering phishing and social engineering campaigns end to end – standing up the supporting infrastructure (domains, redirectors, mail and landing-page servers), crafting convincing pretexts, and developing the accompanying payloads to emulate realistic threat-actor delivery.
  • Operating and tuning Command and Control frameworks (e.g. Cobalt Strike, Nighthawk, or equivalent) through initial access, post-exploitation, and lateral movement.
  • Developing custom tooling, tradecraft, and EDR / defence-evasion techniques to emulate realistic threat actors.
  • Turning engagements into clear, compelling attack narratives – the kind that land with both the engineers who’ll fix the issues and the executives who need to understand the risk.
  • Contributing to detection and resilience improvements through close collaboration with defensive teams.
  • Researching emerging TTPs. Threats, and tooling, and bringing new techniques into the team’s methodology.
  • Setting the technical bar and mentoring across the team – coaching operators, reviewing tradecraft, and helping develop the next generation of Red Team talent.

Some other highly valued skills may include:

The Product Stewardship Solution Engineer is a client-facing, pre-sales role that partners closely with the Sales team to understand prospective customers’ business and technical needs and demonstrate how Sphera’s solutions can address their challenges. The Solution Engineer plays a critical role throughout the sales cycle from discovery and value assessment through solution demonstration, proposal development, and transition to implementation.

The role requires strong domain expertise in Product Stewardship, regulatory compliance, and data management, combined with the ability to engage confidently with both technical and senior business stakeholders. The Solution Engineer serves as a trusted advisor to prospective customers, helping them understand the value of Sphera’s solutions and build compelling business cases for investment.

Responsibilities

  • Act as a client-facing subject matter expert throughout the sales process, building trusted relationships with prospective customers and serving as a strategic advisor on Product Stewardship and regulatory compliance solutions.
  • Participate in discovery meetings with prospective customers to understand their business objectives, current technical environment, challenges, requirements, and future needs.
  • Analyze customer requirements and determine how effectively Sphera’s solutions can address their needs, while identifying potential solution gaps and opportunities.
  • Conduct and/or participate in Vision Alignment, Value Assessment, and Business Operations workshops to identify customer pain points, desired business outcomes, expected ROI, and the overall value of Sphera’s solutions.
  • Deliver compelling, tailored software demonstrations and technical presentations to prospective customers, including Product Stewardship professionals, IT teams, and senior executives.
  • Partner with Account Executives and Sales Managers to develop effective strategies for advancing and winning sales opportunities.
  • Guide sales opportunities through the Sphera sales process, ensuring appropriate best practices, methodologies, and documentation are followed.
  • Support prospective customers in developing internal business cases and building the justification for investment in Sphera solutions.
  • Lead or support the development of responses to customer RFIs and RFPs, providing thorough and well-written responses to functional and technical requirements.
  • Maintain a strong and current knowledge of Sphera’s Product Stewardship solutions, capabilities, roadmap, and value proposition.
  • Maintain strong knowledge of Product Stewardship, regulatory compliance, and data management, staying current through industry publications, regulatory updates, conferences, and other relevant sources.
  • Maintain knowledge of competitive solutions, including their technical strengths, weaknesses, positioning, and potential competitive strategies.
  • Partner with Product Management to communicate customer and market feedback and help inform future product enhancements and development priorities.
  • Partner with Services and Implementation teams to transition discovery findings, customer requirements, solution design, and other relevant information to support a successful implementation and customer experience.
  • Support marketing initiatives by participating in webinars, contributing to industry publications, presenting at conferences, and serving as a subject matter expert representing Sphera.
  • Contribute to achieving monthly, quarterly, and annual sales objectives by helping Sales teams effectively position, demonstrate, and close Sphera solutions.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience implementing, using, supporting, or selling enterprise data management or software solutions, preferably within Product Stewardship or regulatory compliance.
  • Demonstrated domain knowledge in Product Stewardship, environmental compliance, regulatory compliance, data management, and/or enterprise software.
  • Experience working in a client-facing, consulting, pre-sales, solution consulting, or solution engineering environment.
  • Strong experience presenting and communicating with a range of audiences, from Product Stewardship and IT professionals to senior business leaders and executives.

  • 2+ years of experience developing, analyzing, and responding to software RFPs/RFIs.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts and regulatory requirements into clear business value for customers.

Specialized Knowledge & Skills

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, planning, and presentation development skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

jobs.description:
About Sharesource:

We are a BCorp company whose purpose is to democratise opportunities for individuals from developing countries. With our brand and culture empowering our partners to attract and keep the most qualified members, we share the knowledge to unleash potential and grow scaling teams for Australian and Canadian businesses.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for an experienced and detail-oriented Accountant to support month-end reporting, reconciliations, financial reporting, payroll, and day-to-day accounting operations.

The ideal candidate will have strong Australian accounting knowledge, advanced Excel skills, and the ability to analyse financial data, maintain accurate records, and support compliance and financial decision-making.

What are you expected to do?

  • Manage and support month-end closing and financial reporting processes.

  • Prepare and review journals, accruals, prepayments, and account reconciliations.

  • Maintain the accuracy and integrity of the general ledger and ensure transactions are correctly recorded.

  • Prepare and analyse monthly financial and management reports.

  • Review revenue, expenditure, balance sheet movements, and financial variances, providing explanations where required.

  • Monitor cash flow and assist with cash flow forecasting and planning.

  • Assist with annual budgeting, forecasting, and ongoing variance analysis.

  • Provide financial information and analysis to assist management with business and financial decisions.

  • Support Accounts Payable (AP) and Accounts Receivable (AR) processes.

  • Perform and review bank reconciliations, identifying and resolving discrepancies.

  • Process fortnightly payroll and payroll-related reconciliations.

  • Assist with BAS, GST, year-end reporting, and other statutory and financial compliance requirements.

  • Reconcile home care funding, claims, client contributions, and Support at Home (SAH) financial transactions.

  • Prepare and review weekly payment batches and expense reimbursements.

  • Maintain effective financial controls, procedures, and supporting documentation.

  • Assist with external accountants, auditors, and other financial reporting requirements.

  • Review finance processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and automation.

  • Provide support and guidance across the broader Finance and Accounts function as required.

You'll be a great fit if:

  • You have 3–5+ years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in an Accountant or similar role.

  • You have a tertiary qualification in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.

  • You have demonstrated experience with month-end close, financial reporting, general ledger, reconciliations, and financial analysis.

  • You have a strong understanding of Australian accounting standards, GST, BAS, and taxation requirements.

  • You have experience managing or supporting AP, AR, payroll, and general accounting functions.
  • You have advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, data analysis, reconciliations, reporting, and spreadsheet management.
  • You are proficient in Xero and confident working with other accounting and financial systems.
  • You have a strong understanding of financial controls and reconciliation processes.
  • You have excellent attention to detail and accuracy, particularly when handling large volumes of financial data.
  • You have strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify discrepancies and investigate issues independently.
  • You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • You have a proactive, reliable, and solutions-focused approach and can work independently and collaboratively.

It would be desirable if:

  • You have a CPA qualification (not required).

  • You have experience in home care, aged care, healthcare, disability, or community services, particularly in a government-funded environment.

What you gain beyond the role:

  • Remote + Hybrid Flexibility: Enjoy the best of both worlds—collaborative office days when it counts, balanced with the freedom to work from home.
  • Achieve Work-Life Balance and Flexibility: Work in an environment where you're trusted and empowered to work independently, while still having the support you need to deliver your best. Here, flexibility isn't just a perk—it's how we help you perform at your best, without sacrificing life outside of work.
  • Open Culture: Your voice matters, we encourage proactive communication and fresh ideas.
  • Supportive Team: From your very first day to every career milestone, we've got your back—with long-term growth and projects you can truly thrive in.

  • Learn and Grow: Training, coaching, and international opportunities to level up your skills and career

  • Be part of a B-Corp company that puts people and planet first while creating meaningful impact.

Please note: This role is remote; however, we require candidates to be based locally in the Philippines. This is to support occasional onsite activities such as team events, client meetings, or equipment handover. Additionally, local residency is necessary for compliance with Philippines labor laws and employment regulations.

Why work for Sharesource?

Our clients come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire hundreds of skillful individuals from a wide variety of backgrounds, genders, ages, and personalities to live out our diverse culture and make a positive impact on the world!

Our 5 Values:

  • Make a social impact: We balance our work for client teams and for society by constantly making a positive impact.

  • Be proactive: We encourage brave thinking and continuous improvement, and drive change through action.

  • Create value: We create measurable values for our stakeholders: our teams, partners, suppliers, investors, and communities.
  • Be fair, open and honest: We foster equality and inclusivity in a supportive environment that embraces diversity and celebrates achievements.

  • Add fun, passion and love: We prioritise fun and passion, fostering higher engagement and a positive can-do attitude.

What to Expect in the Process?

  1. You'll go through 3–4 interviews plus a possible assessment with our client partner. This includes an initial chat, a culture-fit interview, and 1–2 conversations with our awesome client. The whole process usually takes 1–2 weeks, but we'll let you know if things need to move quicker.
  2. Our best advice? Be yourself and enjoy the conversations. We'll keep you updated every step of the way, and you're always welcome to reach out for updates anytime.
  3. If all goes well, we'll complete reference checks and requirements quickly—so we can get that job offer to you without delay.

We would be grateful if you have these already:

  • Fit to Work/Health Card (Basic 5 employment medical tests)

  • NBI Clearance

  • Social IDs - PHIC, SSS, HDMF, TIN

  • Character references with contact info

At Sharesource, we believe in the value of diversity and inclusion. We are committed to creating a diverse, respectful, and inclusive workplace, and we do not discriminate based on factors such as race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, or disability.

Job Description:

The Committee Engagement Specialist is responsible for the day-to-day management and facilitation of Safety and Compliance Committee(s) operations, with a primary focus on maintaining accurate and up-to-date committee rosters, maintaining thorough record-keeping, and coordinating effectively with internal and external stakeholders. This role supports the integrity of committee activities by tracking and managing member appointments, overseeing onboarding processes, maintaining conflict-of-interest (COI) records, and ensuring alignment with OPTN governance and HRSA oversight requirements.


Reporting to the Director of Membership or the designated supervisor, this position maintains the accuracy of committee rosters, tracks member training completion, maintains detailed records to support compliance with governance and oversight standards, and facilitates the availability of resources to support committee functions. The Committee Engagement Specialist must excel in data management, attention to detail, and collaboration with stakeholders to ensure the seamless execution of membership processes.

Key Responsibilities

1. Committee Membership Management

  • Maintain accurate, current, and transparent records of Safety and Compliance Committee(s) membership, including member roles, appointment timelines, affiliations, contact information, and training status.
  • Execute the appointment and onboarding process for new committee members, ensuring timely assignment of roles and subcommittee responsibilities.
  • Track annual orientation and training status for all committee members to ensure compliance with governance requirements.
  • Develop and maintain a Conflict of Interest (COI) tracking log, monitoring and addressing potential conflicts for committee members and participants.
  • Collaborate with HRSA, OPTN contractors, and internal teams to ensure alignment and continuity of committee operations.

2. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) Implementation

  • Facilitate the execution of the Appointment and Roster Draft Plan by adhering to SOPs for:
    • Monitoring and updating committee membership rosters.
    • Coordinating with contractors and stakeholders to support committee operations.
    • Submitting updated rosters and related documentation within specified timeframes.
    • Maintaining detailed records of processes, authority boundaries, and roles in committee-related activities.
  • Support updates to SOPs based on internal feedback or COR requests, ensuring alignment with organizational and governance standards.

3. Subject Matter Expertise Coordination

  • Facilitate the availability and access to a pool of HRSA-approved Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) with specialized knowledge in areas such as patient safety, risk management, healthcare analytics, transplant medicine, and quality assurance.
  • Implement procedures for selecting, maintaining, and rapidly deploying SMEs to support site visits, incident reviews, or other committee functions.
  • Track and document SME involvement, including expertise type, hours used, request sources, and outputs delivered.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to address ad hoc expertise requests, ensuring timely and accurate responses.

4. Data Management and Reporting

  • Provide ongoing access to committee records, data, trackers, dashboards, and SOP documentation to the COR and relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure transparent and accurate reporting of committee membership activities, including rosters, training status updates, and COI logs.
  • Submit reports and deliverables in formats and timeframes required by the Appointment and Roster Draft Plan and Subject Matter Expertise Draft Plan.

5. Committee Coordination and Support

  • Collaborate with other entities supporting the OPTN to enable the execution of committee-related processes.
  • Track changes to committee membership and notify the COR of updates within one business day.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for committee meetings, member communications, and related activities.
  • Facilitate alignment with the approved OPTN Patient Safety and Compliance Operations Plan, ensuring all contractor support procedures are implemented effectively.

Qualifications

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, healthcare management, public policy, or a related field.

Experience:

  • At least 5 years of experience in roles involving policy compliance, operational coordination, healthcare processes, or committee/board management.
  • Experience with maintaining accurate records, managing workflows, and coordinating among multiple stakeholders.

Skills and Knowledge:

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage complex workflows and meet deadlines.
  • Knowledge of healthcare operations, compliance standards, or governance processes preferred.
  • Proficiency in office productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite) and data tracking systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing reports, facilitating stakeholder interaction, and supporting governance activities.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams, including contractors, government stakeholders, and committee members.

Get to Know the Opportunity:

The Product Delivery Director is a senior business-facing leader accountable for shaping, prioritizing, and guiding the delivery of Employee Benefits technology capabilities. This role represents the business strategy and operational perspective across cross-functional delivery teams, helping ensure solutions align with business objectives, customer needs, compliance expectations, and operational efficiency goals.

The ideal candidate brings strong business product ownership, delivery management, FINEOS expertise, and stakeholder leadership experience, with the ability to translate business priorities into actionable delivery plans. This leader will influence roadmap decisions, drive prioritization, prepare business teams for change, and support successful adoption of solutions across Employee Benefits products.

This role also serves as the business product owner for claims metrics and reporting, setting the strategy and building the function as a service across operational, leadership, and external-facing reporting views. The leader translates business requirements into a comprehensive reporting suite and connects claims metrics to actionable operational outcomes in partnership with Underwriting, Pricing, and Actuarial teams.

  • Proven ability to translate business requirements into a full suite of operational reports, with experience defining and delivering external-facing reports.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate claims metrics into operational outcomes and partner effectively with Underwriting, Pricing, and Actuarial teams on reporting needs, analysis, and business implications.
  • Experience operating in Agile and Scrum delivery environments as a business partner, product representative, or business product owner.
  • Strong understanding of SDLC, release management, and testing methodologies from a business delivery and stakeholder readiness perspective.
  • Demonstrated experience leading operational readiness, change adoption, training coordination, stakeholder communications, hypercare, and post-launch stabilization for business solutions.
  • Experience within Employee Benefits, Disability, Absence, Leave Management, Life, and/or Supplemental Health.

Preferred Knowledge & Experience:

  • Experience partnering with IT Product Owners and cross-functional technology teams while representing business priorities and operational needs.

  • Experience supporting digital transformation, modernization, and business capability improvement initiatives.
  • Knowledge of accessibility, usability, and digital experience best practices.

Voya’s Core Four reflect how we deliver for our customers, our business, and one another. In this role, you’ll bring them to life through thoughtful product leadership, disciplined delivery, and strong cross-functional partnership.

  • Instill Customer Obsession: Shape and prioritize Employee Benefits capabilities using customer, employer, and operational needs to improve experiences and business outcomes.
  • Transform with Automation/AI: Help advance digital capabilities and modernization by identifying opportunities to reduce friction, strengthen analysis, and improve delivery and operational efficiency through responsible automation and AI.
  • Drive Higher Performance Through Our People: Create clarity and accountability across business, product, technology, and operations partners by aligning priorities, removing obstacles, and preparing teams for successful change and adoption.
  • Execute on the Fundamentals: Strengthen delivery discipline through clear requirements, rigorous testing and UAT, regulatory and compliance consideration, release readiness, risk management, and post-launch stabilization.

  • Working knowledge of bioinformatics tools and statistical methods for omics data processing, analysis, visualization, and biological interpretation.
  • Foundational knowledge of human genetics and genomics, including genetic variation, genome builds and annotation, linkage disequilibrium, population structure and genetic ancestry, and common genomic data formats (e.g., VCF, PLINK, FASTQ/BAM).

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • To qualify, candidates must be legally authorized to work int he United States and should not require, now or in the future, sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B visa status, etc.)

Preferred qualifications

jobs.description:
Hyperproof is looking for a Senior Product Designer who has already changed how they work because of AI, and can show us the results.

About us

Hyperproof is a modern, AI-powered GRC platform that helps IT, security, and compliance teams manage controls at scale, connect them to risk, and build trust with their customers. Our customers work in regulated environments where accuracy, auditability, and trust are not optional.

How we work

Design at Hyperproof starts with customers and ends in production code. You'll meet with customers to understand the problem. Design and prototype with Claude in our codebase. Test and iterate with real users. Write UX specs and partner with engineering to ship.

You own problem framing and UX decisions for your work. Your PM partner owns the why, priority, and business outcomes. Engineering owns architecture and scale.

What you'll do

  • Discovery and research: Lead interviews, usability tests, and analytics reviews to frame problems before solving them. Use AI agents to transcribe and tag interviews, cluster themes across customer calls, support tickets, and product feedback, and pull usage data from analytics in hours instead of days. Then check every finding against the raw quotes and numbers before it shapes a decision.
  • Prototype in code: Use Claude Code to build several working versions of a flow in a branch of our live codebase, with real components and data, then put the strongest in front of customers in days, not weeks.
  • Ship to production: Use Claude Code to make small UI and UX pull requests, such as polish, fixes, and component updates. Review the AI's changes yourself before engineering review, and meet the same quality bar as any other code.
  • Code first, specs second: Your primary output is working code: prototypes in our codebase that engineering builds from directly. Specs and design files are secondary, used where the code needs support, such as states, edge cases, and accessibility.
  • Design system: Contribute documented, reusable components and tokens, in Figma and in code. Use AI to audit screens for off-system patterns, generate component variants and usage docs, and flag drift between Figma and production.
  • AI features: Design AI experiences compliance teams can trust, with clear provenance, human review, traceable reasoning, and graceful handling of uncertain or wrong output. Prototype with real model responses, not placeholder text, so the design reflects how the AI actually behaves.
  • Accessibility: Meet WCAG 2.1 AA before anything ships. Use AI to run checks on contrast, keyboard paths, and screen reader labels, then verify the results by hand.
  • Raise the bar: Turn the workflows that work for you into reusable prompts, Claude skills, and agents, and help other designers and PMs adopt them. Run design reviews and explain complex decisions to any audience.
  • Ownership: Define success before launch and measure outcomes after. Use AI to query our product analytics and report what changed, without waiting on an analyst.

What you bring

  • Proof that AI changed how you work. You can point to specific workflows you rebuilt, what you stopped doing as a result, and what improved, such as cycle time, the number of concepts you tested, or the quality of the outcome.
  • Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools. Claude Code is our standard. Deep experience with Cursor or a similar tool also counts.
  • Front-end literacy. Enough HTML, CSS, React, and Git to direct AI coding tools, read a diff, and recognize when the output is wrong.
  • Sound judgment with AI. You treat its output as a draft, know when not to use it, and hold AI-assisted work to the same standard you would if it took a week to make.
  • Strong research skills, both qualitative and quantitative, and a tireless advocate for the customer with strong facilitation skills. You've used AI tools and agents in real research work, such as synthesizing interviews, analyzing survey and usage data, or running unmoderated tests, and can show how you checked the results.
  • Design systems experience, including design tokens.
  • A passion for simplifying complex problems in enterprise software.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of product design experience, including 3+ years in B2B SaaS.
  • Hands-on experience building prototypes in a real codebase with Claude Code, Cursor, or a similar tool.
  • A portfolio that includes interactive or shipped work and shows your reasoning, not only final screens.

Nice to have: experience in GRC, security, or another regulated domain; experience designing AI or agent-based experiences.

What you can expect from us

  • Direct collaboration with the Design Director for guidance and support.
  • Competitive base salary and equity compensation.
  • Unlimited PTO for a healthy work-life balance.
  • A 401(k) plan with immediate vesting and a 4% company match.
  • A $1,000 home office stipend and your choice of PC or Mac.
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents.
  • 12-week parental leave and free diapers for a year.
  • Fully remote work.

Candidate experience

  • We value your time and want you to know what to expect from us.
  • Expect a 30-minute chat with a recruiter, a 45-minute discussion with our hiring manager, a 1-hour portfolio review, a 1-hour working session using Claude to solve a product problem, and a 45-minute 1:1 with a member of our product team.
  • You will have space to ask any important questions as our team gets to know you and thinks about the right fit for you within our team.

WHAT WE OFFER:

  • This role reports to the Design Director who values weekly team collaboration, 1:1 communication, on-demand coaching and will give you the support and autonomy to create your own success.
  • Base salary and equity compensation.
  • Unlimited PTO: strongly encourage to unplug and recharge.

  • $500 home office stipend
  • Choose your tech - PC or Mac laptop.

  • Annual company in-person events.
  • Health & Wellness: coverage for medical, dental, and vision - employee and dependents.
  • 12-week parental leave for all new parents and free diapers for a year.

LOCATION:

  • We are a fully remote company! Rather than restrict ourselves to only finding talent in one city, we’d rather find the absolute best people regardless of where they live.

COMPENSATION

$130,000 to $153,000 USDWhy you'll love Hyperproof

  • Own problems and shape what ships.
  • Work on a team where designers build in code and AI is part of how we work every day.

  • Help compliance professionals do the right things so the wrong things don't happen.

Learn more about our culture and how it all started.

WHERE YOU’LL GO

Learn more about the @hyperproof culture and how it all started.

EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. THIS POSITION REQUIRES U.S. CITIZENSHIP.

Role Description

This is a forward-deployed engineering role. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with mission heroes- the users, operators, and program engineers who run real workloads in real DoD environments- and lead the software integration of modular Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-UAS) sensors and effectors. You will deploy, harden, integrate, and operate our modular C-UAS solution.

Forward-deployed means aligned with the mission hero, not always on a plane. Most of the work is remote. You'll travel to sites when the engagement genuinely calls for it — initial standup, in-SCIF integration work, on-the-ground incident response, training, and knowledge transfer- and you'll be on a video call or in a shared chat with that same mission hero the rest of the time. The job is being their engineer, not living at their desk.

You are a cross-functional engineering leader. You can take responsibility for the full breadth of a data and software integration platform- make it work where it has to work, analyze what's running through it, and solve problems in real time for the mission hero. About 20% of your time, you'll also help make Defense Unicorns' forward-deployed team better — pairing with junior Data Engineer FDEs on hard problems, helping them develop technical judgment, and raising the ceiling on what the team can take on.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy and harden UDS Data Capability in the mission hero's environment — stand up UDS Store (Iceberg, Rook/Ceph, pgvector, Postgres), wire up UDS Transit for air-gap data movement, configure UDS Govern policies (Pepr/Lula), and integrate UDS Connect (Strimzi/Kafka) where streaming or legacy connectors are required.

  • Own integration with existing mission systems — connect UDS Data Capability to existing infrastructure, including sensor arrays, computer-vision-enabled UAS interceptors, and a broad range of C-UAS solutions.

  • Build pipelines that move data through classification boundaries — ingestion, transformation, catalog registration, model/dataset packaging via Zarf, cross-domain transit, and eventual consistency across DDIL conditions.

  • Operate what you deploy — own initial day-2 operations, including capacity, performance, backup/restore (Velero), observability (Vector/Loki), incident response, and upgrade paths. Transition ownership to the mission hero's operations team once stable.

  • Generate accreditation artifacts — STIG evidence, cATO documentation, FIPS validation notes, and policy mappings to support ISSM/ISSO requirements in IL4/IL5 environments.

  • Represent the mission hero to product and engineering — document issues, write postmortems, recommend operator improvements, and communicate field challenges to the platform engineering team.

  • Train and transfer knowledge — develop runbooks, architecture documentation, working sessions, and knowledge-transfer materials that enable mission teams to operate independently.

  • Mentor junior Data Engineer FDEs — pair on complex problems, review integration designs, and help engineers develop technical judgment without direct people-management responsibilities.

Clearance & Travel

  • Clearance: Active TS/SCI required.

  • Travel: Approximately 10%–25%, based on mission and customer requirements.

  • On-site expectations: Ability to work in SCIFs and other restricted environments for days or weeks when required for integration, incident response, training, or knowledge transfer. Most work is performed remotely.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience working in tactical edge and interoperable mission environments, including TAK Server administration, ATAK/WinTAK, tactical communications, and disconnected or air-gapped systems.
  • Production experience with modern data platforms, including lakehouse technologies (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Hudi), object storage (Ceph or S3-compatible), PostgreSQL, and analytical query engines such as Trino, DuckDB, ClickHouse, or Spark SQL.
  • Experience with streaming and data integration technologies, including Kafka or equivalent messaging platforms, stream processing, change data capture (CDC), and integration of legacy systems into modern data pipelines.
  • Hands-on experience building, scheduling, monitoring, troubleshooting, and recovering production data pipelines using Airflow, Dagster, Argo Workflows, or comparable orchestration tools.
  • Working knowledge of data governance, cataloging, access control, and auditability, including REST catalogs, ABAC/RBAC, OIDC/OAuth, and data lineage.
  • Strong SQL proficiency and experience designing data models and schemas for analytical and operational workloads.
  • Hands-on production Kubernetes experience, including deployments, operators, CRDs, storage classes, networking, and troubleshooting.
  • Strong Linux, containerization, networking, TLS, and secrets-management fundamentals.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar) and GitOps deployment practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex software and data integrations across multiple systems in secure, disconnected, or mission-constrained environments.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work directly with mission operators, program engineers, and technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently, adapt to changing mission requirements, and deliver practical solutions in environments where established documentation or processes may not exist.
  • Experience mentoring engineers through technical problem-solving, design reviews, and knowledge sharing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience administering TAK Server and supporting ATAK/WinTAK integrations in operational environments.
  • Experience with Link 16/TADL-J network operations and message-level analysis.
  • Familiarity with NIPR/SIPR environments, SATCOM, multi-band radios, and tactical communications interoperability.
  • Direct experience integrating C-UAS sensors, effectors, computer-vision-enabled interceptors, or other autonomous and unmanned systems.
  • Experience with Strimzi-managed Kafka on Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, or similar streaming and CDC technologies.
  • Experience with PostgreSQL extensions such as pgvector and open-source catalog technologies including Iceberg REST, Polaris, Gravitino, or Nessie.
  • Familiarity with the CNCF ecosystem and open-source infrastructure technologies.
  • Experience deploying or supporting software in DoD IL4/IL5 environments, including STIG compliance, cATO processes, FIPS requirements, and accreditation documentation.
  • Experience with air-gapped software delivery, Zarf packaging, cross-domain data movement, or DDIL operating conditions.
  • Experience supporting operational DoD users through field integration, incident response, training, and knowledge transfer.

The listed responsibilities are not exhaustive, and additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the evolving needs of the organization. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is able to adapt and take on new responsibilities as they arise.

Full compensation packages are based on candidate experience. Compensation ranges are established using national benchmarking data and apply across all geographic locations within the United States.

Who We Are

Defense Unicorns delivers mission value by streamlining software delivery so our customers can focus on the most important challenges. We share a vision of freedom and security for the advancement of progress and innovation. Our commitment to this vision, and to our mission-driven customers, means a commitment to speed, user experience and optionality, without compromising security. We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!

As a Senior Security Analyst on our Compliance team, you will play a key role in strengthening OpenSesame’s security posture in a fast-moving, high-growth environment. We’re looking for someone who brings deep technical security expertise, a proactive mindset, and the ability to turn complex risks into practical, scalable solutions.

This role spans vulnerability management, penetration testing, bug bounty operations, cloud and application security, and audit readiness. You’ll partner across Engineering, DevOps, IT, and Compliance to improve security processes, support compliance efforts, and help ensure security is built into how we work, especially as we continue evolving our approach to AI security. Establish Security Ownership & Technical Depth (0–6 Months)

Operationalize Continuous & AI-Aware Security (6–12 Months)

  • Own and mature the bug bounty program — improving signal quality, triage processes, researcher engagement, and remediation workflows.
  • Lead implementation of AI security practices across internal systems and product development:
    • Apply OWASP Top 10 for LLMs / AI systems to identify and mitigate emerging risks

jobs.description:
We’re looking for a Staff AI Builder to lead the design and delivery of AI/ML systems. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer who thrives on architectural decisions, can confidently own systems end-to-end, and contributes to technical leadership across the team.

In this role, you will work as a key technical leader on a cross-functional team, defining AI architecture, leading model development and optimization, and solving challenging integration problems. You’ll be joining real, in-flight work where reliability, security, and scalability are critical. You’ll establish engineering standards, raise the bar on how we build AI systems, and contribute to the technical decisions that shape how our AI work scales over time.

Why This Role Matters

At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.

Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

What You'll Do

Agentic & GenAI Engineering

  • Design and build agentic workflows — reasoning loops, tool/function calling, and orchestration across single- and multi-agent architectures — with clear judgment on which pattern fits the problem and which doesn't
  • Build and maintain RAG pipelines: chunking strategy, embeddings, vector search (OpenSearch), re-ranking, and staleness/refresh handling for dynamic knowledge sources
  • Integrate with AWS Bedrock and Agent Core, including MCP-based tool design — writing tool descriptions precise enough that an orchestrator routes correctly every time
  • Write and iterate on production system prompts — structured role framing, output constraints, and few-shot design — not just prompt tinkering
  • Build eval and observability into every agent you ship: golden datasets, RAGAS-style metrics, LLM-as-judge (as both a runtime guardrail and an offline eval), and tracing via LangFuse/LangSmith or equivalent
  • Design for LLM failure, not just LLM success: retries with backoff and jitter, circuit breakers, fallback models, and a clear user-facing story when something upstream degrades

Full-Stack & Platform Engineering

  • Build backend services in Python and Node.js, including serverless architectures (AWS Lambda, API Gateway) that support agentic workflows
  • Design DynamoDB single-table schemas — composite keys, transactional writes — for conversation state, agent memory, and session history
  • Support event-driven orchestration (Step Functions, SQS, EventBridge) for asynchronous agent operations, with an eye toward reliability and clean error handling
  • Contribute to frontend integration points so agentic features land cleanly for end users, and write clean, well-tested code across the stack
  • Support deployment, monitoring, and production troubleshooting in cloud-native environments (AWS, Docker), with guidance from senior engineers where needed

Collaboration & Technical Leadership

  • Bring informed technical judgment to architecture discussions — naming the real trade-offs of a pattern (e.g., gateway centralization vs. latency, single- vs multi-agent design) rather than defaulting to what's familiar
  • Partner with product, design, and delivery leads across global teams to scope and ship features end-to-end
  • Mentor other engineers on the pod and help raise the bar on agentic engineering practices, including AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code
  • Own assigned features and releases end-to-end — including the unglamorous parts: debugging, hardening, and keeping production systems trustworthy

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including meaningful time shipping GenAI/LLM-powered systems in production — not just prototypes
  • Real, hands-on depth in agentic AI: reasoning loops, tool/function calling, multi-agent orchestration, and a considered point of view on when single-agent design beats multi-agent, and why
  • Practical RAG expertise: chunking strategies, embeddings, vector databases (OpenSearch or similar), cosine similarity search, and re-ranking — you can explain the mechanism, not just the terminology
  • Experience building evaluation and observability for LLM systems: golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, RAGAS or comparable metrics, and tracing tools like LangFuse/LangSmith
  • Strong prompt engineering skills — you can write a production system prompt with real structure and constraints on request, not just describe the concept
  • Hands-on experience with the AWS GenAI stack: Bedrock, Agent Core, Lambda, DynamoDB (single-table design), S3, SQS, EventBridge, Step Functions
  • Strong Python and Node.js skills, with experience building full-stack applications and RESTful APIs
  • Solid understanding of production reliability patterns for LLM-backed systems: retries/backoff, circuit breakers, fallback models — as a bundle, not a single tactic
  • Experience with containerization (Docker) and cloud-native deployment
  • Comfort owning ambiguous, integration-heavy problems, and the ability to go a level deeper when someone pushes on your answer instead of staying abstract

Helpful Extras and Unique Skills

  • Direct experience with Amazon Bedrock Agent Core — agent registration, MCP tool wiring, memory/session management, gateway provisioning
  • Experience in a regulated or high-stakes domain (education, healthcare, financial services) where evaluation rigor and reliability carry real consequences
  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Step Functions, Sequencer, or similar state-machine-based systems
  • A point of view on LLM observability tooling, gained from actually running it in production rather than reading about it
